If the answer involves crossing the city twice, the arrangement will not survive the term.

faqs.question: What happens at the society gate when a tutor arrives?
faqs.answer: Share the tutor's full name and mobile number with your building's security desk before the first visit and the rest is routine. Most buildings in Bhayandar and Mira Road log a visitor once and then wave through a regular weekly caller, but the first evening is the one that goes wrong when nobody told the watchman. If your building insists a resident confirms each entry, tell the tutor at the start so they ring you from the gate rather than standing outside for ten minutes. Buildings with a visitor app are easier still: register the tutor as a recurring visitor and it stops being a weekly negotiation.

faqs.question: Does online IB tuition really work, or is it a compromise?
faqs.answer: It works well for motivated students from about Year 10 upwards and badly below that. An IB online tutor in Bhayandar gives you access to HL subject specialists who would never travel this far north, and for a DP student who can sit still and work, the screen costs you very little. For a PYP or early MYP child who needs somebody to notice they have quietly stopped thinking, it is the wrong tool for the job. The honest test is whether your child can work alone for ten minutes unsupervised. If not, start with home tuition and move online later, once the habit is there.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows criteria instead of marks. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: MYP work is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each describing a different skill for that subject group rather than a share of the content. A student can know the science well and still score low on the criterion the task was testing, usually because they answered a slightly different question from the one the task sheet set. A tutor who knows MYP spends the first sessions teaching your child to read the task sheet and the command term before writing. Ask your school's coordinator for the current criteria descriptors for that subject, because the IB revises them on its own cycle.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, with no argument about whose fault it was. Three or four sessions is enough to know whether your child will talk to this person, and a quiet child who has stopped asking questions is a mismatch rather than a bad student. We ask what specifically is not working, because sometimes the real answer is the time slot rather than the tutor, and then we shortlist again from the same verified pool. There is no lock-in and no cancellation penalty. We would far rather change a tutor in week four than read a complaint in month four.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in Bhayandar attend for IB?

faqs.question: When in the year should I book an IB home tutor in Bhayandar?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do. An IB home tutor in Bhayandar booked in August has the pre-mock weeks free; the same enquiry made in January finds a much thinner shortlist, because every reliable tutor on the Mira-Bhayandar corridor is already committed by then. If you are planning the hybrid pattern most families here use, line up the online specialist at the start of the academic year and reserve the local in-person tutor for the pre-examination weeks at the same time. Holding a slot early costs nothing, and you can always reduce the frequency later in the year.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home during the lesson?
faqs.answer: For children below about Year 9, yes, or another adult should be. It is not about supervising the tutor; it is that younger students drift the moment nobody is accountable, and a parent in the next room changes that completely. From Year 10 upwards it matters much less, and many DP students work better without a parent listening in. Either way, give the lesson a room with a door and a table rather than the dining area with the television on. Fifteen minutes with the tutor at the end of a session once a fortnight is worth more than sitting through every one.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor on the discovery call?
faqs.answer: Ask four things. Which board and which year group did you teach most recently, and for how long. What would you look at in the first session to work out where the marks are going. What will you show me after four weeks. And where do you travel from for an evening lesson in Bhayandar. A tutor who answers those four clearly has taught recently; one who answers with a philosophy of education has not. Be wary of anybody who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a pass rate, because the assessment does not work in a way that would allow it.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram a coaching institute or a school?
faqs.answer: Neither. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service: we verify tutors, shortlist two or three for your specific request, arrange the free discovery call, and review progress with you every few weeks. We do not run classes of our own, we are not affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and we are not affiliated with any school named on this page. faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one subject?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and above MYP it is usually a mistake. Through PYP and the early MYP years one good generalist can genuinely carry several subject groups, which is why a single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families ask about is a reasonable request at that stage. In DP it stops being reasonable: HL Chemistry and HL Mathematics are different jobs, and a tutor claiming both at Higher Level is usually strong at one of them. Two specialists at one session a week each beats one generalist at two, once internal assessments begin to land.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which part of the IB is your child actually in?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate is three different jobs wearing one name, and the right tutor for one is often the wrong tutor for another. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is inquiry-led and almost unmarked in the way parents expect marks to work, so support there is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) introduces criterion marking, which is where most confusion in this district starts. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two years where subject depth, internal assessment and examination technique all land at once.

A PYP parent who hires a DP subject specialist usually gets a frustrated child and a tutor teaching above the brief. A DP parent who hires a generalist gets friendly sessions and no movement on Paper technique. So the programme, not just the subject, is part of the request. For MYP families the useful question is which criteria the comments keep pointing at, because a child losing marks on criterion A knowledge is a different problem from one losing marks on criterion D reflection, and they need different work.

The transition years deserve their own mention. MYP Year 5 into DP1 is the step where workload, independence and the weight of written assessment all change at the same time. Families in Bandra East and Santacruz East often ask for help in the first DP1 term for exactly this reason. A tutor who has taught both sides of that step can tell you whether what you are seeing is a genuine subject gap or a child still writing at MYP length for a DP task.

Parents who ask for all IB and IGCSE subjects tuition in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) almost always turn out to need depth in one or two, plus a sensible second opinion on the combination before the school's selection deadline closes.

Every DP subject carries its own internal assessment, and these are where quiet marks leak away. Sciences carry a scientific investigation. Mathematics carries an exploration. Languages carry oral components. History and Economics carry written work with their own command terms. None of these are graded the way a school test is graded, which is why a student who tests well can still come out of an IA with a mark that surprises the whole family. A tutor who has supervised that specific IA reads a draft completely differently from one who has not.

Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay sit outside the six subjects and land in the middle of DP1 and DP2. Neither is content you can revise. Both are writing and argument, which means a student who is strong in Physics can still be stuck on an EE research question for six weeks. When we take a brief in this part of Mumbai we ask explicitly whether the help needed is subject content, internal assessment, or core writing, because those are three different tutors more often than they are one.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix along the Western Express Highway
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default request and usually the right one, especially for MYP students and for any child whose problem is attention rather than content. A tutor at the table can see the page, see the working, and see the moment a student stops following. Nothing on a screen replaces that for a thirteen-year-old. IB home tuition in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) also removes the evening travel that eats a school night, which matters more in this district than people expect given how traffic behaves around the office blocks at close of business.

Online earns its place in two specific situations. The first is subject scarcity: if your child needs a niche HL subject and the nearest specialist is in South Mumbai or outside the city entirely, an IB online tutor in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) is better than a nearby generalist who is learning the syllabus alongside your child. The second is DP2 crunch, when a thirty-minute question clinic two days before a deadline is worth more than a scheduled ninety-minute session next week. Online is also the honest answer during the monsoon weeks when evening road time doubles.

Hybrid is what most families here end up with by the second month, and it is worth planning deliberately rather than drifting into it. One weekly session at home for teaching and diagnosis, plus short online check-ins pinned to draft deadlines. The honest trade-off: online demands a working camera angle on paper, a quiet corner that is genuinely quiet, and a student who will keep writing while being watched. Younger students rarely clear that bar. DP students mostly do, and they often prefer it.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a grade change, and any tutor who promises one is selling. What you should see is a diagnosis you can repeat back: which topics are genuinely missing, which are present but unusable under time pressure, and which marks are being lost to method rather than knowledge. You should also see written work coming back annotated. If after a month you still cannot name the specific weakness in one sentence, the tutoring is not working regardless of how pleasant the sessions have been.

At one term the measurable changes are usually in the mechanics. Written work handed in on time rather than at midnight. An IA draft that follows the criteria instead of the student's instinct. Paper questions attempted in the order that protects marks. Grades often move a term after the habits do, which is the part families find hardest to sit with. We do not guarantee grades, and no platform honestly can: the tutor controls the teaching, not the examiner, not the cohort, and not the week your child falls ill.

Across a full examination cycle the realistic picture is a student who walks into the May session knowing what each paper asks of them. That is what good all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) are actually for. The honest limits are worth stating plainly. A tutor cannot fix two years of missed foundations in six weeks. A tutor cannot make a student do the independent reading. And home classes for one hour a week will not outrun a subject choice that was wrong from the start, which is why the subject conversation belongs in DP1, not DP2.

A home tutor sees hesitation, crossing out and the point where a student stops following; a screen hides all three unless the camera is pointed at the paper and the student is willing to keep writing while observed. sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Three different programmes sit under the International Baccalaureate (IB) label, and they need three different kinds of tutor. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs to roughly age eleven and is inquiry-led with no external examinations, so a PYP tutor is working on reading stamina, number fluency and the habit of explaining thinking out loud. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years across eight subject groups and marks everything against criteria A to D rather than a percentage. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year pre-university stage with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, Internal Assessment (IA) coursework, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). Asking for an IB home tutor in Borivali East without saying which of the three applies is the single commonest reason a first match misses.

The distinction matters most at the joins. A student moving from MYP Year 5 into DP1 has usually never been marked on a numerical scale against a subject grade boundary, and the first set of DP internal exams lands hard for that reason alone. Parents read a 4 in a subject their child used to be strong in and assume collapse, when what has actually happened is a change of measuring instrument. A good tutor explains that in week one, then works on the gap that is real. We see the same pattern at the PYP to MYP join, where a child who was praised for creative inquiry suddenly needs to produce evidence against stated criteria.

Borivali East sits inside a stretch of Mumbai where the IB intake is genuinely mixed. Some families here are at a school that runs the full PYP to DP pathway, others moved in from a national board at Year 8 or Year 9, and a few are managing a mid-year transfer from another city or another country. The brief we build with you records that history, because a child who joined the Middle Years Programme two terms ago needs command-word and criteria work that a child who has been in the system since PYP 3 does not. IB home tuition in Borivali East is far more effective when the tutor is told the truth about that starting point.

If you are uncertain which programme label applies, the quickest check is what the school report is written in. Criteria A to D and a 1 to 8 scale is MYP. Subject grades 1 to 7 with HL and SL markers is DP. Descriptive comments against learner-profile attributes with no scale is PYP. Send us a photograph of that report page on the discovery call and we can tell you what kind of IB tutor Mumbai parents in your position usually need.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the coursework underneath them
paragraphs: In the IB Diploma Programme a student picks six subjects across the groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and almost every one of those six carries an Internal Assessment that is marked at school and moderated externally. That coursework is where tutoring earns its place, because it is the part of the grade a student can still influence in the week they are sitting with somebody. A sciences investigation, a mathematics exploration, a language oral, a history essay and a business research project are five completely different pieces of writing with five different command vocabularies, and a tutor who knows one of them well is not automatically useful on another.

The HL and SL decision is the one families get wrong most often, and it is rarely about ability. A student who enjoys Physics but will read Economics at university does not need Physics at Higher Level, and taking it there costs them hours they needed for the Extended Essay. The reverse mistake is just as common: a student who wants engineering takes Mathematics at Standard Level because DP1 looked hard, then finds the university entry requirement names Higher Level. We ask for the intended direction on the first call, not because tutoring can change a requirement, but because the honest answer to some requests is to talk to the school coordinator about a level change before paying anybody for lessons.

Command words are the other hidden subject. The difference between state, outline, explain, analyse, evaluate and justify is worth real marks in every IB subject, and students who write fluently in English still lose those marks because they answer a different question from the one asked. A tutor working at your dining table in Borivali East can mark a single past-paper answer line by line against the command word and show exactly where the response stopped describing and failed to evaluate. That is a fifteen-minute piece of teaching that no amount of silent revision produces. IB Gram covers all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Borivali East might be asked for, and we match by specific subject and level rather than by a general label.

Because subject guides are revised by the International Baccalaureate on its own cycle, we do not quote paper structures, weightings or mark totals on this page. Component names change, and a figure that was right two years ago can be wrong for the session your child actually sits. Your school's IB coordinator and the current subject guide are the authority on that, and any tutor you take on should be reading the same version your child is being examined against. Ask them which guide they are working from; a specialist will answer immediately.

paragraphs: Children in Borivali East attend a mix of schools, and two shape most of the IB requests we get here: JBCN International School, Borivali, which runs IB and IGCSE pathways, and Singapore International School a little further north. The pressure points in a Mumbai IB year are reasonably predictable. The school year opens in June, and the first internal assessments of any weight land from late August into September, which is when a DP1 parent discovers that the summer was not used. The long festival stretch through October and early November eats two or three weeks of teaching and lands immediately before the DP1 winter examinations, so students who were coasting arrive at those papers underprepared. December and January are the IA quarter: first drafts, second drafts, and in DP2 the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay competing for the same fortnight. February and March belong to mock examinations, and the May session follows immediately after. A tutor started in February is working inside that compression; a tutor started in July is not.

This is the practical reason we tell families here to start a term earlier than feels necessary. A home tutor engaged in late June has eight unhurried weeks to diagnose, repair the gaps from last year and establish a working rhythm before any deadline matters. The same tutor engaged in January is triaging. Neither of us can change the calendar, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades in any case, but the difference between those two starting points is larger than the difference between a good tutor and an excellent one.

School schedules also decide what a weekly slot can look like. Buses from the Borivali East schools get home in the late afternoon, co-curriculars run two or three evenings a week in most years, and a child who has been in a classroom since 8am is not learning anything new at 8.30pm. The workable windows here are usually a weekday slot between 5.30pm and 7.30pm on the two evenings that are genuinely clear, plus a longer Saturday morning session when a coursework deadline is close. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for an IB student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the right default for most IB students in Borivali East, and it is what the majority of families on this corridor of Mumbai actually book. A tutor in the room can see the page the student is avoiding, take the pen, and watch a working method rather than a finished answer. For anybody below DP1, and for any student who has not yet learned to work alone, that physical presence is doing most of the work. An IB home tutor in Borivali East also sees the study space, which is frequently the real problem: a desk facing a television, a younger sibling in the same room, a phone charging within arm's reach.

Online is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who cannot yet sit down without supervision, and it is the right choice for a DP2 student who knows what they are stuck on. The honest split runs along self-management rather than age. A DP2 student with a shared screen, a tablet and a stylus can get a Paper 3 walkthrough from a specialist anywhere in the country at 9pm after the household has quietened, and that is better than no specialist at all. Travel is the fourth, and this is where Borivali East has a genuine structural advantage over much of Mumbai. Because tutors from Dahisar and Mira Road reach this locality faster than tutors from Andheri, matching north rather than south removes the travel premium that a long crossing adds. The fifth factor is session length and frequency: a ninety-minute session usually costs less per hour than a sixty-minute one, because the travel is amortised, and a twice-weekly arrangement is usually priced below two separate singles.

There are two things worth paying more for and one worth paying less. Pay more for a specialist in the exact component your child is losing marks on, because four sessions with the right person beats a term with a generalist. Pay more for somebody who will mark written work between sessions, since that is where the improvement actually happens in essay subjects. Pay less, or not at all, for additional hours added because the first ones did not work. Group arrangements come up often here, usually two children from neighbouring buildings in the same subject and year. They work when the two students are genuinely at a similar level and the parents accept that the pace follows the slower one. They do not work for coursework support, where the whole point is that your child's investigation is their own. sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you should be able to see process changes, not grade changes, and a tutor who promises otherwise is managing you rather than teaching your child. Specifically: the student can say what they are weak at in topic language instead of saying the subject is hard; written work comes back with fewer structural errors even if the content is still thin; homework is started without a negotiation. In a science or mathematics subject you should see a worked solution laid out properly for the first time. These are small, checkable, and they are the honest leading indicators that one term from now the grade will move.

At one term, expect the grade to have moved if the diagnosis was right and the work got done. That usually looks like one band in an internal assessment, or a coursework draft that comes back with teacher comments about refinement rather than about the whole approach being wrong. It can also look like a grade that has not moved while the student has stopped going backwards, which in a DP1 year where content difficulty rises every month is a real result that report cards hide. Ask the tutor to show you a piece of the student's work from week one next to one from week twelve. That comparison is more informative than any number.

At one examination cycle, the question is whether the student can perform under timed conditions on unseen questions, and that is a different skill from understanding the material. Many students in Borivali East who have understood everything still lose marks because they have never done a full paper against the clock without their notes. The last four to six weeks of any arrangement should look different from the rest: whole papers, timed, marked strictly, and then a cold review of where the marks went. If your tutor is still teaching new content in that window, something earlier went wrong.

Here are the honest limits. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and nobody can. A tutor cannot fix a subject chosen at the wrong level, cannot replace two years of missed foundations in six weeks, and cannot make a student who will not work do work. We also will not tell you tutoring is the answer when it is not: some students need a level change, some need a conversation with the school about a learning difficulty, and some need their phone out of their bedroom more than they need an IB home tutor in Borivali East. Parents searching for the best IB tutor in Borivali East are usually looking for certainty, and the closest thing to it is an accurate diagnosis in week one plus honest reporting after that.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which IB stage is your child actually in?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs as three separate programmes, and the help a child needs differs completely between them. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is inquiry-led with no external papers, so tuition here is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) marks against published criteria rather than a percentage, which is why a Year 8 report can show a four in Criterion C and a seven in Criterion A for the same subject. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year examined stage, with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, internal assessments and external papers that land in a tight window.

Getting this wrong is the most common reason a first tutor fails. A parent at JBCN International School, Borivali whose child is in MYP Year 4 often books a tutor who teaches DP content well and has never read an MYP criterion descriptor. The child then gets harder questions and the same marks, because nobody has told her that Criterion D asks her to apply the mathematics to an unfamiliar real situation and show the limitations of her model. An IB home tutor in Borivali West who works at the right stage will start from the descriptor and the task sheet, not from a textbook chapter.

The transition years are where families in the Western Suburbs ask for help most. MYP Year 5 into DP1 is a jump in independence rather than content: the same student who was handed structured tasks is now expected to choose a research question for an Extended Essay (EE) and defend it. Year 11 into DP1 at a school that offers both pathways adds a second decision, because subject combinations taken at IGCSE shape what is realistic at HL. We keep that conversation separate from the tuition itself so you are not being sold hours while you are still choosing subjects.

If you are unsure which stage applies, the school's programme coordinator is the right first call, and the current IB subject guide is the only reliable source for how a course is structured in the year your child actually sits it. Those documents are revised on the organisation's own cycle. We will not quote a weighting or a paper length at you, because the figure that was correct two cohorts ago may not be correct for yours.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessments each one carries
paragraphs: Most families arrive with a subject problem and leave with a level decision. In the Diploma Programme a student takes six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), and the HL choices are what the next two years will actually feel like. HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is a different animal from SL Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, and a child who was strong through MYP can still find the HL course relentless because the pace assumes algebraic fluency she never had to prove before. A tutor who has taught both routes will tell you within two sessions which one the work in front of her supports.

Every DP subject carries an internal assessment, and that is where the term-time pressure comes from. The sciences carry a scientific investigation the student designs; Mathematics carries a written exploration; the languages carry oral components; History and Economics carry written tasks with their own command words. These are marked against published criteria and moderated, so the quality of the first draft matters more than the number of hours spent on it. A good tutor's first job on an internal assessment is to make the student state the research question in one sentence and defend why it is answerable with the data she can actually collect in Mumbai.

Command words are the quiet mark-killer. A student who writes a beautiful paragraph for a question that said "evaluate" and then never weighs one position against another has lost marks she had the knowledge to earn. The same goes for "to what extent", "justify" and "compare and contrast", each of which expects a specific shape of answer. We ask tutors to mark one piece of the student's own written work against the published criteria in the first fortnight, so the parent can see the gap between what the child knows and what the paper is asking her to show.

On subject breadth, be realistic about who you are hiring. All IB and IGCSE subjects any tutor in Borivali West claims to teach should make you ask which ones they have actually taught to the final assessment. One person teaching Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Economics and English at Higher Level is a scheduling convenience rather than a subject specialist. Two specialists on alternate evenings usually beats one generalist across five, and an honest tutor will say which of your subjects is not theirs.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for IB in Borivali West
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it is the right default for most children. An IB home tutor in Borivali West sees the desk, the lighting, the sibling walking through, the phone face-up next to the notebook, and the folder where three weeks of handouts have gone unopened. None of that is visible on a video call, and for a Year 9 or Year 10 student who cannot yet run their own study time, it is most of the diagnosis. The physical presence also enforces a start time in a way that a link in a chat window does not.

An IB online tutor in Borivali West makes sense in two specific situations, and it is worth being blunt about both. The first is subject scarcity: if your child needs Higher Level Physics, Economics at HL or a second language with few teachers in north Mumbai, the right specialist may simply not live within reach of the Borivali end of the corridor, and an online match with exact subject experience beats a local generalist every time. The second is the DP2 examination run-in, when a confident eighteen-year-old wants three short sessions a week rather than two long ones and travel time becomes the limiting factor.

Online is the wrong choice for a Year 8 or Year 9 student who cannot yet work alone for forty minutes without being watched. We say this to families every week and some of them book online anyway because it is cheaper and easier to schedule; a term later they are asking why nothing changed. If you are choosing online for logistics rather than for subject fit, make sure a parent is in the room for the first month, and insist on a shared document the tutor annotates live so the work survives the call.

Hybrid is the pattern that holds up best through a Mumbai school year. One home session a week for diagnosis, written work and the awkward conversations, plus one shorter online session for drills, past-paper corrections or a quick pre-test check. It survives traffic on the Western Express Highway, it survives a tutor's own exam-season crunch, and it keeps the cost of travel out of the arrangement on one of the two sessions. Families who start with home classes and add the online half in DP1 tend to stay with the same tutor longest.

sections.heading: How are IB tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every profile we shortlist has been checked on four things before it reaches you: identity, qualification in the subject, teaching experience at the level requested, and a reference we have actually spoken to. An IB private tutor Borivali West families hire through us has also told us which subjects and levels they will not take, which is more informative than the list they will. We do not publish ratings, we do not count years in business at you, and we do not describe a tutor as the best IB tutor in Borivali West, because that is not a claim anyone can check.

What we cannot do is assess chemistry between a tutor and your child, and that is why the discovery call exists. Use it. Ask which board and programme they have most recently taught to final assessment, and in which year. Ask what they would do in the first session with your child's actual report in front of them. Ask how they would know in four weeks whether this was working. A tutor who answers those three clearly is usually a good tutor; one who answers with credentials and enthusiasm may still be, but you have learned nothing.

There are checks only you can run, and they take ten minutes. Sit within earshot of the first session, not in the room, and listen for the ratio: is the student talking and working, or being lectured at? Look at the notebook afterwards and see whether anything in the child's own handwriting changed. Ask your child one question that evening: did she have to think, or did she watch someone else think? Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, promises a specific points jump, or asks for a long package before a single lesson has happened.

Replacement is part of the arrangement rather than a complaint process. If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, tell us what specifically did not work: the pace, the level, the explanation style, the punctuality. We re-shortlist from the same local pool across Borivali West, Kandivali West and Dahisar, and we would rather change the tutor in week three than have you quietly stop after week nine. There is no lock-in period and nothing to argue your way out of.

sections.heading: What does an IB internal assessment actually ask of your child?
paragraphs: An internal assessment is a piece of work the student designs, produces and submits from school, marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated externally. That single sentence explains most of what parents in Borivali West find confusing about the Diploma Programme: the marks that decide a final grade are not all earned in May, and the ones earned during the two years are earned on a timetable the family has to manage alongside everything else. A tutor who only does exam practice is helping with half the course.

Take the science investigation. A DP1 student has to choose a question, justify a method, collect or source data, process it with sensible treatment of uncertainty, and then evaluate the limitations honestly. The commonest failure we see is not weak science; it is a question too broad to answer with the equipment and time a Mumbai school day allows, chosen in a hurry the week it was set. One session spent narrowing the question, before any data exists, saves a month. The same logic applies to the Mathematics exploration, where students pick a topic they find interesting and then discover there is no mathematics in it at their level.

The written components carry a different risk. A History internal task, an Economics commentary or a Language A essay is marked on structure and the handling of the command word as much as on content. Students who write well in English often score below their ability because they present information instead of arguing a position, or because they never explicitly answer the question in the final paragraph. Marking one of their own pieces against the actual criteria, line by line, is uncomfortable and it is the fastest improvement available in the whole course.

What this means practically for IB home tuition in Borivali West is that the calendar drives the plan. From August to October the useful work is planning and drafting. From November to January it is redrafting, mock papers and timing under pressure. From February the work narrows to past papers and the specific topics the student still loses marks on. A tutor who runs the same session shape in September and in February has not read the course, and you should say so.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking for a grade change, and any service that promises one is selling you something. What you should see is diagnostic clarity: the tutor can name the two or three specific things costing your child marks, in the language of the course rather than in generalities, and there is written evidence in the child's own hand that one of them has moved. If after four weeks nobody can tell you what the problem actually is, the problem is the tutor. That is the right moment to change, and it costs you a month rather than a year.

At one term the measure is independence. A student who needed the tutor to start every question should now be starting some of them alone, attempting the harder parts before the session rather than during it, and bringing her own list of what she did not understand. Marks usually follow that change rather than lead it, and they often move on internal assessment drafts and class tests before they move on a report card. Ask the tutor at the ten-week mark to show you one piece of work from week two beside one from week ten.

Across a full examination cycle the honest statement is that good tuition improves the probability of a better outcome and guarantees nothing. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not publish a success rate, because neither we nor any tutor controls how much a student works between sessions, what else happens in a family's year, or how a paper falls on the day. What a well-matched tutor reliably changes is the number of marks the student leaves on the table for reasons that have nothing to do with knowing the subject.

There are also cases where the right answer is not to hire anyone. A child who is managing fine academically but sleeping badly, or who is in the wrong subject combination, or who has three tuitions already and no unstructured evening, does not need a fourth adult explaining things. We have told families in Borivali West to drop a tuition rather than add one, and to raise the subject-change conversation with their school coordinator instead. Nobody pays us for that advice, which is rather the point.

sections.heading: Starting IB home classes in Borivali West, Mumbai
paragraphs: Have four things ready and the first week saves itself. The most recent report card, one piece of the child's own marked written work, the school's assessment calendar for the term, and an honest list of which evenings are actually free once school transport, sport and the existing tuitions are counted. Parents who send a list of three possible evenings and then discover two of them are gone lose a fortnight to rescheduling, and a tutor who has shifted a slot twice before starting rarely stays past the first month.

A good first session is mostly the tutor listening and the student working. Expect your child to be asked to attempt something slightly too hard while the tutor watches how she approaches it, where she stops and what she does when stuck. Expect a short conversation with you at the end, naming what the tutor saw and what the next three sessions will target. Do not expect a syllabus plan for the year; anyone offering one before they have seen your child write has written it in advance for everybody.

Fees are a fair question to ask on the call, and we will not quote a figure on this page because it would be invented. IB tuition fees in Borivali West depend on the board and programme, the level, how scarce the subject is in north Mumbai, how far the tutor travels and whether the session is sixty or ninety minutes. A Higher Level science specialist travelling up from Andheri on a weekday evening will cost more than an MYP Mathematics tutor living in Kandivali West. Ask what the rate covers, whether it changes for exam-season intensives, and what the notice period for cancelling a session is.

Then start small. One subject, one or two sessions a week, a written review at the end of the first month, and a decision point at four weeks that you have agreed in advance. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai schools teach does not exist as one person, so begin with the subject that is actually costing marks and add the second only if the first is working. That sequencing is the difference between a term of progress and a term of busy evenings.

Give evenings that are genuinely free after transport and sport

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Borivali West actually cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one before hearing the subject is guessing. The price depends on five things: the programme and level, how scarce that subject is in the northern Western Suburbs, the tutor's own travel distance, the session length, and whether you are booking one subject or two. Higher Level sciences and Economics cost more here than MYP Mathematics, simply because fewer people in reach of Borivali teach them to final assessment. Ask on the discovery call what the rate covers, whether exam-season intensives are priced differently, and what notice you need to give to cancel a session.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Borivali West for an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the slot time matters more than the distance. A tutor living in Borivali East, Kandivali West or Dahisar will take a 6.30pm or 7pm start without difficulty because they are travelling a few kilometres along Link Road or the Western Express Highway. A tutor coming from Bandra or Khar for the same slot is agreeing to something that will not survive a full term. Ask any prospective tutor where they live and leave from, not just whether they can come. The honest answer sometimes points you to a slightly less decorated profile who lives fifteen minutes away.

faqs.question: How does society gate access work for a weekly home tuition slot?
faqs.answer: Most buildings in Borivali West will issue a standing visitor entry for a tutor once you register them at the gate, which takes one message to your society office and removes the ten minutes lost to a fresh entry every week. Give the tutor's name, the day and the time window, and tell them which gate to use, because several buildings on the Link Road side have a separate visitor entrance. If your society requires a photo identity record, ask the tutor in advance rather than at the gate on the first evening. It is a small administrative job that prevents a recurring weekly delay.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 4. Can a DP tutor teach her?
faqs.answer: Often badly. The Middle Years Programme marks against criteria A to D with task-specific descriptors, and a tutor whose experience is entirely in the Diploma Programme will teach content well while missing what the criterion is actually asking for. A Year 4 student losing marks in Criterion D is being told she cannot yet transfer a method into an unfamiliar situation; more worked examples will not fix that. Ask directly whether the tutor has marked MYP work against descriptors and in which subject group. If the answer is vague, ask for a different profile. Stage match matters more than seniority at this age.

faqs.question: Does an IB online tutor in Borivali West work as well as home sessions?
faqs.answer: For a motivated DP2 student with a scarce subject, yes, and sometimes better. For a Year 8 or Year 9 student who cannot yet work alone for forty minutes, no. The deciding factor is whether the child's problem is content or self-management. Online solves content scarcity brilliantly, which matters in north Mumbai where Higher Level specialists are thinner on the ground than in Juhu or Bandra. It solves nothing about a phone face-up beside the notebook. If you choose online for scheduling reasons, keep a parent nearby for the first month and insist on a shared document the tutor marks live.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us what specifically did not work and we re-shortlist, usually within the same week. Useful detail sounds like: too fast, pitched at the wrong level, explained without checking understanding, or arrived late twice. Vague detail slows it down. We draw replacements from the same local pool across Borivali West, Borivali East, Kandivali West and Dahisar, so the travel logic that made the original match viable still holds. There is no lock-in, no notice period to argue over and no fee for changing. Changing a tutor in week three costs a fortnight; staying with a poor fit until the mock exams costs a term.

faqs.question: Which months are the worst for finding a weekday slot in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: November to January, by a wide margin. That is when internal assessment drafts, Theory of Knowledge (TOK) deadlines, mock papers and MYP interim reports converge, so every experienced tutor in the Western Suburbs is full and the ones with free weekday evenings are usually free for a reason. August and September are the sensible months to start: the same tutors have open slots, and you get a full term of diagnosis before the pressure arrives. If you are reading this in December, expect to take a weekend slot or a hybrid pattern rather than the Tuesday evening you wanted.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Rarely well. A profile claiming Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Economics and English at Higher Level is offering scheduling convenience rather than subject depth, and the weakest of those five is usually the subject you hired them for. Two specialists on alternate evenings beats one generalist across five. The exception is the lower MYP and PYP years, where a strong all-round teacher genuinely can cover several subject groups because the demand is reading, number sense and study habits rather than syllabus depth. Ask which subjects the tutor has taught to final assessment, and in which year, before you decide.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to JBCN International School, Borivali?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service, not a coaching chain and not affiliated with JBCN International School, Borivali, Singapore International School or any other school named here. We also have no affiliation with the International Baccalaureate organisation, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We name local schools because their calendars and programme pathways are the context a family in the northern suburbs is working inside. Any tutor we shortlist works independently of your child's school, and anything about internal deadlines or predicted grades should be confirmed with the school's own coordinator.

faqs.question: What should I prepare before the first session at home?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them take long. The most recent report card, one piece of your child's own marked written work, the school's assessment calendar for the term, and a clear desk with a chair for the tutor and no television in earshot. The marked work is the most useful of the four and the one parents forget: a tutor who can see where the marks were lost in your child's handwriting will diagnose faster than one working from a verbal description. Tell the tutor which subject matters most if there is more than one.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an IB student usually need?
faqs.answer: One or two per subject for most students, and two is the right starting point only when there is a specific deadline. More is usually a sign that something else is wrong: the wrong level, a missing foundation from the previous year, or so much scheduled tuition that there is no time left to practise alone. Practice between sessions is where the marks come from, so an evening with no tutor in it is part of the plan rather than a gap in it. Start with one subject and one or two sessions, review at four weeks, and add only if the first is clearly working.

faqs.question: Do you cover Dahisar and Kandivali West as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most tutors treat Borivali West, Borivali East, Kandivali West and Dahisar as one working area because they share the Western Line and the same two roads. A tutor living in Dahisar is often an excellent match for an early-evening slot in Borivali West, since they travel against the commuter direction. Across the whole stretch, home tuition in Mumbai works best when the tutor's own journey is short and predictable, which is why we shortlist along the line rather than pulling impressive profiles northward from Bandra or Juhu for a weekday start.

sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Which IB programme your child sits in decides nearly everything about the tutoring. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three school-age programmes in Mumbai: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through middle school, and the two-year Diploma Programme (DP) at the top. A tutor who is genuinely strong in one of them is not automatically useful in another.

PYP work is inquiry-led and reported against learning outcomes rather than marks, so what parents in Breach Candy actually ask for at this stage is quieter than it sounds: a child who reads fluently, who holds a number fact without counting on fingers, and who can write a paragraph that stays on topic for six sentences. Home tuition here works best short, frequent and light. Three half-hour sittings across a week beat one long Sunday session, and part of the tutor's job is stopping the household from turning nightly homework into a standing argument.

MYP is where the vocabulary changes and parents lose their footing. Subjects are assessed against published criteria, each one testing a different kind of thinking, so a child can write a page of perfectly correct content and still score low because the task asked for evaluation and they produced description. A report full of criterion letters and single digits gives a parent no way of knowing whether a four is a crisis or a normal mid-year position. The first useful thing an MYP tutor does is translate that report into plain English, then teach to the criterion that is genuinely weak rather than the subject as a whole.

DP is the two years everything before it was rehearsal for. Six subjects spread across the groups, three of them usually at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the creativity, activity, service strand. The internal assessments (IAs) are what catches families out, because they are drafted during term while ordinary classes carry on regardless. An IB tutor Mumbai parents keep for a full DP cycle spends as much time on draft structure, command terms and criterion language as on content.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL: what an IB tutor in Mumbai needs to know
paragraphs: Subject choice generates more tutoring requests in South Mumbai than any other single decision, and it is usually made in a fortnight on incomplete information. A DP student picks six subjects across the groups, decides which three sit at Higher Level, and commits to an internal assessment in every one of them. Those choices are awkward to reverse once the first term's coursework has started, so a conversation with someone who has taught the subject matters more than a conversation with someone who has read the option sheet.

The spread is wide. Group 1 covers studies in language and literature; Group 2 language acquisition; Group 3 individuals and societies, where History, Economics, Psychology and Business Management sit; Group 4 the sciences; Group 5 mathematics, where the choice between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation changes the whole character of the two years; and Group 6 the arts, or a second subject from an earlier group. The register covers all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai families search for, from early PYP numeracy through to DP2 Higher Level sciences.

Every one of those subjects carries an internal assessment, and they do not arrive politely spaced. A DP2 student may be drafting a scientific investigation, a mathematical exploration and a historical investigation inside the same two months, each marked against its own criteria, each needing a supervisor's sign-off at a date her coordinator sets rather than one the IB publishes. This is the work a tutor is most useful on, because it is the work a school teacher has least time to sit beside one student and unpick.

We will not reproduce component weightings, paper lengths or mark totals on this page. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, and a figure that was accurate when a brief was written can be wrong for the session your child actually sits, so check the current guide or your school's Diploma Programme coordinator for structure. A single all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Breach Candy is rarely the right answer for a DP2 student carrying two sciences; it is often exactly right for a Year 7 child who needs one person to hold the whole week together. The Core and Extended tier decision belongs to the IGCSE page for this locality.

What those schools give you, from a tutoring point of view, is a calendar. The Mumbai academic year opens in June, which is the single best month to start tutoring and the month families most often skip because nothing has gone wrong yet. The first real reporting round lands a couple of months in, and that is when our enquiries from South Mumbai spike. By then the strong subject specialists have filled their weekday evenings, and a parent who starts looking in October is choosing from what is left rather than from who is best for the child.

The pressure points then stack. For a DP2 student the internal assessment drafts and the Extended Essay milestones tend to crowd the second half of the calendar year, with mock examinations after the winter break and the May examination session closing everything out. For MYP students the personal project in the final year collides with ordinary coursework. For PYP families the pressure is softer but real: a reading or number gap identified in the first reporting round is cheap to fix in July and expensive to fix in February.

Practically, that means booking against the calendar rather than against panic. A family who begins IB home tuition in Breach Candy in June gets the pick of the tutors and a diagnostic session before any coursework is at stake. A family who begins in November gets a tutor doing triage on a draft that is already due. Both are worth doing. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for IB in Breach Candy?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and for good reasons. A tutor sitting at your table sees the things a screen hides: the child who copies a method correctly and cannot say why it works, the exercise book with three weeks of unmarked work in it, the phone face-down beside the calculator. An IB home tutor in Breach Candy also gets the practical benefit of a short commute, which means a 5:30 slot genuinely starts at 5:30 rather than at 5:50 with apologies. For PYP and MYP children, where attention is the scarce resource rather than content, being in the room is worth more than any software.

Online tutoring earns its place in two specific situations and is oversold everywhere else. The first is scarcity: if your DP2 child needs HL Economics or a less commonly taught Group 2 language, the pool of tutors who can teach it well inside the island may be two people deep, and an online specialist from elsewhere in Mumbai or outside it is better than the nearest available compromise. The second is the monsoon, when a tutor who would otherwise sit out a flooded evening can still teach. Booking an IB online tutor in Breach Candy for those reasons works. Booking one because it is cheaper, for a Year 6 child who struggles to stay seated, usually does not.

Hybrid is what most of our longer-running placements settle into without anyone planning it. The weekly teaching session happens at home, and a shorter screen session gets added in the fortnight before a deadline, when a student needs twenty minutes on an introduction rather than a full hour on new content. That shorter session also travels: it survives a family trip, an exam-season schedule change, and the week the tutor is unwell. A parent booking all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Breach Candy families use for a Year 8 child should expect this pattern to emerge by the second term.

The honest trade-off is attention versus reach. In the room you get a tutor who notices everything and a radius of about two kilometres. On a screen you get the whole city and a tutor who only knows what the child chooses to show. Neither is better in the abstract. For a DP2 internal assessment draft, reach usually wins. For a child who has quietly stopped trying, the room wins, and no amount of screen time substitutes for it.

sections.heading: How are IB tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Before a profile reaches you, we check identity against a government photo document, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and the teaching history: which boards, which year groups, which subjects, and over what period. We ask when they last taught the current subject guide for their subject, because a teacher who last ran DP Chemistry several revisions ago is a different proposition from one teaching it this year. We take references from people who have actually seen them teach, not from a list of family friends. Where a tutor claims school experience, we ask which school and which years, and we expect the answer to be specific.

There are things no platform can verify, and pretending otherwise is how families get burned. We cannot verify that your child will like the tutor, that the tutor will still be in Mumbai in March, or that a strong DP teacher will be patient with a distracted Year 7. Those only show up in the room, which is why the first session is a diagnostic you are allowed to walk away from and why an IB home tutor in Breach Candy is confirmed for the term only after it.

Your own checks matter as much as ours. Ask what the tutor does in the first thirty minutes of session one, and look for an answer about diagnosis rather than a syllabus plan. Ask which command terms they drill and how they teach the difference between describing and evaluating. Ask what they do when a student plateaus for a month, because every student does. Ask for an account of an internal assessment they supervised from draft to submission, with the student's details left out. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or a promised band, and prefer the one who tells you what will take longer than you hoped.

If something feels off after two or three sessions, tell us early rather than waiting for the term to end. A replacement is a conversation, not a complaint process: you say what did not work, we use that to narrow the next shortlist, and the new tutor starts from a written handover of what has already been covered. Families who tell us in week two get a better second match than families who tell us in week ten, because by week ten the problem has usually stopped being about teaching.

sections.heading: What do IB tuition fees in Breach Candy actually depend on?
paragraphs: IB tuition fees in Breach Candy depend on five things, and no honest page can quote you a number without knowing them. Those five are the programme and year group, the level the subject is taught at, how scarce that particular subject specialist is, how far the tutor travels and at what hour, and how long each session runs. Two families on the same road can pay very different rates for what looks like the same service, and the difference is almost always one of those five rather than anything about the tutor's confidence.

Level and scarcity do most of the work. A PYP numeracy tutor and a DP2 HL Physics tutor are not in the same market, because the second one is one of a small number of people in South Mumbai who can mark a draft investigation against the criteria and say what is missing. Scarcity also moves within a year: HL science and HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches slots in the island are effectively gone by the time first reports land, so the same tutor who had an opening in June is negotiating from a different position in October.

Travel is the factor parents underestimate and the one Breach Candy is best placed on. Because this pocket is a ten-minute drive from Babulnath and Peddar Road, an IB private tutor Breach Candy families book is often filling a slot that sits next to another one, which makes the travel cost per family lower than it would be for an isolated address in the Eastern Suburbs. A tutor crossing the island in the evening peak is pricing forty minutes of lost time into your hour; a tutor walking over from Kemps Corner is not. This is also why the 7:30 slot can be easier to staff than the 6:00.

Session length and frequency are where families have real control. Two shorter sessions a week usually produce more than one long one for anyone below DP, and for a DP student with an internal assessment due, a fortnight of short, frequent contact around a draft beats a monthly marathon. Ask what a package covers in writing: marking of drafts between sessions, availability by message in the week before a deadline, and what happens to a session missed because your child's school ran a late activity. We do not publish a price list, because a published figure would be wrong for most of the people reading it, and we do not guarantee grades at any price.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look at whether your child can tell you what the task was asking for. A student who comes out of a session able to say that the question wanted evaluation and she had been writing description has made the single most valuable shift available in the first month. Other honest four-week signals: homework started without a standoff, a notebook that is organised enough to revise from, and a tutor who can describe the specific gap in one sentence rather than saying the child needs to work harder.

At one term, expect a visible change in one measurable thing and a stubborn one somewhere else. Perhaps the mathematics internal assessment draft now has a clear aim and a method that matches it, while the end-of-topic test scores have barely moved because the topics tested were the ones covered before tutoring began. That pattern is normal and is not a failure. What should have changed by now is the tutor's description of the problem: it should be narrower and more specific than it was in week one, because they have more evidence.

At one exam cycle, you can judge properly. A full year gives you mock results, internal assessment submissions and a teacher's comments to compare against where the child started. Some students move a long way. Some move a little and hold it. A few do not move, and the reason is usually not the subject: it is sleep, a timetable with no slack, a school subject chosen for the wrong reasons, or something going on that tutoring is not the right tool for. A tutor who notices that and says it is more useful than one who books more hours.

Two honest limits. First, there are situations where you should not hire a tutor at all: when the child is already in six activities and has no free evening, when the real problem is a subject choice that needs changing rather than supporting, or when the issue is attendance or wellbeing rather than content. Second, booking one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need at once is tempting at DP level and usually wrong; one tutor who is excellent at one subject beats one who is adequate at four. We do not guarantee grades, we do not publish success rates, and we will tell you when the answer is fewer hours rather than more.

sections.heading: Getting started: what to prepare before session one in Breach Candy
paragraphs: Three documents make the first session twice as useful, and all three are already in your house. The most recent school report, with the criterion grades or subject marks intact rather than summarised. One recent piece of marked work, ideally one the child did badly on, because a wrong answer tells a tutor more than a right one. And the subject list, with Higher Level and Standard Level marked for a DP student, or the subject groups for an MYP student. Have those on the table and a tutor can diagnose in one session what otherwise takes three.

Session one is not teaching. A good tutor spends the first part asking the child to work through something while they watch, because the point is to find where the method breaks rather than to cover a topic. Expect questions that feel too easy. A DP2 student stuck on a Higher Level science topic is often stuck on an algebraic rearrangement from three years earlier, and no amount of work on the current topic fixes it. At the end you should get a plain summary: this is the gap, this is the order I would work in, this is what the first month looks like.

On logistics, say the awkward things up front. Whether a parent will be at home, where the tutor will sit, whether your building wants a visitor pass arranged in advance, and what time the child actually gets back from school activities rather than what the timetable says. Families who start IB home tuition in Breach Candy at 5:30 on paper and 6:05 in practice lose half an hour a week to a problem that one honest conversation in June would have solved.

After that, the rhythm is simple. The tutor teaches weekly, flags the drafts and tests coming up, and tells you when a slot needs moving around a school event. You tell us if the fit is wrong, and you tell us early. IB Gram stays independent of your child's school throughout, we are not affiliated with Bombay International School or Activity High School, and we do not guarantee grades. What we do is keep a verified subject specialist arriving at your door on the same evening every week for as long as it is working.

Bring one recent piece of marked work the child got wrong

faqs.question: How quickly can an IB home tutor start coming to our flat in Breach Candy?
faqs.answer: In most cases within a week, and often sooner in June and July. The constraint is almost never finding a tutor in South Mumbai; it is matching your preferred evening to one they still have free. A request for a PYP or MYP generalist on a 5pm weekday slot is usually filled in two or three days. A request for a Higher Level science specialist at 6pm in October may take two weeks, because those slots fill first. Tell us your second-best time as well as your first and the wait usually halves.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel from Worli to Breach Candy for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, but we would rather not build your term on it. Worli to this part of the island is eight kilometres and can still cost forty minutes in the evening peak because of the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. A tutor doing that twice a week in June will do it reliably; the same tutor in November, after one late arrival and one cancelled session, often asks to move you. Matching within Breach Candy, Cumballa Hill, Napean Sea Road and Kemps Corner holds for a full academic year far more often.

faqs.question: Our building asks for a gate pass for every visitor. How does that arrangement work?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a recurring weekly visitor rather than clearing them at the gate each week. Most buildings here will accept a standing entry for a named person on a fixed day and time if a resident requests it in writing, and that single step removes the most common cause of a session starting fifteen minutes late. Give the tutor the exact wing and flat number, not just the building name, and tell them which entrance the lift lobby is on. If your building requires photo identification each visit, say so before the first session so the tutor arrives carrying it.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be in the house for the first one. You want to hear the tutor's closing summary yourself rather than through your child, and you want to see how the two of them interact when a question lands badly. After that, most families leave them to it and come back for the last five minutes. For younger PYP children, being within earshot helps for the first few weeks. For a DP student, a parent hovering in the room usually makes the session worse, not better.

faqs.question: What makes one IB tutor more expensive than another in South Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Level and scarcity, mostly, then travel. A tutor who can mark a Higher Level science draft against the criteria and tell a student exactly which criterion is costing them is in a much smaller pool than a tutor supporting Middle Years Programme coursework, and that pool shrinks further once first reports land. Travel adds to it when a tutor crosses the island in peak hours. Session length and whether draft marking between sessions is included change the figure as much as anything about the tutor. Ask what is included in writing before you commit to a term.

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring genuinely as good as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For a motivated Diploma Programme student working on a draft, close to it. For a younger child, no. A screen shows the tutor what your child chooses to show, which means an unmarked exercise book, a copied method or a phone under the desk stays invisible. Online wins in two cases worth taking seriously: a scarce subject where the best available teacher is not within reach of Bhulabhai Desai Road, and a monsoon evening that would otherwise be cancelled. Most of our long-running placements here end up home-led with occasional screen sessions around deadlines.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor one question: what is the specific gap, in one sentence? A tutor who answers with a narrow, concrete diagnosis after four weeks is working, even if marks have not moved, because the topics being tested are usually ones covered before tutoring started. A tutor who answers that your child needs to work harder has not diagnosed anything in a month, and that is a replacement. Tell us either way. We would rather rematch you in week five than have you quietly stop in week twelve.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Higher Level Physics and Standard Level Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and at Standard Level more often than you would expect, but we would not recommend it for a Higher Level subject in Diploma Programme year two. The person who can mark a Higher Level Physics investigation against the criteria and the person who can unpick a mathematical exploration are rarely the same teacher at the depth DP2 needs. Below DP, one tutor across two or three subjects is often ideal, because the limiting factor for a Middle Years Programme student is study habits rather than subject depth.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP5 and starts DP next year. Who should we book now?
faqs.answer: Book for the transition, not for the current year. The jump that unsettles families is from criterion-marked Middle Years Programme coursework to Diploma Programme internal assessments and examination-style papers, and the useful tutor is one who has taught both sides of it. Use the months before DP1 to close the specific gaps that will hurt later: algebraic fluency before Higher Level sciences, essay structure before a Group 3 subject, and the habit of reading a command term before answering. Starting this work in MYP5 is considerably cheaper in effort than starting it in DP1.

faqs.question: What should we ask an IB tutor on the first phone call?
faqs.answer: Four questions. What will you do in the first thirty minutes of session one? Which year groups and boards have you taught in the last two years? Tell me about an internal assessment you supervised from draft to submission. And what do you do when a student stops improving for a month? Listen for specifics and for a willingness to say what will be hard. A tutor who promises a particular grade on a first call is telling you something useful about themselves, and the answer is no.

faqs.question: Do you place tutors with students at Bombay International School and Activity High School?
faqs.answer: Families from both schools do use IB Gram, and tutors here are familiar with how those calendars run, but we have no affiliation with either school and no arrangement with their teachers. We name them because they set the assessment pressure points for children living around Bhulabhai Desai Road, Babulnath and Peddar Road. A tutor who knows that a cohort's drafts are due in a particular fortnight plans around it. That is local knowledge, not a relationship, and we will never claim otherwise.

faqs.question: Can evening slots hold through the Diploma Programme examination season?
faqs.answer: They hold better here than in most of Mumbai, for a geographical reason. Because this pocket is a ten-minute drive from Babulnath and Peddar Road, a tutor can teach two families back to back on the same evening, so your slot is part of a pair they want to protect rather than an isolated trip they may drop. During the examination season expect to shift times around school revision sessions and mock papers. Agree in advance how a session missed at short notice is handled, and the season passes without argument.

sections.heading: How a Byculla enquiry turns into two or three real names
paragraphs: The request that arrives from a Byculla flat is almost never "an IB tutor". It is more specific than that: a Year 10 student at Bombay International School who has stopped handing in Economics work, or a first year Diploma Programme student who picked Higher Level Biology in July and by October cannot see how the internal assessment is supposed to come together. The first conversation exists to get that specific, because the shortlist depends on it. We ask which school, which year, which subjects, what the last report said, and what the parent thinks is actually wrong, which is often different from what the report says.

After that call the search runs against two filters at once. The academic filter asks who has taught this subject at this level, under this board, recently enough to know how the current assessment reads. The geographic filter asks who can stand outside your gate at the hour you need, every week, for a whole term. Byculla is unusual in Mumbai because the second filter is kinder here than it looks: the Central Line stops at Byculla station and the Eastern Freeway on-ramp sits close by, so a tutor living in Chembur or Wadala can be at a Byculla address on a weekday evening in a way that the same tutor could never manage for Colaba or Cuffe Parade.

What you receive is short. Two or three names, each with the subjects they teach, the boards they have taught under, the area they travel from, and the evening slots they still have open. You speak to them. You pick one. If the first session does not work, you say so and we go back to the list rather than asking you to make the best of it. Nothing here is automated matching against a database field, because the thing that decides whether IB home tuition in Byculla survives past the first month is usually temperament rather than credentials. The pool these names come from is deliberately wide: all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai requests draw on it, from a Year 3 reading target to a finished internal assessment.

sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: There are three International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes and they ask for completely different help. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early school years and is inquiry-led, with no external examinations. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and introduces criterion-based marking. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year pre-university course with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and a set of internal assessments. A tutor who is excellent at one of these is not automatically useful at another, which is why we ask before we shortlist.

Most Byculla enquiries we see sit at the two ends. Younger children in the Primary Years Programme need someone who can sit with a reading log and a maths investigation without turning either into drill work, and who can explain to a parent why there is no test score to look at. Diploma Programme students need close to the opposite: a tutor who knows what the subject guide asks of an internal assessment, who can read a draft the way a teacher will read it, and who will push a student to finish a rough first version early instead of polishing an outline for three weeks.

The middle years sit between those two and are the easiest to misjudge, because the marking is criterion-based and a parent reading a criterion descriptor for the first time usually cannot tell whether their child is doing well or badly. We cover those years, but the detail of how each subject group is assessed belongs on our Middle Years Programme page rather than this one. What matters here is that the programme question comes first. An IB home tutor in Byculla who has only ever taught the Diploma Programme will struggle with a Year 4 reading target, and saying so on the first call saves a wasted month.
