sections.heading: Choosing HL and SL when the Mumbai tutor pool is this wide
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision that quietly sets the next two years, and Dadar families get to make it with better information than most, because the specialist supply reaching this address is deep. Across the board we cover all IB and IGCSE subjects one tutor in Dadar rarely holds alone: mathematics in both routes, the three sciences, English, economics, business management, psychology, history, geography, and the language acquisition and language A courses that are hardest to staff in person anywhere in Mumbai.

The practical question is not which subject is easiest but which Internal Assessment (IA) your child can actually finish. Every DP subject carries coursework, and the coursework is where marks are lost quietly over months rather than dramatically in May. A Biology IA needs a measurable independent variable and enough trials to say something. A History IA needs a question narrow enough to argue in the word count. A Mathematics exploration needs a genuine mathematical idea the student can own. An IB home tuition in Dadar plan that ignores the IA calendar and only drills past papers is half a plan.

Level choice follows the same logic. Higher Level (HL) is not Standard Level (SL) with extra topics bolted on; it changes the depth of the questions and the amount of independent reading assumed. A student holding three HLs they chose for a university application they have since abandoned is a common and fixable problem, and the honest conversation about dropping one to SL is usually better had in DP1 than in February of DP2. A tutor who has taught both levels can tell you what the child is realistically carrying.

For MYP students the equivalent decision is which of the eight subject groups is being treated as a soft option at home while the school marks it hard. Design and the arts carry the same four criteria as sciences, and the written reflections in those subjects are frequently where an otherwise strong report dips. We place a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families actually need rather than defaulting to maths and physics because those are the subjects parents think of first.

sections.heading: One tutor, three addresses: Matunga, Prabhadevi and Dadar Parsi Colony
paragraphs: Dadar sits almost exactly in the middle of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and that position is the whole argument of this page. A tutor who takes a Dadar slot can hold a working week that nobody could hold in a peripheral suburb: Dadar Parsi Colony on Monday, Matunga on Wednesday, Prabhadevi on Thursday, and a Dadar address on Saturday morning, all inside walking or short-auto distance of one another. That density is why the same tutor will quote a weekday evening here and refuse one across the creek.

Dadar Parsi Colony is the quietest of the three and the easiest to teach in, with low buildings around Five Gardens and far less street noise than the main road. Matunga, a short hop south on the Central line, mixes older housing stock with a heavy study culture and a lot of families who already run two or three coaching commitments, so the scheduling conversation there is usually about what to drop rather than what to add. Prabhadevi is closer to Worli and the sea face, with newer towers, tighter visitor protocols and a commute that is short in kilometres and long in minutes after six.

The travel reality in this part of Mumbai is worth stating plainly, because it is the opposite of what the map suggests. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a handful of kilometres and can still lose most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Tutors here are usually matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, and Dadar is the one address where that rule relaxes.

Practically, that means we plan a Dadar route rather than a single journey. If your child needs two subjects, the strongest arrangement is often two tutors on adjacent evenings who both already teach somewhere in this cluster, rather than one tutor stretched across both subjects. And if you live in Prabhadevi or Matunga and the shortlist for a scarce subject looks thin, meeting at a Dadar address, or running that one subject online, usually opens it up again.

sections.heading: Mumbai term dates: what Don Bosco International School and JBCN set in motion
paragraphs: Children in this pocket of Mumbai are spread across a handful of international schools rather than concentrated in one, and the two that come up most in Dadar enquiries are Don Bosco International School and JBCN International School, Parel. Both are a short and predictable journey from a Dadar address, which is part of why families settle here and stay. Naming them is local context only: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel or any other school mentioned on this page.

What matters for tutoring is the shape of the year rather than the name on the blazer. An IB school year in Mumbai starts after the monsoon break in June, and the first real pressure point lands in the second half of the first term, when MYP criteria tasks and DP1 internal assessments arrive in the same fortnight as the first proper unit tests. Families who start home tuition in October are usually reacting to that collision. Families who start in July are responding to a report they received in May, and they get far more out of the term.

The second pressure point is the stretch between the Diwali break and the mock examinations, which in most Mumbai IB schools sit in the first weeks of the calendar year. For DP2 students that window carries the Extended Essay (EE) final submission, Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay drafting and at least two subject IAs at once. For MYP Year 5 students it carries the personal project. A tutor who knows the rhythm will front-load content revision before Diwali and switch to examination technique after it.

The third is the quiet one: the gap between the end of school examinations and the start of the next academic year, when nothing is due and almost nobody books a tutor. It is the cheapest and most effective time to fix a two-year-old gap in algebra or a reading speed problem, because there is no deadline competing for the hour. Dadar families who use July and August this way spend less across the whole of DP than families who only ever hire in a crisis.

sections.heading: Is home tuition in Dadar better than online for an IB student?
paragraphs: For most Dadar families, in person wins, and the reason is attention rather than teaching quality. A tutor sitting at your dining table sees the pencil stop moving, notices the child reaching for the phone, and can turn a page around and make them redo a working line in front of them. That is why home tuition in Dadar is our lead service and why the majority of the weekly slots we arrange in this part of Mumbai are physical visits rather than screens.

Online is not a consolation prize, and there are three situations where it is genuinely the better call. The first is a scarce subject: if your child needs DP Economics Higher Level (HL) or a language A course and the in-person shortlist has one name on it, an IB online tutor in Dadar drawn from a national pool beats a local generalist. The second is a DP2 student with a compressed revision window who cannot afford to lose travel time in either direction. The third is monsoon weeks, when a 7pm slot in July is a coin toss on the road.

The honest trade-offs run both ways. Online demands a working desk, a stable connection, a document camera or at least a phone propped to show handwritten working, and a child disciplined enough not to open another tab. It is markedly weaker for early PYP and MYP years, where the tutor needs to watch a hand write rather than read a scan. In person demands that the tutor's travel is sustainable across a whole term, which in South Mumbai is a real constraint and not a formality.

Hybrid is what most families in Dadar settle into by the second term without planning it. One physical visit a week carries the relationship, the diagnosis and the hard conversations, and a shorter online session midweek handles homework review and question practice. It costs less than two visits, survives traffic and examination weeks, and keeps the contact frequent enough that nothing drifts for ten days. We will set it up that way from the start if you ask.
bullets: In person first: the tutor sees the pencil stop and intervenes immediately
Online wins for scarce subjects, compressed DP2 revision and monsoon weeks
Online needs a desk, a stable line and a way to show handwritten working
Screens work poorly for early PYP and lower MYP years

sections.heading: What we check about a Dadar tutor, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Before a tutor appears on a Dadar shortlist we verify identity against a government photo document, confirm the degree claimed, and take the subjects and levels they say they have taught alongside the schools or boards they taught them with. We ask directly about examining, moderating or coordinating work, because that is the single most useful signal for Diploma Programme (DP) coursework. We also confirm that they can realistically reach your address at the hour you want for a full term, which is the check most often skipped and most often the reason an arrangement collapses in week six.

What verification cannot tell you is whether this person will teach your child well. That is why we put an IB home tutor in Dadar in front of you for a conversation and one diagnostic session before any ongoing commitment, and why you should treat that session as an interview rather than a lesson. Four questions separate a specialist from a confident generalist, and they are listed below. A tutor who cannot answer them concretely is not necessarily bad, but they are not the person for a DP2 student in February.

Two warning signs are worth naming. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest tutor can promise one; the variables that decide a May result include the child's own work, the school's teaching and the examination itself. And be cautious of anyone who wants to replace the school's method entirely in week one. A tutor whose first instinct is to teach a different notation from the one the class uses creates two syllabuses in the child's head at the worst possible moment.

On the parent's side, the checks are simple. Ask for the tutor's own name and photograph before the first visit and inform your building desk, keep the sessions in a room you can walk past, and ask your child one open question after each of the first three sessions. Families looking for the best IB tutor in Dadar usually find the search ends not with a credential but with a tutor the child will admit confusion to, which only shows up after a few weeks of home classes.
bullets: Identity, degree, and the subjects and levels actually taught are verified
Examining or moderating experience is asked about directly, not assumed
Travel sustainability for a full term is checked before you are shown anyone
Ask: which criteria does this task hit, and what separates a 5 from a 7?

sections.heading: Why the Dadar interchange widens the Mumbai tutor pool
paragraphs: Dadar is where the Western and Central lines cross, which makes it the single easiest address in Mumbai for a tutor to reach from anywhere. It sounds like trivia. It is actually the most useful thing a Dadar parent can know, because tutor supply, not tutor quality, is what usually limits a hire. Tutors accept Dadar slots they would refuse elsewhere, and that one fact changes what you should be willing to hold out for.

Here is what it looks like in practice. A family in a far western suburb asking for DP Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level (HL) on a Wednesday at 6pm is choosing from the tutors who live within that suburb's own travel shadow, because nobody is crossing the city for a single ninety-minute lesson. The same request from Dadar draws on tutors living along the Western line from Churchgate to Borivali and along the Central line from Byculla to Thane, plus anyone who can get to Dadar on the Harbour line. For a scarce subject that difference is often the difference between one candidate and four.

So the advice is counterintuitive. In most of Mumbai we tell families to compromise on specialism to protect reliability, because a brilliant tutor who cannot sustain the commute will quit by October. In Dadar we tell them the opposite: hold out for the person who has actually taught that subject at that level, because the commute problem that forces the compromise elsewhere mostly does not apply here. If your first shortlist for an IB private tutor Dadar request is thin, ask us to widen the radius rather than lowering the bar.

The same logic applies to timing. The hardest slot to fill anywhere in Mumbai is a weekday 7pm to 8.30pm, because it sits inside the evening peak. In Dadar a tutor coming down the Western line is arriving at a station they would pass through anyway, so those slots are fillable here when they are not in Prabhadevi or Matunga. If you have been told a late weekday slot is impossible, it may simply have been quoted against the wrong address. That is the one advantage of this neighbourhood that no amount of money buys elsewhere, and most families never use it.

sections.heading: What should four weeks of home classes in Mumbai have changed?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see changes in behaviour, not in grades. The specific markers: your child can say what the current task is being marked against, they start homework without a negotiation, and they bring a question to the session instead of waiting to be given one. If none of that has shifted after four sessions, something is wrong with the match and you should say so rather than waiting for a test result to prove it.

At one term the markers move to work quality. Written answers start using the command terms the question asked for. A science student writes a method somebody else could repeat. A maths student shows the step they used to skip. Report comments shift from "needs to show more working" to something about depth or precision. Internal assessment drafts arrive with the supervisor on the date agreed rather than three weeks after it, which is often the single biggest change an IB home tuition in Dadar arrangement produces in a first term.

At one exam cycle you find out what the work was worth, and this is where honesty matters. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and we do not publish success rates, because a figure like that says nothing about whether this tutor will help your child. What a good term of tutoring reliably buys is a student who walks into the examination hall having already done the hard thinking, and a coursework portfolio submitted on time without a crisis. The number at the end is not ours to promise.

The limits are worth stating too. Tutoring does not fix a subject choice that was wrong from the start, though it can help you decide to change it. It does not compensate for a child sitting six subjects they have no interest in. It does not work at one session a week for a student who has stopped attending school lessons. And it does not work when the tutor and the class teacher are pulling in opposite directions, which is why we keep asking what the school actually said.
bullets: Four weeks: names the criteria, starts without nagging, brings own questions
One term: command terms used correctly, working shown, IA drafts on time
One exam cycle: the thinking already done before the hall, nothing promised

sections.heading: Starting an IB home tutor search in Dadar: the practical first steps
paragraphs: Three things make a first shortlist good. The first is the most recent school report, including the comments nobody reads, because the comments say what the grades cannot. The second is a photograph of the last assessed piece of work with the teacher's marks on it, which tells a tutor more in thirty seconds than a phone call does in twenty minutes. The third is two realistic weekly windows, not one ideal one, because the single hardest constraint in any Mumbai arrangement is the calendar rather than the money.

The first session is a diagnosis and you should expect it to look slightly disappointing. A good tutor spends most of it finding out what the child can do unassisted: a short piece of written work under something like test conditions, a few questions pitched above the current level to see where the method breaks, and a conversation about what the child thinks is going wrong. Parents sometimes read that as the tutor not teaching. It is the most valuable hour of the engagement.

By the end of session one you should have a plan in plain language: what we are fixing, in what order, and what will be visible by when. Ask for it. A tutor who cannot tell you the first three things they intend to change has not diagnosed anything. From session two the work is ordinary and repetitive, and that is the point; the all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Dadar families get value from are the boring, consistent ones, not the dramatic ones.

On fees, we will not quote you a figure on this page because it would be fiction. What an IB tuition fees in Dadar conversation actually depends on is the programme and level, how scarce that subject is in person, how far the tutor travels and how long the session runs. A DP Higher Level (HL) science with coursework supervision costs more per hour than MYP maths support; an online slot costs less than a visit. We tell you the range for your specific request before you speak to anyone.
bullets: Bring the latest report, including the written comments teachers add
Photograph the last marked assessment; it tells a tutor more than a call

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Dadar actually cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things, and anyone quoting a flat rate before hearing your request is guessing. The programme and level matter most: Diploma Programme (DP) Higher Level (HL) sciences with Internal Assessment (IA) supervision sit at the top of the range, Middle Years Programme (MYP) support in the middle, Primary Years Programme (PYP) work lower. Subject scarcity matters next, because a language A tutor who can reach Dadar in person is rarer than a maths tutor. Then travel distance, session length, and whether you want one or two sessions a week. We give you the realistic range for your exact request before you speak to any tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Dadar for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more easily here than almost anywhere in Mumbai. Dadar is where the Western and Central lines cross, so a 7pm slot is reachable for a tutor living anywhere along either line, which is why tutors accept Dadar evening slots they would decline in Colaba or Kasarvadavali. The practical limits are the ones everyone shares: the evening peak on the roads around Dadar TT and Hindmata is genuinely slow, so we build in a fifteen-minute arrival window rather than a hard start time, and we confirm that the tutor can sustain that journey every week for a full term before you commit.

faqs.question: What gate and building formalities should we sort out before the first session?
faqs.answer: Tell your building desk the tutor's name, the day and the standing time before the first visit, and ask whether your society wants a one-off visitor entry or a recurring pass. In Dadar Parsi Colony this is usually informal. In the newer Prabhadevi towers it often is not, and a tutor stuck at the gate for twelve minutes loses a sixth of the lesson. Give the tutor your flat number, the wing or building name and a working mobile number, and tell them which lift or entrance to use. The families whose home tuition runs smoothly in Mumbai are almost always the ones who did this once, properly, in week one.

faqs.question: Does my child need help at Higher Level or Standard Level first?
faqs.answer: Start with the subject where the gap is costing the most marks, which is not always the Higher Level (HL) one. A student losing six points across two Standard Level (SL) subjects is in more trouble than one losing three in an HL subject they enjoy. Look at the last two assessed pieces in each subject and at the teacher comments rather than the headline grades. If the pattern is the same complaint in several subjects, about working not shown or command terms ignored, that is one problem across subjects and one tutor can often address it, which is cheaper than hiring three.

faqs.question: Is an IB online tutor in Dadar as effective as one in the room?
faqs.answer: For a focused Diploma Programme (DP) student, close to it. For a Middle Years Programme (MYP) or Primary Years Programme (PYP) child, no. The difference is supervision: online, the tutor can see a face and a shared screen but cannot see the hand hesitate over a page, and a younger child will quietly disengage long before anyone notices. Where online genuinely wins in Dadar is subject scarcity and compressed revision windows, because it removes travel entirely and widens the pool to the whole country. Most families we work with end up running one in-person visit plus one shorter online session rather than choosing.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: Call it early, because a month is long enough to know. First, separate three things: has the child's behaviour changed, has their work changed, and has the grade changed. Grades move last and often not within a term. If behaviour has not shifted at all, the match is the problem and we will shortlist again. If behaviour has shifted but work has not, the diagnosis was probably wrong and the tutor should redo it rather than continue. If work has improved and only the grade has not, give it another assessment cycle before changing anything.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us, not the tutor, if that is easier. We ask for specifics rather than a verdict: what the child says afterwards, whether sessions start late, whether the work being set connects to what the school is doing. Sometimes the fix is a conversation about method and the arrangement recovers. When it does not, we shortlist replacements from the same pool and you are not charged for the matching again. Because Dadar draws tutors from both railway lines, a replacement here is usually available faster than in a peripheral suburb, which is a real practical advantage of this address.

faqs.question: Do you cover Matunga and Prabhadevi as well as Dadar itself?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga and Prabhadevi are all within a single tutor's working radius, and many of our tutors hold slots in two or three of them in the same week. Matunga is a short Central line hop and the easiest of the three to add. Prabhadevi takes longer than the distance suggests after six in the evening, because the roads towards Worli congest. If your shortlist for a scarce subject in Prabhadevi looks thin, moving the venue to a Dadar address or taking that one subject online usually widens it immediately.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle more than one IB subject?
faqs.answer: Within limits. A single tutor can credibly cover Mathematics and Physics, or Biology and Chemistry, at Middle Years Programme (MYP) level and often at Standard Level (SL). At Higher Level (HL), especially with Internal Assessment (IA) supervision, one subject per tutor is the honest arrangement, because HL depth and the current assessment criteria take real maintenance to hold. The exception is a skills problem rather than a content problem: if the issue is written structure, command terms or examination timing across several subjects, one strong tutor addressing that directly beats three subject specialists working separately.

faqs.question: Do you work with students from Don Bosco International School or JBCN International School, Parel?
faqs.answer: We work with students who attend them, which is a different thing. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel or any other school, and no tutor on our platform speaks for a school. What the tutor does is work with your child's own teaching: the notation the class uses, the deadlines the coordinator set, the feedback already written on the last assessment. If the school has issued specific guidance on a coursework task, that guidance wins over anything a tutor would otherwise prefer.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP student in Mumbai usually need?
faqs.answer: One well-used ninety-minute session per subject per week is the common starting point, and it is enough if the homework between sessions actually gets done. Two sessions a week makes sense in three cases: a Diploma Programme (DP) subject the student is genuinely behind in, a compressed window before mock examinations, or an Internal Assessment (IA) with a hard deadline. More than two per subject usually signals a different problem, often that the student is not following the class at all, and the useful conversation then is with the school rather than with a tutor.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not in the room, but somebody should be in the flat, particularly for the first few weeks and for younger students. The useful arrangement is a room with the door open that an adult walks past occasionally, rather than a closed study. For a Diploma Programme (DP) student working at a dining table, your presence elsewhere in the house is enough. We also ask you to be reachable by phone during the first three visits, because the questions that come up early are about scheduling and scope and are faster to settle live than over messages the next day.

sections.heading: How an IB home tutor in Dahisar is actually shortlisted
paragraphs: Shortlisting an IB home tutor in Dahisar is a geography problem before it is a talent problem. The deepest pool of experienced International Baccalaureate (IB) teachers in Mumbai sits around Bandra, Juhu, Andheri and Goregaon, because that is where the city's oldest IB schools are. Dahisar is the last station on the Western Line inside the municipal limits, so a match that looks sensible on a map can fall apart in week three, when the tutor works out that the 8pm return leg is an hour each way and starts asking to shift the slot.

The filter therefore runs north first. Before we read a profile's subject depth we read where that person already teaches: Borivali East, Borivali West, Kandivali, Mira Road. A tutor who already holds two standing slots within fifteen minutes of Dahisar station will keep a third one for a full term. A tutor coming up from Khar for a single lesson a week usually will not, whatever they say on the first call. Matching along the Western Line instead of across it is most of the work in the Western Suburbs.

The brief you send decides the quality of the shortlist far more than the size of any tutor database does. 'Middle Years Programme Year 4, integrated sciences, criterion B and criterion C marks sliding since October' produces a different set of names from 'needs help with science'. Give us the programme, the year group, the subject, the one weekday slot you can genuinely protect, and whether an adult will be in the flat. We then check who has taught that exact programme level, because a confident Diploma Programme (DP) Chemistry teacher is not automatically the right person for a Primary Years Programme (PYP) Year 3 reader who is still decoding word problems.

After that the process is slow at the front and quick at the back. You see two or three profiles, not twenty. You speak to the tutor before any money moves. sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Three programmes sit under the International Baccalaureate label and each one needs a different kind of tutor. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years and is inquiry-led, with no external papers. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and reports against criteria rather than percentages. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the examined two-year finish. A parent in Dahisar who books 'an IB tutor' without naming the programme very often gets the wrong one.

Dahisar East is the reason this matters more here than in most northern localities. Singapore International School is at Dahisar East, so a suburb at the city's northern edge carries genuine PYP and MYP demand instead of only Diploma Programme demand, which is the usual pattern once you go north of Malad. An IB PYP home tutor in Dahisar is a completely different hire from a DP subject specialist. The PYP tutor is building reading stamina, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud; nobody is revising for a paper, and a tutor who turns up with past papers has misread the job.

In the MYP, the thing that unsettles parents is the mark scheme. Criteria are reported as levels against descriptors, and a level in criterion C is not a percentage you can convert. Parents who grew up with aggregate marks read a criteria row as a bad score when it is actually a specific diagnosis: the investigation was planned well and the conclusion did not refer back to the data. A tutor who can read that row aloud and say which paragraph of the write-up caused it is worth more than one who simply re-teaches the topic.

In the Diploma Programme the structure itself is the pressure: Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, an Internal Assessment (IA) in every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) running alongside. Weightings, paper lengths and deadlines are revised by the IB on its own cycle, so ask your school's Diploma coordinator or read the current subject guide rather than trusting any figure you find on a tutoring site, including this one.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessment attached to each one
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision that most changes how much tutoring a family in Dahisar ends up needing, and it is usually made in a rush. Six subject groups, one Higher Level or Standard Level decision per subject, and an Internal Assessment sitting under every single one. A student who picks three Higher Level sciences because a relative said it looks strong on an application has quietly committed to three separate investigations with three separate write-ups in the same academic year.

Mathematics is where most of the regret shows up. The two routes, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, are not easier and harder versions of one course; they reward different habits. A student who is strong at pattern-spotting and weak at algebraic manipulation is often placed in the wrong one by ambition rather than by evidence. The same applies to languages: a child who speaks fluent Hindi at home and has never written a formal literary commentary in it is not automatically ready for a language A course in it.

What a good tutor does in the first fortnight is separate content gaps from assessment gaps. A Year 11 student can know chemical bonding perfectly and still lose marks because the answer never addressed the command word. Explain, describe, outline, evaluate and justify are not decoration; each one asks for a different structure. When parents ask what all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Dahisar covers looks like in practice, this is the honest answer: one person can cover the thinking skills across subjects, but only a subject specialist can mark a Higher Level write-up against the actual criteria.

The home classes in Mumbai that work best on the subject side are the ones with a visible artefact. Every session ends with something on paper that a parent can look at without understanding the content: a corrected question, a planned investigation, a paragraph rewritten with the command word underlined. If four weeks pass and there is nothing to look at, the sessions have become supervised homework, and you are paying tutor rates for a study companion.

sections.heading: Dahisar, Borivali and Mira Road: what the Western Line does to a timetable
paragraphs: IB home tuition in Dahisar is scheduled around the Dahisar–Western Express Highway corridor, and the corridor is the constraint. Dahisar station is the northern end of the Western Line within the city, which makes the suburb unusually well connected northwards and southwards and badly connected sideways. Metro Lines 2A and 7 now run from Dahisar towards Andheri and Gundavali, which has genuinely changed which tutors will take a standing slot here, and the Link Road gives a second route when the highway is backed up near the toll.

A tutor working this patch will normally also cover Borivali East, Borivali West and Mira Road, and those four areas behave as one matching zone. Borivali East and Borivali West are close enough that a tutor can hold back-to-back slots across the station. Mira Road sits beyond the city boundary but is a short run up the highway, so an evening tutor finishing in Dahisar can reach it. What does not work is pulling someone from Khar or Santacruz for a 6pm lesson: the Western Suburbs run north to south, and crossing the line costs more time than covering twice the distance along it.

This is why a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hire in the north is usually someone already rooted in the north. Searches for IB tutors near me in Dahisar return plenty of profiles with a south-Mumbai address and a willingness to travel, and that willingness is real in September and gone by November. We would rather give you two names in Borivali than six names from Andheri.

Practical scheduling, then. Weekday slots after 7pm hold better than 5pm slots, because a tutor coming off the highway is fighting the same traffic as everyone else and a 5pm start means leaving at 4pm. Saturday mornings are the most reliable slot in the whole week in this part of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and they are the first to go. If two subjects are needed, stacking them on one evening saves the tutor a journey and tends to keep the engagement alive for longer than two separate trips would.

sections.heading: What the school calendar in north Mumbai sets for you
paragraphs: The school year, not the tutor's availability, decides when tutoring is useful in north Mumbai. Families around Dahisar mostly send children to Singapore International School at Dahisar East or JBCN International School, Borivali, and both run a June-start year with the heavy internal assessment load landing in the second half. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with either school, or with any other school named on this page; we mention them because their calendars are what your week actually revolves around.

June to August is the window nobody uses and everybody should. New programme, new subjects, no deadlines yet, which makes it the only time of year when a tutor can work on the underlying skill rather than the assignment due on Friday. A Middle Years Programme student who learns in July how to plan an investigation has a different October from one who learns it the night before the write-up is due.

October and November are when the first real reports arrive, and that is when the search volume for home tuition in Mumbai spikes. The report is useful: criteria levels show you precisely which skill is soft. By January, Diploma Programme students are inside the stretch where Internal Assessment drafts, mock examinations and the Extended Essay all compete for the same evenings, and a new tutor starting in January is doing damage limitation rather than teaching. Starting in September gives the same tutor a term to actually fix something.

There is one more local reality worth naming. Because Singapore International School sits at Dahisar East, this suburb has a steady population of PYP and MYP families, which is unusual this far north and means younger-year tutoring here is not an afterthought. It also means tutor demand peaks at predictable moments across every year group at once, so the week after reports go home is the worst week of the year to start looking for a specific subject at a specific time.

sections.heading: Should you book home tuition in Dahisar or go online?
paragraphs: Book home tuition first and treat online as the fallback, because for most students in Dahisar the value of a tutor in the room is attention, not content. An IB home tutor in Dahisar sitting at your dining table can see the exact moment a student stops writing, can turn the page back to the question they skipped, and can take the phone off the table without a negotiation. On a screen, all three of those things are invisible or impossible.

Online is genuinely better in three situations and it is worth being blunt about them. The first is subject scarcity: if your child needs a Higher Level subject with a thin tutor pool, the right specialist may simply not live within reach of the Western Express Highway, and a weekly screen session with the right teacher beats a weekly house call from the wrong one. The second is the Diploma student who already works independently and needs marking and question-level feedback rather than supervision. The third is the exam term, when a thirty-minute targeted call about one past-paper question is more useful than a ninety-minute visit.

Online is the wrong choice for a Year 8 or Year 9 student who cannot yet work alone for twenty minutes without someone glancing over. It is also the wrong choice when the real problem is organisation rather than understanding, because the folder, the planner and the half-finished draft are all in the room and none of them are on the screen. Parents who switch an unmotivated middle-years student to online to save travel time usually switch back within six weeks.

Hybrid is what most families in this part of Mumbai settle into without planning it. One visit a week for the teaching and the accountability, one short online check between visits before a submission. The home classes carry the relationship and the discipline; the online slot carries the deadline. It also quietly solves the monsoon problem, when the highway near Dahisar can turn a twenty-minute run into an hour and a cancelled visit becomes a screen session instead of a lost week.

sections.heading: How are IB tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every profile we send has been checked on four things: identity, the qualification claimed, the programme levels actually taught, and a reference where one can be reached. That is the floor, and it is deliberately narrow, because the checks that matter most are the ones only you can run. IB home tuition in Dahisar, Mumbai is a person coming into your home every week; a document check is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.

Ask the tutor to name the last three students they taught at your child's exact level and what happened. Vague answers are the signal. Ask what they would do in the first session, and listen for whether they plan to find out where the student is before they plan to teach. Ask them to explain one criterion or one command word to you, the parent, in plain language; a teacher who cannot explain the mark scheme to an adult will not explain it to a fifteen-year-old. If you are considering an IB private tutor Dahisar neighbours recommended, run the same questions anyway, because a recommendation is evidence about one child, not about yours.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success percentage, or claims an official link with a school or an examination board. IB Gram is not affiliated with Singapore International School, JBCN International School, Borivali, the International Baccalaureate Organization, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and neither is any tutor on the platform. We are a matching service: we find and check people, and we do not guarantee grades.

Parents searching for the best IB tutor in Dahisar are really asking a comparison question, and the honest answer is that there is no single best tutor, only a best match for one child in one subject at one level. The tutor who transformed a neighbour's Diploma Programme Economics result may be a poor fit for a Middle Years Programme student who needs structure more than insight. Judge the match on the first four weeks, not on the first phone call, and change it without guilt if the evidence says to.

sections.heading: One tutor for everything, or one tutor per subject?
paragraphs: For a child in the Primary Years Programme, one tutor for everything is right. For a Diploma Programme student, it almost never is. That single answer resolves most of the confusion behind this search, and the middle years are where the judgement call actually lives. A PYP child needs one adult who knows them, builds reading and number confidence, and can work across whatever the unit of inquiry happens to be. Splitting that across three specialists buys nothing and costs the relationship.

In the Middle Years Programme, one strong generalist can usually carry the language and humanities side plus general study skills, while mathematics and the sciences are worth separating once criteria-based marking starts biting. By the Diploma Programme the subject guides are specific enough that a general tutor cannot mark a Higher Level Internal Assessment properly. A Biology IA and a History IA are judged on different things, and a tutor who is honest about which they can mark is more useful than one who takes both.

Scheduling is the hidden constraint. Each additional tutor is another journey up the Dahisar–Western Express Highway corridor and another evening committed, and families regularly discover in week five that three tutors means five evenings gone and no time left for sport or sleep. Two subjects stacked on one evening with the same tutor is often better for the student than three subjects spread perfectly across the week with three specialists. Consider all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Dahisar families realistically book: in practice it is one or two subjects at a time, sequenced, not everything at once.

This is also where cost is decided, so it is worth being direct about what drives it. IB tuition fees in Dahisar depend on the programme and level, on how scarce the subject specialism is, on how far the tutor travels and at what hour, on session length and frequency, and on whether the work is weekly teaching or short-notice examination support. Higher Level sciences and the less common languages cost more than middle-years mathematics because fewer people can teach them. A tutor crossing the city for one evening lesson prices the journey in, which is another reason local matching is cheaper as well as more durable. We publish no price list because any number quoted here would be wrong for somebody; ask for a figure against your actual brief.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks in Mumbai home classes
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at grades. You should be looking for three things: the student can say what they are bad at in specific terms, there is physical evidence of corrected work, and the tutor can tell you what they are working on next without checking their notes. If all three are present, the match is working even if the last test score was flat. If none of them are, four more weeks will not fix it.

At one term, expect a measurable change in one narrow place rather than a general improvement. A Middle Years Programme student who could not structure a criterion D evaluation can usually do it by December if that was the actual target. A Diploma Programme student who was losing marks on paper technique can usually stop losing them. What does not reliably move in a single term is a subject the student fundamentally dislikes, or a backlog of two years of missing foundations in mathematics, and any tutor who tells you otherwise in the first month is selling.

Across a full examination cycle the pattern we see most often is that the tutoring did its work in the months nobody noticed. The student who went from panicking in September to submitting a clean Internal Assessment draft in January did the valuable part in October. The home classes we arrange in Mumbai are priced and scheduled as a term commitment for that reason, not because of any lock-in: there is none, and you can stop whenever you want.

The honest limits are worth stating plainly. We do not guarantee grades, we do not publish success rates, and we will not promise that any tutor can compensate for a subject chosen badly at the start of the Diploma Programme. What a good tutor reliably changes is how a student works: how they read a question, how they plan before writing, how early they start a draft. Those habits usually show in results, and sometimes they show one examination cycle later than a parent wants.

sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition in Dahisar this month
paragraphs: Before the first session, gather three things: the most recent report with the criteria or grade breakdown, the last two pieces of marked work with the teacher's comments still on them, and the school's assessment calendar for the term. Those three documents tell a tutor more in ten minutes than an hour of conversation will, and they are the difference between a first session spent diagnosing and a first session spent guessing.

The first session itself should be mostly the student talking and writing while the tutor watches. A good tutor will set a question slightly above the current level and observe where the work stops: at reading the question, at choosing a method, at the algebra, at the structure of the answer, or at the last step where the conclusion should refer back to the evidence. That observation is the plan. If a tutor arrives and starts teaching chapter one, you have hired a lecturer.

Practically, decide your slot before you decide your tutor. In Dahisar the realistic options are a weekday evening after 7pm, when the Western Express Highway has thinned a little, or a Saturday morning, which is the best slot in the week and the first to be taken. Tell us both your first and second choice, because a tutor who fits the subject and not the slot will not last past the first cancelled session, and we would rather solve that before you meet anyone.

We will come back with two or three profiles, you will speak to them for free, and the one you pick starts the following week. Nothing is booked until you say so, and either side can end it with a week's notice.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Dahisar actually cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one without hearing your brief is guessing. faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be at home for the first one. You are not supervising the teaching; you are confirming that your child is comfortable, that the tutor works the way the call suggested, and that the study space is usable. After that, most families in Dahisar leave the tutor and student to it and simply ask for a two-line message at the end: what was covered and what is set for next week. faqs.question: How does a tutor get past the building gate and the visitor register?
faqs.answer: Give the tutor's name and phone number to your society office or gate before the first visit and ask for a standing weekly entry rather than a fresh visitor pass each time. Most buildings around Dahisar station and in Borivali East will add a recurring tutor to the register once a resident confirms it, which saves five minutes of arguing at the gate every week. If your building requires a photo ID copy, we can have the tutor send it to you directly, and the tutor should carry ID to every session regardless.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows criteria levels, not marks. What should I ask a tutor to fix?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the single criterion with the lowest level and show you the piece of work that produced it. Middle Years Programme criteria are a diagnosis, not a score: a weak criterion C usually means the conclusion did not refer back to the data, and a weak criterion D usually means the evaluation listed limitations without explaining their effect. A tutor who can point at the paragraph that caused the level is reading the report properly. One who responds by offering to re-teach the whole topic has not read it at all.

faqs.question: Is online tuition good enough for a Diploma Programme maths student in Dahisar?
faqs.answer: For an independent Diploma Programme student, usually yes. Screen sessions work well when the student can already sit down with a past paper alone, and the tutor's job is marking, method feedback and question selection. Online is also the right answer when the right specialist lives in Powai or South Mumbai and would never sustain a weekly trip to Dahisar. It is the wrong answer if the student needs someone in the room to keep them working, or if the real problem is an unopened folder rather than an unlearned method.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What happens now?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and we will change the tutor rather than defend the match. First we ask three questions: did the sessions actually happen weekly, is there corrected work to look at, and can the student say what they are bad at more precisely than a month ago. If the answer to the last two is no, the match is wrong and a replacement is the right move. If sessions were missed or the slot kept shifting, the fix is the schedule, not the person. Either way there is no lock-in and nothing to argue about.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one IB subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: At Primary Years Programme and early Middle Years Programme level, yes, and it is usually better. One adult who knows the child can work across subjects and build study habits that transfer. By the Diploma Programme, no: Internal Assessments are marked against subject-specific criteria, and a tutor marking a Biology investigation and a History investigation to the same instincts will mislead you. The practical compromise most Dahisar families reach is one tutor for two related subjects stacked on a single evening, which also saves a second trip up the highway.

faqs.question: Do you work with students from Singapore International School and JBCN International School, Borivali?
faqs.answer: We work with students who attend them, and we have no relationship with the schools themselves. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service, not a coaching chain and not affiliated with Singapore International School, JBCN International School, Borivali, or any other school, nor with the International Baccalaureate Organization. What school familiarity actually buys you is practical: a tutor who has worked with children from a particular school tends to know its assessment rhythm and how its reports are worded, which shortens the diagnosis in the first session.

faqs.question: Is a tutor near me in Dahisar better than a more experienced tutor in Andheri?
faqs.answer: For weekly teaching, the nearer tutor usually wins; for a scarce Higher Level subject, experience wins and you go online. Parents searching for IB tutors near me in Dahisar are right to weight distance heavily, because the thing that kills tutoring in Mumbai is not quality, it is attrition: the lesson that keeps moving to Saturday, then to next week, then stops. A good tutor fifteen minutes away who never cancels will outperform an excellent one who arrives late and tired from the Western Express Highway.

faqs.answer: Usually within a week for mathematics, the sciences and English at middle-years level, and longer for a scarce Higher Level subject or an unusual language. The constraint is almost never finding a qualified person; it is finding one whose free slot matches yours. Saturday mornings and the 7pm to 8:30pm weekday window are the most contested times in this part of Mumbai, so a family flexible about the day gets matched faster than one fixed on a single hour. Tell us two acceptable slots and it moves considerably quicker.

faqs.question: What if we want to stop after a few weeks?

We would rather you ended an engagement that was not working than kept paying out of politeness, and we will ask you why, because that answer improves the next match for somebody else. If the problem is the tutor rather than tutoring, ask for a replacement instead and you keep the same slot and the same brief.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which IB stage is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Check with the school office which programme your child is registered in before you book anybody, because the three International Baccalaureate (IB) stages need genuinely different tutors. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs on transdisciplinary units with almost no formal examination, so a PYP tutor is building reading stamina, number sense and the habit of explaining a method aloud. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) brings in subject criteria and the personal project, and marks begin to depend on how a response is structured, not only on whether the final answer is right.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is a different animal again. Six subjects sit at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), most carry an Internal Assessment (IA), and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) run alongside everything else for two years. A DP1 student who has never been taught to plan a four-thousand-word essay will not learn it from more worked examples. That is a separate skill, and it is worth asking a prospective tutor which of the two years they have supervised.

The join between the two programmes is where Dombivli families get caught. A child finishing MYP5 in a Thane school chooses DP subjects in the same months the school is running trial examinations, and the choice is usually made on who taught them in MYP rather than on what the subject demands at HL. IB home tuition at that point is partly subject work and partly an honest second opinion on whether HL Chemistry is realistic for this particular child.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the internal assessments behind each one
paragraphs: IB Gram covers all IB and IGCSE subjects, and for a Dombivli family the practical question is which of them have a tutor within reach on a weekday evening. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English are the subjects where a local shortlist usually exists. Visual Arts, Music, Psychology and the second-language options thin out fast once you insist on someone who will travel past Thane, which is where a hybrid arrangement starts to make sense rather than being a compromise.

Level matters more than subject name. The gap between Standard Level and Higher Level is not extra chapters bolted on; it is a change in what a question is allowed to assume. An HL Physics question will hand a student an unfamiliar situation and expect them to choose the model themselves. An HL Economics paper rewards a candidate who can argue against their own diagram. A tutor who has only taught Standard Level will coach a competent SL answer and quietly cap the student there.

Then there is the internal assessment in each subject, and this is where most of the recoverable marks sit. Every IB subject carries coursework of some kind, assessed against published criteria rather than a mark scheme of right answers. A science investigation, a mathematics exploration, a history essay: each is marked on how clearly the student has defined their own question and justified their own method. Ask the school coordinator for the current subject guide and the internal deadlines, since the boards revise these on their own cycles and last year's advice goes stale.
A sibling page on this site covers Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel subject codes for families whose child is on the IGCSE route; this page stays with the IB programmes.

Arts, Psychology and second languages often need an online or hybrid fix.

sections.heading: Dombivli, Kalyan, Thane West and Palava City: who can actually reach you?
paragraphs: A tutor who can reach you reliably lives on this side of Thane, and that is the shortest honest answer. Dombivli sits one belt further out than Thane on the Central Line, so the pool is drawn from Dombivli itself, Kalyan, the newer towers of Palava City, and Thane West for anyone willing to make the run eastward. Mulund tutors sometimes cross over for a double slot. Anybody promising to come from Bandra or Powai on a Wednesday evening is describing an intention, not a schedule.

The Thane geography is worth understanding even if you never go there, because it sets your tutor's evening. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the schedule: a tutor living near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and nearly an hour in the evening. A tutor who has already crossed that stretch once for a Thane student is not going to arrive at your flat fresh at eight.

So the sensible pattern for an IB home tutor in Dombivli is a tutor whose whole evening lives on the Kalyan–Dombivli belt. Two students in Palava City and one near Dombivli station makes a workable round. One student in Kalyan, one in Dombivli and one in Kasarvadavali does not, and that is the arrangement that collapses in week six. We ask tutors where their other students are before we send a profile, which is an unglamorous question that prevents most cancellations.

Parents type IB tutors near me Dombivli into Google and get coaching centres sorted by review count. Proximity on a map is not the same as availability at seven in the evening, which is the only measure that matters across this part of Mumbai.

sections.heading: The school calendar Dombivli families in Mumbai live by
paragraphs: The international-board schools your neighbours use are not in Dombivli, which is the single fact that shapes tutoring here. Families travel to Thane or Palava, to schools such as Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and NES International School, and the school day therefore starts with a commute and ends with one. A child who leaves before seven and is home at five has already spent two hours in transit before a tutor rings the bell. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation with either school or with any other named here; they are mentioned because their calendars set the pressure points.

Those calendars are predictable once you have lived through one. The first reports land in late August or September, which is when most searches for an IB home tutor in Dombivli begin. October and November bring MYP criterion-based assessments and the first DP internal assessment drafts. January and February are the hardest stretch of the year for a DP2 student: mock examinations, final IA submissions, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay all arrive within a few weeks of each other.

March and April belong to the examination boards, and a tutor booked in March is mostly doing damage limitation. The families who get the most out of home tuition in this part of Mumbai book in September, run a light two-hour week through the first term, and increase only when the January crush arrives. Booking late is not fatal, but it changes what the tutor can honestly attempt, and a tutor who pretends otherwise in February is selling you something.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix for an IB student in Dombivli
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and should stay the default for younger children. A PYP or MYP student needs someone sitting beside them who can see the page, turn it back two steps and notice that the method was abandoned halfway. The home classes we arrange in Mumbai begin with the tutor working at the same table as the child rather than opposite a screen, and for Years 1 to 8 that physical presence does most of the work. IB home tuition in Dombivli is also easier to keep honest: a parent in the next room hears whether teaching is happening.

Online is the wrong choice for a Year 7 student who cannot yet work alone for twenty minutes, and the right choice for a DP2 student revising HL Mathematics with a specialist who happens to live in Pune. Being past Thane on the Central Line means the scarce HL subjects are genuinely easier to staff online, and pretending otherwise would leave families here choosing between a nearby generalist and nobody. An IB online tutor in Dombivli working with a document camera and shared past papers is a real option, not a downgrade.

Hybrid is what most DP families here settle on by the second term: one home visit a week for the subject that needs a person in the room, one online session for the subject whose specialist lives elsewhere in Mumbai, Maharashtra. The honest trade-off is administrative. Two tutors means two sets of notes, two billing conversations and a parent who has to join them up. If nobody at home can do that joining up, one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families ask about is the steadier choice, even at some loss of depth.

sections.heading: How tutors are checked, and what you should check yourself in Mumbai
paragraphs: Verification covers identity, qualification and board experience, and it stops there, which is worth saying plainly. We confirm who the person is from a government photo identity document, we see the degree certificate for the subject they propose to teach, and we take references from families they have taught in Mumbai. What no platform can verify is chemistry between a particular tutor and your particular child, so the first session is designed to be cancellable rather than binding.

There are three things you should check yourself, in the first conversation, before travel and fees are discussed. Ask which board and which years they have taught, and listen for specifics: a tutor who has taught MYP will talk about criteria and command terms, while a tutor who has only taught state board will talk about chapters and portions. Ask what they will do in the first hour. Ask what they will send you afterwards. A tutor who cannot describe their own first session has not planned one.

Be wary of any tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, a fixed number of marks, or a success rate. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and neither can any honest teacher, because the examination is marked by the board and not by us. An IB private tutor Dombivli parents can rely on will instead tell you what they expect to be able to fix in four weeks and what will take a full term, and will say so in writing where you can hold them to it later.

sections.heading: Why does an IB home tutor in Dombivli cost what they cost?
paragraphs: Five things move the number, and travel is the one that is specific to Dombivli. A tutor crossing from Thane for a single hour is pricing that hour against ninety minutes of road, so the rate for one short weekday session will always look worse than the rate for a two-hour weekend block. Families here get better value from fewer, longer sessions than from three short ones scattered through the week, which is the opposite of the advice that works in a dense suburb where the tutor lives fifteen minutes away.

The other four are board, level, subject scarcity and session length. Diploma Programme work costs more than Middle Years work because the tutor pool is smaller and the preparation is heavier. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level for the same reason. A subject with four available tutors across the Kalyan–Dombivli belt prices differently from one with forty, which is why IB tuition fees in Dombivli for HL Economics and for MYP Mathematics are not in the same bracket. Longer sessions usually carry a lower hourly figure because the travel is amortised.

We publish no price list and quote no figures on this page, deliberately. Any number written here would be wrong for somebody: wrong for the family wanting one subject once a week, wrong for the family wanting three subjects before mocks. What we will do is tell you the range a request like yours is attracting this term, before you speak to a tutor, so that you can recognise a quote that is out of line. There is no single best IB tutor in Dombivli at a single correct price, and a service that implies otherwise is guessing.

One warning about the cheapest quote. In this belt the lowest rate usually comes from a tutor who teaches a different board by day and is reading the IB subject guide the night before. That shows up around week five, when the student asks something that is not in the textbook.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks?
paragraphs: After four weeks you should see changes in behaviour rather than in grades, and that is the correct expectation. The student starts the homework without being asked twice. They can say what a question is testing before they try to answer it. They have stopped rubbing out working. For an MYP student, the clearest early signal is that they begin labelling which criterion a task is assessing without prompting. If none of that has shifted in a month, something is wrong with the match and not with the child.

At one term, marks should have moved on the kind of task the tutor has actually worked on. A tutor who has spent eight weeks on Paper 1 technique has no claim on an internal assessment grade. Ask at the start which assessment the tutor is targeting, then judge them on that one. A term is also long enough for the honest diagnosis to arrive: sometimes it is that the student is in the wrong level, and a tutor who tells you that in November has done you a bigger favour than one who keeps coaching HL.

Over a full examination cycle, the realistic goal is that the student is not surprised by the paper. No tutor controls the grade. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, does not publish success rates, and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. What we can promise is the process: a stated diagnosis, a stated target assessment, written session notes, and a replacement tutor arranged quickly when the fit is wrong. The all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Dombivli parents arrange through us are judged on that, not on a slogan.

sections.heading: Starting IB home classes in Dombivli this month
paragraphs: Have three things ready and the first week goes faster. The most recent school report, including the comment paragraphs that parents usually skip; two marked pieces of work with the teacher's annotations still on them; and an honest note of the two evening windows that will survive a busy fortnight. The report tells a tutor what the school thinks. The marked work tells them what is actually happening, which is frequently different. The windows tell us which tutors on the Kalyan–Dombivli belt can realistically be offered.

The first session then runs as a diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend most of it watching your child work rather than teaching: a short written task, a conversation about how they revise, and two or three questions deliberately pitched above the current level to see where the method breaks. You should receive a written summary afterwards naming what will be worked on first and what is being left alone until later.

Keep the first four weeks under review rather than committing to a term. Most families who are unhappy at week six were already uneasy at week two and said nothing. We would far rather move you to a different IB home tutor in Dombivli early than preside over a polite arrangement that nobody wants to cancel. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need is easier to swap in September than in January, which is another argument for starting now.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Dombivli for an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor already lives on this belt. Tutors based in Dombivli, Kalyan or Palava City treat a weekday evening slot here as normal, and Thane West tutors will do it for a longer block rather than a single hour. What does not hold is a tutor coming from the western suburbs; that arrangement looks fine in September and fails by October. When we send you a profile we tell you where the tutor lives and where their other students are, because a tutor with two other families in Palava City will keep your Tuesday and a tutor crossing the whole city will not.

faqs.question: Why do so many Dombivli families end up with online IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because the schools and the specialist tutors are both on the other side of Thane. Dombivli is a belt beyond Thane on the Central Line, so for crowded subjects there is a genuine local pool, while for Higher Level Economics, Psychology or a second language the nearest experienced IB teacher may be nowhere near the Kalyan–Dombivli belt at all. Online carries that load. For younger children we still push hard for a tutor in the room, and most DP families end up with a mix: one in-person subject, one online specialist.

faqs.question: What should I ask in the first phone call with a tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask which IB years they have taught, not which they have studied. Then ask three follow-ups: what will the first hour look like, what will you send me afterwards, and what will you not attempt this term. A tutor who has really taught the Middle Years Programme will answer in terms of criteria and command terms. One who has taught a different board will answer in terms of chapters and portions. Both answers are useful; only one of them matches what your child is being marked against at school.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Dombivli for just one subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually the better place to start. One subject, two hours a week, reviewed at four weeks, tells you more than three subjects started at once. If the diagnosis in session one shows the real problem is a general one, which is often reading the question rather than the mathematics, we will say so and you can decide whether to widen. Starting narrow also keeps the week survivable for a child who is already commuting to Thane or Palava daily and getting home at five.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP5 and choosing DP subjects. Is tutoring useful now?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for a different reason than you expect. At that point the most valuable hours are not extra content; they are an honest second opinion on whether the Higher Level choice is realistic. A tutor who has taught both MYP5 and DP1 can look at two pieces of marked work and tell you where the step up will hurt. They can also start the habits DP demands, mainly planning long written work, which is the skill most new DP students arrive without and the one no amount of past papers fixes.

faqs.question: Is there parking at the gate, or should the tutor come by train?
faqs.answer: Most tutors on this belt travel by train to Dombivli station and take an auto to the building, so the practical question is whether your society allows an auto to the lobby and how the visitor register works after seven. Tell us at booking if your gate requires a resident to call in each visitor, because a tutor who has to wait fifteen minutes at the gate each week will quietly start arriving late. Where a tutor drives, ask your committee whether visitor parking is available at the hour you have chosen.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we arrange a different tutor, without a fresh deposit and without needing you to justify the decision. In practice we ask two questions first: has the tutor been late or inconsistent, or is the teaching itself not landing. The answer changes who we send next. A punctuality problem usually means we misjudged the travel, and the fix is a tutor living closer or a different time. A teaching mismatch means we send someone with a different style, often a stricter one, which parents are frequently too polite to ask for.

faqs.question: How much does IB home tuition in Dombivli cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things and we will not invent a figure. Board and level come first, because Diploma Programme and Higher Level work draw on a smaller pool of tutors than Middle Years work. Subject scarcity comes next. Then travel, which matters here more than in a dense suburb, and session length, since a two-hour block usually carries a lower hourly figure than a single hour. Tell us the subject, the level and the windows and we will give you the current range for requests like yours before you speak to anyone.

faqs.question: Do you cover Kalyan and Palava City as well as Dombivli?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we treat them as one matching cluster rather than three separate areas. A tutor with students in Palava City and Dombivli is running a sensible evening; a tutor with one student in Kalyan and one in Kasarvadavali is not, and that round is what collapses in week six. Thane West sits at the edge of the cluster: tutors there will come for a longer session but rarely for a single hour, and Mulund tutors occasionally cross over when two families can share an evening between them.

faqs.question: Does my child need me at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but somebody should be at home, especially for the first few weeks and for younger children. You do not need to sit in. What helps is being within earshot at the start and the end: the start tells you whether the tutor settles the child quickly, and the last five minutes are when the useful summary happens. For a DP2 student, stepping back entirely is usually right. For a Year 6 child, a parent in the next room is part of why home tuition works at all.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School, NES International School, or any other school, board or organisation named anywhere on this site. We name them because their calendars and board pathways set the assessment pressure points that Dombivli families actually live with. We also do not guarantee grades or publish success rates. Tutors are verified for identity, qualification and prior board experience, and what they will attempt is stated in writing before you commit to a term.

For an IB home tutor in Dronagiri that last answer carries more weight than it would in Powai or Bandra, because the number of trained Diploma Programme (DP) and Middle Years Programme (MYP) specialists living inside this node is genuinely small, and anyone matching tutors in Navi Mumbai honestly will tell you so in the first call rather than the fourth.

sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child in, and what changes at each stage?
paragraphs: Three programmes sit under the International Baccalaureate and the tutoring they need is not interchangeable. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs to roughly Year 5, is inquiry led and carries no external examinations. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers Years 6 to 10 and is graded against published criteria rather than percentages. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two year course that ends in external papers, and it behaves like nothing that came before it.

PYP work at home looks almost nothing like tutoring as most Indian parents experienced it. There is no chapter to finish and no weekly test to beat. A PYP home tutor in Dronagiri, Mumbai spends the hour on reading fluency, number sense, the vocabulary of the current unit of inquiry, and the habit of explaining an answer rather than producing one. Parents who moved here from a state or national board often cannot see a gap at all, because the report says things like developing and consolidating instead of giving a mark out of fifty. The useful diagnostic at this stage is to listen to the child read aloud for five minutes and ask them to explain what they just read.

MYP is where most families in the Dronagiri–Ulwe node first ask for help, and the reason is usually the criteria. Each subject is assessed against four strands with their own command terms, and a student can know the content perfectly and still score badly because the response was not structured the way the criterion asks. Criterion based marking rewards process, and process is teachable. Years 9 and 10 add the personal project and, in many schools, the first serious coursework the child has ever had to plan alone.

DP is the stage where the calendar starts doing the damage. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus TOK, the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service, all landing in the same eighteen months. The subject choice made in Year 11 constrains everything afterwards, which is why a conversation about level and route belongs before the first exam result rather than after it. Families searching for the best IB tutor in Dronagiri in DP2 are often really searching for someone who can rescue a timetable, and that is a different and harder job.
