sections.heading: Starting with an IB home tutor in Powai this week
paragraphs: To get a useful shortlist back on the first attempt, send five things: the school and year group, the exact programme stage, the subjects in question, the society and tower, and two evening windows that genuinely work. The society name matters more here than anywhere else in Mumbai, because it decides which tutors can realistically reach you. Parents who send Powai and nothing else get a slower and worse match than parents who send Hiranandani Gardens, tower name, Thursday or Friday after half past six.

Have three documents ready for the first session: the most recent school report, the last two marked pieces of work, and your school's assessment calendar if it has been published. The report tells the tutor what the school thinks. The marked work tells her what is actually going wrong, which is usually narrower and more fixable. The calendar tells her how much runway there is. With those three on the table, a competent tutor can tell you at the end of the first hour what she thinks the problem is and what she would do about it over six weeks.

Internally we tag this kind of request as all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, which is a clumsy label for a simple thing: a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families might ask about, one enquiry, any year group, and a shortlist of people who can get to your door. If your child is at the Middle Years Programme to Diploma Programme step, say so, because that is the transition where the right tutor matters most and the wrong one wastes a term.

One last practical note for this corridor. Ask for a start date, not a start week. A tutor who says she can begin Tuesday at seven and sends her identity details for the gate on Monday is a tutor who has thought about the journey. A tutor who says she will confirm closer to the time has not, and in Powai that difference shows up by the third lesson rather than the tenth.
bullets: Send school, year group, programme stage, subjects, society and two evening windows
Have the last report and two marked pieces of work ready for session one
Ask for a start date and the tutor's gate details, not a start week
Say if your child is at the MYP to DP transition; it changes the match
Book March and April slots in November, not in February

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Powai for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, but which tutor depends entirely on where she starts from. Because Powai has no station, a 7pm start is reliable from Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali or Kanjurmarg, workable from Ghatkopar, and genuinely difficult from Andheri East in the evening peak. We therefore shortlist by road distance rather than by credentials alone. If your preferred time is 7pm sharp on a weekday, ask us for a tutor inside the corridor and expect to wait a little longer for the match. If you can offer 8pm or a weekend morning, the pool widens considerably.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get through the gate at Hiranandani Gardens or Lodha Bellissimo?
faqs.answer: The same way any regular visitor does, and it is worth setting up once rather than weekly. Send your society office or gate desk the tutor's name, phone number and identity document before the first visit, and ask for her to be recorded as a standing weekly visitor rather than a one-off. In tower clusters such as Hiranandani Gardens, also tell her the tower name and the entrance, because the layout is large enough that the wrong gate costs fifteen minutes. Where clearance runs through a single visitor desk, a pre-listed tutor walks in and an unlisted one waits.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Powai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them is a published rate. Fees depend on the programme stage, whether the subject is taken at Higher Level or Standard Level, how scarce that specialist is in this corridor, the session length, and how far the tutor travels to reach you. A tutor living inside Powai who walks to your tower has no travel cost to recover; a Diploma Programme specialist coming across from Andheri East in the evening peak does. We do not publish figures because any number would be wrong for half the families asking. Settle the rate, the session length and the cancellation rule in writing before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Where in the home should the lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: At a table in a shared room with the door open, not in a bedroom and not on a sofa. The dining table is the standard answer in most Powai flats and it works: hard surface, room for two sets of books, and enough household traffic that nobody is isolated. Keep the television off, keep phones out of reach rather than face down, and make sure there is a plug point for a laptop if the subject needs past papers on screen. If your flat is genuinely short of space, a society study room or library is a reasonable alternative, provided it is bookable at the same time each week.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home while the session runs?
faqs.answer: Someone adult should be in the flat, particularly for the first few weeks and for younger students. You do not need to sit in the room, and hovering usually makes a teenager worse rather than better. What helps is being present enough to hear the tone of the hour and to catch the tutor for two minutes at the end. That two-minute handover is where you learn whether the agreed work was done, and it is far more useful than a monthly written report. For Primary Years Programme students, a parent nearby is not optional.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level or Standard Level help first?
faqs.answer: Start with the subject where she is closest to losing the thread, which is not always the Higher Level one. Higher Level subjects demand unfamiliar application and sustained argument, so they consume more tutoring hours per improvement, but a Standard Level subject that has quietly collapsed will cost her more in the final total. The practical approach is to spend the first session diagnosing across both, then commit hours where the gap is widest rather than where the label looks most serious. Your Diploma Programme coordinator can confirm the current combination rules if changing a level is still an option.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one IB subject?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and you should be sceptical when the answer is an easy yes. Within a group, a strong tutor often handles two related subjects well. Across groups, a single tutor covering a science, a language and an essay subject at Higher Level is unusual and worth probing. For younger Primary Years Programme and Middle Years Programme students a single generalist is often the better arrangement, because consistency matters more than depth. For Diploma Programme students we would rather give you two specialists on different evenings than one person stretched across subjects she teaches at different standards.

faqs.question: Is online a real substitute when the Chandivali road is blocked?
faqs.answer: For a single session, yes, and that is exactly what it is best at. Agree at the start that a blocked road or a monsoon evening converts the lesson to an online one rather than cancelling it, and the term stops losing hours to weather. An IB online tutor in Powai can run worked problems and essay drafting on a shared screen effectively. What online does not replace is the accountability of someone arriving at the door, so use it as the fallback and the review slot rather than the main arrangement, especially for a student who has been drifting.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss a session during the Diploma Programme examination run?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as you can and agree in advance how missed lessons are handled, because in March and April there is very little spare capacity in Powai. Most tutors will reschedule a session cancelled with a day's notice and charge for one cancelled an hour before, which is reasonable given the travel involved. During school mock weeks, families often switch to shorter, more frequent online slots instead of the usual home hour, and that is a sensible adjustment rather than a downgrade. Put the rule in writing in the first week and neither side has to negotiate it under pressure.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so, with one specific example. Three sessions is enough to know whether a student will talk to this person, and not enough to know whether the teaching is working, so the useful complaint at that point is about fit rather than results. We arrange a replacement, pass on what the first tutor recorded about where your child actually is, and hold the same slot where the new tutor's travel allows it. You do not have to tell the outgoing tutor anything; that conversation is ours to have. Waiting a full term out of politeness is the expensive option.

faqs.question: How soon can an IB home tutor in Powai start?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week for common subjects, and two to three weeks for a scarce Higher Level specialist who also has to be reachable in this corridor. The limiting factor is almost never qualification; it is whether someone with the right subject already holds free evenings within reach of Powai. Sending your society name and two workable evening windows in the first message is what shortens this most. If your need is urgent, ask us for an online start while the home match is arranged, then move the lesson to your table once the right local tutor is confirmed.

faqs.question: Our neighbour's deadlines are different from ours. Why?
faqs.answer: Because internal deadlines are set by each school, not by the International Baccalaureate. Two Powai children in the same tower attending different schools can have internal assessment submission dates weeks apart, and school mock examinations rarely align either. This is why we ask for your school's own published assessment calendar at the first session instead of working from a general IB timetable. It is also why advice swapped at the gate is unreliable: the parent telling you there is no rush may be looking at a genuinely later deadline than yours.

ib-home-tutor-in-powai.closingCta: Send one message with the school, year group, programme stage, subjects, your society and two evening windows. You get two or three checked profiles back with qualifications you can verify, and you speak to the tutor before any address or schedule is confirmed. The first session is diagnostic and ends with a written six-week plan. If the match is wrong, tell us and we arrange another. IB home tuition in Powai is easiest to set up in June and hardest in March, so start earlier than feels necessary.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB home tutor in Prabhadevi
paragraphs: A request for an IB home tutor in Prabhadevi arrives carrying three pieces of information that matter and a great deal that does not. What matters is the year group, the exact subjects and levels, and the two evening windows the family can genuinely keep free every week. What does not matter at this stage is how the request is worded. One parent writes asking for a Standard Level Biology teacher. Another asks for somebody to fix a child's Mathematics before the next report. A third simply wants a tutor who can reach the flat near the seaface on Tuesdays. All three become the same internal brief.

From there the shortlist is built by road rather than by postcode. Prabhadevi sits on the Prabhadevi–Worli seaface, with Prabhadevi (Elphinstone Road) as the nearest station, so the plausible pool is every tutor already teaching between Colaba and Dadar. We do not begin with the full roster of International Baccalaureate (IB) tutors in Mumbai and filter downwards by distance. We begin with the handful who already hold a standing commitment within a few kilometres and work outwards only if the subject is scarce. The reason is retention, not convenience. A tutor whose Thursday already ends in Lower Parel will still be at your door in week nineteen.

Two or three profiles then go to the parent, with the subject history, the levels taught and the realistic arrival window for each. Nobody is asked to choose on a photograph. The intake call is where most of the useful information surfaces anyway: whether the child has stopped asking questions in class, whether an Internal Assessment (IA) draft deadline is already overdue, whether an older sibling in the house also needs a slot. Home tuition in this part of Mumbai is a household arrangement, and pretending otherwise produces a schedule that collapses by Diwali.

The first session is diagnostic and the family should expect it to look unimpressive. No syllabus is covered. The tutor reads the last two report cards, the most recent class test with the marks still on it, and whatever the child can produce from memory on a blank sheet. That is the baseline against which week four gets measured.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP inside one Prabhadevi household
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate is not one thing, and the commonest mistake a family makes when hiring is to treat it as one. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early and middle primary years and is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subjects, so the useful tutor there is not a subject expert at all but somebody who can build reading stamina, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud. A PYP parent who hires a Diploma Programme Physics specialist has bought the wrong person at a higher rate.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the five years that follow and is where most of the trouble in Prabhadevi households actually starts. Assessment moves to criterion-referenced marking across subject groups, and the band a child is given is not a percentage. A parent reading a 5 on a report assumes roughly sixty per cent and is wrong in a way that matters: the band describes what the work demonstrated against a published descriptor, and moving up is a matter of doing a specific thing the descriptor names, not of scoring more marks. An IB home tutor in Prabhadevi working with MYP students spends the first fortnight on that translation alone.

The Diploma Programme (DP) brings the six subject groups, the Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) split, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Internal Assessment in nearly every subject. The pressure is not conceptual difficulty so much as simultaneity. A DP1 student choosing subjects in the first term is making a decision that constrains university applications two years later, and very few fifteen-year-olds have the information to make it well.

We ask which programme and which year before anything else, because the answer changes the kind of person we look for, not merely the subject label. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Prabhadevi might cover, the stage matters more than the name on the timetable.

MYP: criterion-referenced bands, subject-group breadth, early research habits

sections.heading: Which IB subject choices cause the most trouble?
paragraphs: Subject choice causes more avoidable damage than weak teaching does. The two decisions that go wrong most often are Mathematics route and Higher Level count. Mathematics in the Diploma Programme splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and the choice is made on where the student is going, not on which sounds easier. A student aiming at engineering or economics at a competitive university generally needs the analysis route, and a student who picked the applications route because a friend did will discover the mismatch at application time rather than at report time.

The Higher Level count is the second. Three Higher Level subjects is the standard load, and a student who takes three sciences at Higher Level because every option looked interesting in Year 10 is carrying three substantial Internal Assessments through the same fortnights. A tutor cannot fix a timetable, but a tutor who has taken students through two exam cycles can tell a DP1 family in November what the following October will feel like, which is the information the decision actually needs.

Internal Assessment is where marks are lost quietly. Every subject carries one in some form, and the common failure is not weak content but a research question that cannot be answered within the word count. A Chemistry investigation built around a reaction the student cannot measure precisely at school, or an Economics commentary on an article with no usable data, loses marks that no amount of revision recovers. The fix is early: a tutor should see the research question before the experiment, not the draft after it.

For Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel subject choices at the International General Certificate of Secondary Education stage, a sibling page covers the Core and Extended tier decision in full. Here the focus stays on the IB side of the same question. Consult the current subject guide and your school's IB coordinator for the structure that applies to your child's examination session, because the boards revise these on their own cycles.

sections.heading: Worli, Lower Parel and Dadar: the evening a Mumbai tutor can actually hold
paragraphs: Prabhadevi has one property no other locality in Mumbai quite shares. It is the hinge between South Mumbai and Dadar, which means a tutor based here is the only tutor in the city who can reasonably hold a South Mumbai family and a Dadar family on the same evening. In practice that produces a Tuesday that runs from a flat on the seaface at half past five to a Dadar address by half past seven, and both families get a tutor who is not exhausted and not late. Everywhere else in the island city, a tutor who tries that loses the second slot inside a month.

The consequence for a Prabhadevi parent is pricing and availability rather than geography. A tutor who can fill an evening efficiently has less reason to refuse a single ninety-minute slot at an awkward hour, because the slot is not stranded. The same tutor asked to come up from Chembur or across from Andheri would need the whole evening to justify the trip. This is why we match inside the island for home tuition across this part of Mumbai rather than casting the net city-wide and hoping.

The coverage from here runs to Worli immediately south along the seaface, Lower Parel inland across the rail corridor, and Dadar to the north. Worli and Lower Parel are short enough hops that a tutor can absorb a fifteen-minute overrun without wrecking the next appointment. Dadar is the direction where the rail corridor matters: a tutor coming from Dadar station to Prabhadevi is quick by train and slow by road at six in the evening, and the choice they make affects whether your session starts on time.

South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow, and parents consistently underestimate this. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers about eight kilometres and can still lose a large part of an hour at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. The Coastal Road has changed the northbound run meaningfully; the signals have not changed at all. An IB home tutor in Prabhadevi who already lives on this stretch is worth more than a more decorated tutor forty minutes away.

sections.heading: The school calendar Prabhadevi families plan around
paragraphs: Children from this stretch of Mumbai are spread across a small number of international schools rather than concentrated in one, and that shapes how tutoring has to be scheduled. Families here commonly attend JBCN International School, Parel, which is a short run inland, and Ryan Global School, which has a Worli presence on the seaface side. Both are named here only as local context. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with JBCN International School, Parel, Ryan Global School, or any other school mentioned on this page.

What matters practically is that these schools do not share a single assessment calendar, so a tutor serving two children in the same building may be working to two different sets of deadlines. The IB year in Mumbai starts in the first half of the academic year with settling and unit work, tightens through the second term as Internal Assessment drafts come due, and converges on the May examination session for Diploma Programme candidates. The months that hurt are the ones where draft deadlines, mock examinations and school productions collide.

For a Diploma Programme student in Prabhadevi sitting the May session, the fortnight where a Physics investigation draft, a Theory of Knowledge essay outline and a Mathematics exploration all come due is the point at which home tuition stops being about content and becomes about sequencing. A tutor who has done this before will tell the student which one to finish first and why. A tutor who has not will try to teach the syllabus faster.

The practical instruction for a parent is to put the school's published assessment calendar in front of the tutor in the first week, not the fourth. Mock examination dates, draft submission dates and the school's own holiday pattern determine where the slack is. Home classes booked without that calendar in hand are booked on guesswork, and guesswork is what produces the panic call in February.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for IB students in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead option and for most families here it is the right one. A tutor in the room reads what a child will not say: the pause before a question, the page that gets turned too quickly, the calculator reached for on a problem that should not need one. For younger Primary Years Programme and Middle Years Programme students the physical presence is most of the value, because attention at that age is not something a screen holds reliably for ninety minutes. The honest cost of home tuition is scheduling rigidity. The slot is fixed by travel, so moving it is a negotiation rather than a click.

Online works better than most parents expect and worse than most providers claim. It works well for a Higher Level Diploma Programme subject where the scarce thing is a genuine specialist, and specialists in a narrow subject are not always available within reach of the seaface. It works well for short, frequent contact during a revision fortnight. It works badly when a student needs to be watched working, and it works badly when the household has no quiet corner, which in a Mumbai flat is a real constraint rather than a hypothetical one.

Hybrid is what most of our longer-running arrangements settle into without anybody planning it. One session a week at home for the diagnostic and the difficult teaching, one shorter online session for review, marking feedback and the specific question the child could not ask on Tuesday. It also absorbs the monsoon, when a Prabhadevi evening can turn an eight-kilometre journey into an hour, and the alternative to an online session is no session at all.

A family wanting an IB online tutor in Prabhadevi should ask the same verification questions they would ask of a tutor coming to the flat, because the screen hides more than it reveals. An IB private tutor Prabhadevi families keep for a second year is almost always one who adjusted the mode when the term demanded it rather than defending the original arrangement.
bullets: Home tuition first: the tutor sees what the student will not report
Online for scarce Higher Level specialists and short revision contact
Hybrid handles monsoon evenings without cancelling the week

sections.heading: How are IB home tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor on the platform is checked on identity, on claimed qualification and on teaching history before a profile reaches a parent, and the subject claim is checked separately from the teaching claim. A candidate who says they teach Diploma Programme Chemistry at Higher Level is asked which syllabus they last taught, which Internal Assessment they last supervised and what went wrong with it. The last question is the useful one. A tutor who cannot name a failure has not supervised enough work to be trusted with your child's investigation.

Verification does not end at onboarding. Parent feedback after the four-week review is recorded against the tutor, and a tutor who is repeatedly late, repeatedly rescheduling or repeatedly vague about what was covered stops being shortlisted. For an IB home tutor in Prabhadevi that record includes punctuality in the evening peak, because a tutor who is honest about arriving at six forty rather than six thirty is a better match than one who promises six thirty and delivers chaos.

There are checks only a parent can do, and they are worth ten minutes. Ask to see a marked piece of work the tutor has given feedback on, with the feedback visible. Ask what they would do in the first three sessions and listen for whether the answer is specific to your child's reports or generic. Ask directly how they handle a student who has stopped doing homework. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest tutor can offer one.

IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor on the platform is authorised to. What verification buys is a smaller chance of wasting a term on somebody who cannot do the job, and a route to a replacement that does not require starting the search again. Home tuition across this part of Mumbai works on continuity, and continuity is what a bad first match destroys.

Subject claims tested with syllabus and Internal Assessment questions

sections.heading: What IB home tuition in Prabhadevi actually costs you in time and money
paragraphs: Nobody publishes a credible price list for this work and anybody who does is averaging across situations that are not comparable. What a parent can know in advance is what the number depends on, and there are five factors that move it. Board and level come first: a Diploma Programme Higher Level science sits at the top of the range and a Primary Years Programme numeracy slot at the bottom, because the pool of people who can teach the former is a fraction of the pool who can teach the latter. Subject scarcity is the second and it is sharper than parents expect.

Travel distance is the third factor and in South Mumbai it behaves unusually. The distances are short and the times are long, so what you are paying for is not kilometres but the slot the tutor cannot sell to anybody else because they are sitting at the Haji Ali signal. This is precisely where the Prabhadevi position helps: a tutor who can chain a seaface session into a Dadar session loses less of the evening, and a tutor who loses less of the evening has less reason to price for the loss. IB tuition fees in Prabhadevi are quoted against a usable evening rather than against a map.

Session length and frequency are the fourth, and the fifth is the shape of the engagement. Two ninety-minute sessions a week through a term is a different commitment from an intensive fortnight before mock examinations, and the second is usually quoted higher per hour because it cannot be planned around. A family that fixes the slot early in the academic year, before the tutor's evenings fill, has more room to negotiate than a family calling in February.

The question worth asking is not what the hourly rate is but what the term costs and what it is expected to change. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families might want sounds economical and is usually a false economy, because one person covering six Diploma Programme subjects is covering four of them thinly. Two specialists for two genuinely weak subjects beats one generalist for all six, and costs less over a year than the generalist plus the panic hiring in March.

sections.heading: What four weeks of IB home classes should change
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at grades. Grades at four weeks are noise, and a tutor who points to one improved test score as evidence is selling rather than reporting. What should have changed is the shape of the homework. The child should be starting work without being asked twice, should be able to say what the current unit is about in a sentence, and should be bringing a specific question to the session rather than a general complaint about the subject. If none of that has happened in four sessions, the match is wrong and saying so early costs nothing.

At one term the measurable things appear. Internal Assessment drafts are submitted on time rather than late, class test marks stop swinging wildly, and the teacher's comment on the report changes register from effort to understanding. A term is also long enough to see whether the gain is real or whether the tutor has been doing the work. The test for that is simple: give the student an unseen past paper question with nobody in the room and see what happens.

At one exam cycle the honest statement is narrower than families want. A student who was failing a subject and now passes it comfortably is a real outcome. A student who was at the top of the middle band and now sits at the bottom of the top band is a real outcome. A student who was going to get a particular grade and was promised two more is a fiction, and the promise is the warning sign rather than the ambition. We do not guarantee grades and we do not publish success rates, because the honest version of both is unflattering to everybody in this industry.

The limits are worth stating plainly. Home tuition cannot replace attendance, cannot substitute for a student who will not open the book, and cannot compress two years of missing foundations into a pre-examination fortnight. Where it reliably works is on a specific, diagnosed gap with a student who turns up. That is the honest claim and it is enough.

sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition in Prabhadevi this month
paragraphs: Before you send a request, spend ten minutes gathering four things. The last two report cards, including the teacher comments nobody reads. The most recent class test or mock paper with the marks and the corrections still on it. The school's assessment calendar for the term. And the two weekday evening windows your household can genuinely hold, which is usually fewer than the number you think you have. A request with those four attached gets a useful shortlist in a day; a request saying the child needs help in Maths gets a conversation first.

The intake call takes about a quarter of an hour. We ask the year group and programme, the exact subjects and levels, what the school has already said, and what has already been tried. We ask about the room: whether there is a table, whether the television is in the same space, whether a younger sibling will be in and out. These are not polite questions. A session held at the dining table in a flat where dinner is being cooked at seven behaves differently from one held in a study.

Then two or three profiles arrive with the subject history and the realistic arrival window for each. You pick one, the first session is scheduled, and that session is diagnostic. Expect the tutor to leave with your child's test papers and return the following week with a written note naming the first three things being fixed and in what order. That note is the thing to hold them to.

Searches for the best IB tutor in Prabhadevi, or for IB tutors near me Prabhadevi, are really asking the same narrow question: will somebody competent turn up every Tuesday until June. faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Prabhadevi actually do in the first session?
faqs.answer: Almost nothing that looks like teaching. The first session is a diagnostic: the tutor reads the last two report cards, works through the most recent marked test, and asks the student to attempt two or three questions cold so they can see where the reasoning breaks rather than where the marks were lost. Expect questions about what the school has already said and what has already been tried. The output is a written note the following week naming the first three things being fixed and in what order, which is the document to judge the arrangement against at week four.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Prabhadevi for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the easier parts of Mumbai to staff for a late weekday slot. Prabhadevi sits between South Mumbai and Dadar, so a tutor can chain an early seaface session into a later one without crossing the city. The honest caveat is the arrival window. A tutor coming through the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals in the evening peak should quote a ten-minute range rather than a time, and a tutor who insists on an exact minute is either coming from very close by or is about to disappoint you.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Prabhadevi depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and no honest answer quotes a figure without them. Board and level, because a Diploma Programme Higher Level science draws on a much smaller pool of teachers than a primary numeracy slot. Subject scarcity, which in practice matters more than distance. Travel, priced as the evening time a tutor cannot sell to anybody else. Session length and frequency. And the shape of the engagement, since a fixed term slot booked early is cheaper per hour than an intensive fortnight before mock examinations. Ask what the term costs and what it is meant to change, not what the hourly rate is.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does one IB subject need?
faqs.answer: One ninety-minute session a week is the usual starting point for a single Diploma Programme or Middle Years Programme subject, moving to two during a mock examination run or an Internal Assessment crunch. Two subjects at once is manageable; four is usually a sign that the real problem is organisation rather than subject knowledge, and adding tutors makes it worse. Start with the weakest subject, run the four-week review, and add a second only if the first has produced a visible change in how homework gets started.

faqs.question: Our building needs a gate pass for regular visitors. How is that handled?
faqs.answer: The tutor is given the building name, the flat number and the parent's contact before the first visit, and most Prabhadevi buildings will issue a standing visitor entry once a parent registers the tutor at the gate as a weekly visitor. It is worth doing that in week one rather than letting the tutor argue with security every Tuesday, because ten minutes lost at the gate is ten minutes lost from the session. If your society requires identity documents on file, ask us and the tutor will carry what is needed to the first visit.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week three rather than week ten. A replacement is arranged from the same shortlist where possible, so the new tutor inherits the diagnostic note rather than starting from a blank page, and the student does not repeat the first-session interrogation. We also ask what specifically failed, because the useful distinction is between a tutor who cannot teach the subject and a tutor who cannot hold this particular child's attention. The second is a matching error and it is ours to fix; the first affects whether that tutor keeps being shortlisted at all.

faqs.question: Does online IB tutoring work as well as home classes?
faqs.answer: For some things, better. Online is the right call for a scarce Higher Level specialist who is not available within reach of the seaface, for short frequent contact during a revision fortnight, and for monsoon evenings when the alternative is cancelling. It is weaker when a student needs to be watched working, when the household has no quiet corner, and for younger Primary Years Programme and Middle Years Programme children whose attention a screen does not hold for ninety minutes. Most long-running arrangements end up hybrid: one session in the room, one shorter session online for review.

faqs.question: Do you cover PYP, or only MYP and DP?
faqs.answer: All three, but with different kinds of tutor. Primary Years Programme work is about reading stamina, number sense and getting a child to explain their thinking aloud, and the right person there is an experienced primary teacher rather than a subject specialist. Middle Years Programme work centres on criterion-referenced marking and the breadth of the subject groups. Diploma Programme work is subject-deep and deadline-driven. Hiring a Diploma Programme Physics specialist for a nine-year-old is a common and expensive mistake, so we ask the programme and the year before we look at subjects at all.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two children in different IB years?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. A tutor can often take a Middle Years Programme student and a Diploma Programme Standard Level student in the same subject back to back in the same flat, which saves travel and usually improves the rate. It works badly across programmes and across unrelated subjects: a tutor strong in Diploma Programme Chemistry teaching primary numeracy to a sibling is doing a job somebody else does better. Ask for honesty on this rather than convenience, because a tutor who agrees to everything is telling you something about their standards.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: For the first session, briefly, so you hear how the tutor talks to your child. After that, generally not. A student who is being watched by a parent will not admit to not understanding something, and the admission is the whole point of the session. What replaces sitting in is a short written note after each session, or a five-minute conversation at the door. If you want to know whether the work is landing, ask the tutor for an unseen question your child can attempt alone rather than observing the lesson.

faqs.question: What if there is no quiet study space at home for sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so at the intake call and the match changes. A session at the dining table in a flat where dinner is being cooked is a real constraint and a good tutor plans around it: shorter focused blocks, more written work set for later, and no activity that needs sustained silence. Some families use a building's reading room or society common area where one exists. For a Prabhadevi flat with no spare corner, an earlier slot before the household fills up usually works better than a later one, and that is a scheduling decision to make at the start.

faqs.question: What can a tutor honestly change before the next report?
faqs.answer: Within one reporting cycle, the realistic targets are narrow and worth stating. Homework submitted on time. An Internal Assessment research question that is actually answerable. A specific topic the student had stopped attempting now attempted. Teacher comments shifting from effort to understanding. What a tutor cannot do in a cycle is rebuild two years of missing foundations or move a student several bands. We do not guarantee grades and nobody on the platform is permitted to promise a specific one, which is the answer to give any tutor who offers it.

sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Your child is in one of three International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes, and the answer changes everything about what a tutor should do in the room. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs to roughly Year 5 and is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than subjects. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and assesses eight subject groups against four published criteria each. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years, with six subjects at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL) plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Confuse the three and you buy the wrong help.

This matters inside one tower more than you would expect. Raheja Imperia holds families whose children span all three programmes at once, because the building fills across age groups rather than in a single cohort. The flat on one floor needs somebody who can sit with a PYP child and a set of inquiry questions. Three floors up, a DP1 parent needs somebody who has read the current subject guide for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and knows what the exploration asks for. IB home tuition in Raheja Imperia therefore has to be specified by programme before anyone talks about rates or evenings.

A practical warning about structure. Do not take assessment detail from a blog post, this page included. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, so component names, criteria wording and the balance between internal and external assessment move. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the guide that applies to your child's examination session, and hand that to the tutor at the diagnostic session. A tutor who asks for it unprompted is the kind you want. A tutor who says the structure has not changed in years is telling you they have not looked.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the internal assessments that follow
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision with the longest tail, and most families make it in a single evening with a form to return by Friday. In the Diploma Programme a student picks one subject from each of five groups plus a sixth, and decides which three sit at Higher Level. Higher Level is not simply more of the same content. It adds breadth in some subjects, depth in others, and in Physics and Chemistry it adds an additional option material that an SL student never meets. Choosing HL Chemistry because a university page mentioned it, without checking whether your child enjoys quantitative problem work, is the single most common reason a DP1 student is in trouble by December.

Internal assessment is where a home tutor earns their place. Nearly every DP subject carries one: a Mathematics exploration, a Group 4 scientific investigation, a Language A written assignment, a History investigation, a Visual Arts comparative study. These are drafted, supervised and marked inside school, moderated outside it, and they are due in clusters. A good tutor does not write them. A good tutor sits with a vague idea at the shapeless stage, asks the four questions that turn it into a researchable question, and then stays out of the drafting so the work remains the student's own. MYP students meet a lighter version of the same discipline through criterion-referenced tasks and the personal project.

Parents here regularly ask whether one tutor can carry all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes Raheja Imperia families book in the evening. Honestly, no. One person can hold two or three related subjects well, often Mathematics with Physics, or Economics with Business Management, or two languages. Beyond that you are buying supervision rather than subject expertise. The sensible shape for a DP student under pressure is one strong subject specialist for the HL that is hurting, plus occasional sessions on whichever internal assessment is nearest. Spreading one tutor thinly across six subjects produces a child who feels supervised and still cannot do Paper 2.

What matters is that these campuses set the pressure points, and they do not fall where a parent expects. The hard months for a DP student are not May and June, when examinations are actually sat, but the stretch from late October through January when internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay interim deadline and mock examinations arrive on top of each other. A PYP child has no deadline pressure at all, which is exactly why hiring a tutor for one is so often the wrong call.

Use the school's own calendar as the planning document. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the right default for almost every family in this tower, and the reason is physical rather than pedagogical. A tutor sitting at your dining table can see the half-finished worksheet, the phone face-down beside the notebook and the fact that your child has copied a worked example without reading it. An IB home tutor in Raheja Imperia also removes the one variable you cannot control from a flat on a high floor: the child who has to leave the building, find a car and sit through signals for a class, and who therefore arrives already depleted. The lift does the commuting instead.

Online is a real option and sometimes the better one, so here is where it genuinely wins. It wins for scarce subjects, where the only person in the country who properly teaches DP Film or a Group 2 language at Higher Level is not in Mumbai at all. It wins for short, frequent check-ins during an internal assessment, where twenty minutes on a shared document beats a ninety-minute visit. It wins when a family travels, which happens often enough in this part of the island to matter. An IB online tutor in Raheja Imperia is not a downgrade for a self-managing DP2 student. For a Year 7 who cannot yet work alone for forty minutes, online is the wrong choice and we will say so before you pay for it.

Hybrid is what most families end up running by the second term, and it is worth designing on purpose rather than drifting into. The pattern that works: one home visit a week for the teaching, one shorter online session for the checking, and a hard rule that the online one is cancelled rather than converted into watching the student do homework in silence. The hybrid shape also absorbs the Worli evening problem, because the online slot can sit at 8:30pm when nobody wants to be on Annie Besant Road. Home tuition across this part of Mumbai works best when the travelling session is the one that carries the real teaching load.

sections.heading: How is an IB tutor in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor on the platform clears the same three gates before a parent sees their profile: identity and address verification against a government photographic document, evidence of the qualification they claim in the subject they want to teach, and a structured subject conversation with somebody who has taught that programme. The subject conversation is the one that removes people. A graduate who can solve the problems is not automatically somebody who can explain to an MYP student why their answer scored low against criterion C, and the conversation is built to find that out. References from previous families are checked by phone, not by reading a forwarded email.

What we cannot do from here is judge the fit with your child, which is why the diagnostic session exists and why it is paid rather than free. A free trial creates a performance; a paid first session creates a working lesson you can judge on its substance. Sit in the next room with the door open for the first one. You are listening for whether the tutor asks questions and waits, or talks and fills silence. An IB home tutor in Raheja Imperia who spends the first twenty minutes finding out what the student already knows is doing the job. One who opens the textbook at chapter one is not.

There are things you should verify yourself, and they are quick. Ask which examination session the tutor last prepared a student for in this specific subject, and listen for a specific answer rather than a general one. Ask them to describe one topic their students reliably get wrong and what they changed about how they teach it. Ask who they will contact if your child's school raises an academic honesty concern about an internal assessment draft, and expect the answer to be you and the school, in that order. Be wary of anybody who offers a guaranteed grade, publishes a success rate, or claims the best IB tutor in Raheja Imperia title. Those claims are unverifiable and the people making them know it.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks and at one term
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Four sessions is not enough to move a grade in any IB subject and anybody telling you otherwise is selling. What you should see by then is narrower and more useful: your child can describe what the tutor is working on in their own words, homework for that subject is being started without an argument, and the tutor has produced at least one concrete diagnosis rather than a general impression. A tutor who says the student is doing well after four weeks has not been paying attention. A tutor who says the student can rearrange equations but cannot read a question stem and decide what is being asked has.

At one term, marks become a fair measure, with one caveat. A student who was scoring poorly because of missing foundations often gets worse-looking marks before better ones, because the tutor has stopped them guessing and started them showing method. Look instead at the shape of the feedback from school. The comment moving from 'does not attempt the longer questions' to 'attempts the longer questions, loses marks on explanation' is substantial progress even when the number barely moves. By the end of one full examination cycle you should see both the marks and the independence shift, and if neither has, the honest answer is that this was the wrong tutor or the wrong intervention, not that your child needs more hours.

Here are the limits stated plainly, because they matter more than any promise. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, cannot guarantee a particular outcome in any subject, and will not quote you a success rate, because a success rate across a platform tells you nothing about your child. A tutor cannot fix a subject choice that was wrong from the start; the honest move there is to speak to the school about a change while a change is still possible. A tutor also cannot substitute for a student who will not do the work between sessions, and two hours a week against zero hours of independent study is the most common reason a term of good teaching produces nothing.

By the end you should have a short written note: what the gaps are, what the first month will target, and what the tutor needs from you, which is usually a quiet corner and a parent who does not sit in from session three onwards.

faqs.question: Is one tutor enough for all of my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and buying it that way is a common mistake. One tutor can carry two or three related subjects properly, typically Mathematics with Physics, Economics with Business Management, or two languages. Past that you are paying for supervision rather than subject expertise, and a Diploma Programme student can tell the difference within three sessions. The shape that works is one strong specialist for whichever Higher Level subject is actually hurting, plus shorter sessions targeted at the internal assessment that is nearest its deadline. If three separate subjects are failing at once, the problem is often workload management rather than three subject gaps.

faqs.question: Which IB programme does my child's school actually follow?
faqs.answer: Check with the school directly rather than assuming from the year group, because campuses in this part of Mumbai run different combinations. Some offer the Primary Years Programme and Middle Years Programme and then switch to a different pathway for the final two years. Others run the Diploma Programme but offer an alternative alongside it. Ask for the programme name in writing, the subject guide edition in use, and the examination session your child is entered for. Hand all three to the tutor at the diagnostic session. A tutor who asks for this unprompted has taught the programme recently, which is exactly the signal you want.

faqs.question: Where in the flat should the home tuition happen?
faqs.answer: The dining table, consistently, with the same chair and the same light every week. It sounds trivial and it is not: a fixed working place does most of the work of getting a reluctant student started, and the bedroom is where the phone lives. Keep the room semi-public for the first two or three sessions so you can hear the shape of the lesson without sitting in it. Avoid moving the session to the clubhouse study area early on, however pleasant it is, because you give up the ability to overhear and your child gains an audience. Once a rhythm is established, a quieter shared space works fine.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: You tell us, and we treat it as a matching failure rather than a student failure. First we ask what the tutor diagnosed in week one and whether that diagnosis was specific, because a vague opening assessment predicts a wasted month more reliably than anything else. Then we ask whether the work set between sessions was actually done. If the diagnosis was good and the work was done and nothing moved, the intervention was wrong and we change the subject focus or the session structure. If the fit is the problem, we re-match without making you restart the diagnostic process from the beginning.

faqs.question: Does online IB tutoring work as well as sitting at the dining table?
faqs.answer: For some students and some subjects, yes, and for others no, and the honest version matters. An IB online tutor in Raheja Imperia works well for a self-managing DP2 student, for short check-ins during an internal assessment draft, and for genuinely scarce subjects where the right specialist is not in Mumbai at all. It works badly for a Year 7 or Year 8 student who cannot yet sustain forty minutes of independent attention, because the screen removes the tutor's ability to see a wandering hand or a half-copied worked example. Most families in this building settle on a hybrid pattern by the second term.

faqs.question: Can you help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a clear boundary that protects your child. A tutor can help turn a broad interest into a researchable question, can teach the reading and note-taking discipline the Extended Essay (EE) demands, and can work on the argument structure Theory of Knowledge (TOK) rewards. A tutor does not write, edit line by line, or supply arguments, because the work has to be the student's own and schools run academic honesty checks for good reason. The most valuable sessions on both components happen early, at the question-choosing stage, and far fewer families book them then than should.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is simply not working out?
faqs.answer: Say so early and say so plainly, ideally at the four-week review rather than three months in. We ask for one specific example rather than a general feeling, because the example usually identifies whether this is a fit problem, a level problem or a scheduling problem, and each has a different fix. A re-match keeps the diagnosis already done, so the replacement starts from what the first tutor established rather than from nothing. Parents often delay this conversation out of politeness. The tutor would almost always rather know, and a term lost to the wrong fit cannot be recovered later.

faqs.question: Do you take on PYP children, or only MYP and DP?
faqs.answer: Both, with a caution we will give you before you book. For a Primary Years Programme child, a tutor is the right answer when there is a specific identified gap, such as reading fluency or number sense, and is often the wrong answer when a parent is simply anxious about an inquiry-based report they find hard to read. PYP has no examination pressure, and loading a seven-year-old with a second school day after the first one tends to produce resistance rather than progress. If that is the situation, we will say so. An IB private tutor Raheja Imperia parents book for a PYP child should have a named target and an end date.

faqs.answer: Saturday mornings are the easiest slot to fill in this building and the hardest to keep. They are easy because traffic from Bandra, Khar and Lower Parel is light and a tutor will happily take the run. They are hard because weekend plans erode them, and a slot cancelled twice stops being a slot. If you want the weekend, book it early in the morning rather than late, and treat it as fixed. sections.heading: Does one dominant school calendar change the tutoring year?
paragraphs: It does, in two specific ways. Demand becomes synchronised, so the slots you want are contested by your own neighbours at exactly the same moment, and the advice circulating in the complex is unusually reliable because everyone is working to the same deadlines. Families here are largely on the same assessment rhythm, which makes early booking more valuable and makes a late start more costly than it would be in a mixed building.

Within that single calendar the three programmes still behave differently. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs on units of inquiry with no external examination, and the aim of home tutoring at that stage is capability rather than marks: can she read a two-step word problem and work out what is being asked before she starts calculating? Can she explain a method aloud? Short, frequent sessions achieve this and long weekend blocks do not.

The MYP is where marks begin to feel opaque to families, because assessment moves to criteria with descriptor bands and a student is judged on how she documents and reports as much as on what she produces. An Arts process journal that records only finished pieces loses marks that a journal recording decisions and revisions would have earned. A tutor who reads the criterion strip aloud with the student in the first fortnight does more than one who teaches content for a month.

The DP is six subjects across Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and an IA in most subjects, and here the synchronised calendar bites hardest. When one school's DP cohort reaches the coursework convergence together, every competent specialist in South Mumbai is booked within a fortnight. An IB tutor Mumbai parents keep across both DP years is usually one engaged in the quiet opening weeks rather than in the scramble.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessments that follow each one
paragraphs: The requests we take at this address concentrate in Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, English A and Economics, with Geography and the Arts appearing regularly. The HL and SL decision drives most of them, and it is usually made in a week by a fifteen-year-old with incomplete information. A tutor's most valuable contribution in the first weeks of DP1 is often to read three weeks of the student's actual working and say plainly whether the level she has chosen is survivable for two years.

Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and the difference is shape rather than difficulty: one leans into proof and abstract structure, the other into modelling, data and interpretation. A student who enjoys building a model from messy real figures and dislikes algebraic proof has an obvious route, and choosing the other one because of its reputation is how two years of friction begins. The modelling task in the second route rewards a student who can justify assumptions, which is a writing skill as much as a mathematical one.

In the sciences the assessment that consumes most evenings is the individual investigation. A Physics investigation in particular lives on how uncertainty is handled: a student who reports a single value with no sense of its reliability has not done the thing being assessed, however neat the practical work. A tutor who has supervised investigations will spend the first session on the research question and the measurement plan, and almost none of it on content, which feels counterintuitive and is correct.

English A Language and Literature asks students to work with non-literary texts as well as literary ones, and the failure there is treating an advertisement or a speech as if it were a poem: describing features without connecting them to audience and purpose. Geography carries fieldwork, which rewards a question that can genuinely be investigated in the field rather than one that sounds impressive. We arrange all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Raheja Vivarea families ask for, and take component structure from the current IB subject guide or your coordinator rather than from any page on the internet.

It is the wrong choice for a student avoiding a subject rather than finding it hard, because avoidance needs a person at the table, and the wrong choice for a child who cannot yet work alone with the door closed.

Hybrid is where most DP families here end up, and the study room makes it stronger than usual: one longer visit for teaching and supervised timed writing in the quiet space, plus one short online slot for marking and questions. When the Haji Ali signals or the monsoon take out a weekday, the screen session keeps the week intact. faqs.answer: One. Three at once usually reflects worry rather than diagnosis, and it triples the cost while dividing the attention. Choose the subject she will carry at Higher Level, or the one where the marks sit furthest from her real ability. A large share of the time the underlying problem is organisation, note-taking and reading the question, and once a tutor repairs that inside one subject it transfers across the rest at no extra charge. faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For a PYP or early MYP child, usually yes; for a DP student, rarely. Younger children drift within ten minutes if no adult is in earshot, and the tutor should not be the only authority in the flat. An older student needs room to work badly and be corrected without an audience, which is another argument for the study room. What matters more than presence is reading the short written feedback weekly and acting when a pattern repeats. Tell us the arrangement before the first visit so the gate process is settled.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Start with the programme name printed on the report card, not the grade number, because Mumbai schools label year groups in their own way. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs to roughly Grade 5, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years up to Grade 10, and the Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years. A tutor who is strong in one of the three is not automatically useful in another, and that is the single most common mismatch we see.

In the PYP there are no external exams, which is exactly why parents underestimate it. The work is inquiry-led and the assessment is largely a teacher's judgement of how a child reasons, asks questions and presents what they found. A tutor here is working on reading stamina, number sense and the habit of explaining an answer out loud. The PYP exhibition in the final year is the first piece of work most of these children own end to end, and it is a fair test of whether the habits are in place.

The MYP is where families in this complex most often go looking for help. Marking moves to subject criteria labelled A through D, and the language of those criteria is unfamiliar to any parent who grew up with percentage marks. A child can write a good answer and still score poorly because the criterion asked for analysis and they gave description. Good MYP home classes across Mumbai spend their early weeks teaching the command words and the criterion wording before touching content at all. The personal project in the final MYP year rewards planning more than brilliance.

The DP is a two-year machine with its own calendar. Six subjects at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), an Internal Assessment (IA) in almost every one of them, plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity, service requirement. Nothing in that list is individually hard. The difficulty is that they arrive together, and a DP2 student who has not built a drafting habit in DP1 will feel it in January.

sections.heading: Choosing IB subjects and levels from a flat in Runwal Greens
paragraphs: The honest answer about all IB and IGCSE subjects a single tutor in Runwal Greens can cover is: not many, and you should be suspicious of anyone who claims otherwise. Subject choice and level choice are two separate decisions, and the second one is where families lose marks. Picking Higher Level (HL) in three subjects your child enjoys is sensible. Picking HL because a university website listed it, in a subject where last year's school report already showed strain, is how a DP1 November turns ugly.

Every IB subject carries its own internal assessment, and they are not interchangeable pieces of work. A Sciences IA is an individual investigation with a research question the student has to narrow down themselves, which is where most of them stall. A Mathematics exploration needs a genuine mathematical idea and not a survey with a bar chart. A Language A piece asks for close reading of a passage rather than a plot summary. History has its own investigation with a source evaluation built in. A tutor who has supervised the specific IA in the specific subject is worth far more than a general subject expert.

Level and tier questions do shift as a child moves up, and the Core or Extended tier decision belongs to the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel years rather than here. Inside the IB the equivalent conversation is HL against SL, and it is best had in the term before choices are locked, with the school's own subject report in front of you. We put a plan together for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Runwal Greens families ask about, then usually recommend fewer tutors than the parent expected and more weeks with each of them.

A single IB tutor Mumbai parents hire for a Grade 8 child can often hold two or three subjects, because at that stage the skills overlap: structuring a written response, reading a question properly, showing working. By DP1 that stops being true. Sciences, Mathematics and Language A each need somebody who has sat with that subject's assessment language recently, and spreading one tutor across all three usually produces three mediocre sets of sessions rather than one good one.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai areas do Runwal Greens tutors also cover?
paragraphs: A tutor who takes a weekly slot at Runwal Greens almost always also teaches in Kanjurmarg, Bhandup and Mulund West, because those four points sit on one road and one suburban line. The nearest stations are Kanjurmarg / Bhandup, both a few minutes down LBS Marg, and the Central Line (Kurla–Mulund) carries the tutors who do not drive. That clustering is the practical reason an IB home tutor in Runwal Greens can hold a 6pm Tuesday slot for a whole academic year without renegotiating it.

The wider picture matters when a subject is scarce. The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai is the odd one out: it is physically central but has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar. For a Runwal Greens family that is good news, because the Powai tutor pool is deep in IB subjects and the drive down JVLR and onto LBS Marg is one of the easier runs in this part of Mumbai, Maharashtra.

Further out, Metro Line 1 (Ghatkopar–Andheri) and the Santacruz–Chembur Link Road (SCLR) open up the Western Suburbs for a tutor who teaches a rare HL subject, but that is a Saturday arrangement rather than a weekday one. We are straightforwardly unenthusiastic about long cross-city matches for school-night slots. A tutor crossing the city twice in an evening will be tired before the session starts, and the first thing to go is the marking they promised to do between visits.

Mulund West is the other direction and the one that most affects scheduling. A tutor based there reaches the Runwal Greens gate quickly off-peak and slower once the Eastern Express Highway backs up, which is why 7pm and 7.30pm starts hold better than 6pm ones for that pool. Families who insist on the earliest slot in the evening often get a less experienced tutor, simply because the experienced ones have already filled it closer to home.

sections.heading: The school year Runwal Greens families live by, from June to the Mumbai exam season
paragraphs: Children in this complex are mostly bussed to a small set of schools, and NES International School in Mulund West and Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai set the rhythm for most of them. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with either school or with any society or builder named on this page. We name them because their calendars decide when your evenings get difficult, which is the only reason a tutoring page should mention a school at all.

The academic year opens in June and the first six weeks are deceptively quiet. By late August and September the MYP criteria tasks start landing and DP1 students are being asked to think about IA topics they have no feel for yet. October and November are the first real pressure point. Mock assessments, the first graded MYP tasks and DP1 IA proposals collide, and this is the month in which most of the home tuition across this part of Mumbai actually gets arranged, which is also the month in which the good tutors run out of weekday slots.

January and February are the hardest stretch for a DP2 family. Final IA submissions, the Extended Essay (EE) deadline and the TOK essay sit within weeks of each other while the school is also running its own mocks. A DP2 student in Runwal Greens sitting the May session can have a Physics IA final draft due in the same fortnight as a TOK essay and a Maths exploration, and no amount of tutoring fixes that if the work started in January rather than October. March and April go quiet for everyone except the exam cohort, for whom they are the only thing that matters.

The PYP calendar runs differently and is easy to forget. The exhibition falls in the second half of the year and is the first long piece of independent work these children do. A tutor helping with it should be organising the child's process, not the content. If a parent cannot describe what their Grade 5 child actually did on the exhibition, somebody has done too much of it for them.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or both for an IB student in Runwal Greens?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the right default for most IB students in this complex, and it is what the large majority of families here ask for. Most families who approach us for an IB home tutor in Runwal Greens want a person at the table because a child who will not open a book alone will not open one on a video call either. A tutor in the room sees the page the student is avoiding, the phone face-down under the notebook, and the question they pretended to understand. None of that survives a screen.

Online genuinely wins in two situations and it is worth being clear about both. The first is a scarce subject: if your DP2 child needs HL Economics or a less common Language B, the person who has supervised that exact IA may not live anywhere near the Central Suburbs, and an IB online tutor in Runwal Greens who knows the subject beats a nearby generalist who does not. The second is the exam run-in, when a short extra session on a Thursday night is worth more than nothing at all and nobody wants to add a round trip to it.

Online is the wrong choice for a Grade 8 or Grade 9 student who cannot yet work without someone next to them. That is not a technology problem and a better platform will not fix it. We would rather tell a parent that and lose the booking than take it and watch the sessions quietly become homework supervision over a bad connection. The same applies to a PYP child, where almost all of the value is in the physical back-and-forth of being read to and corrected.

The arrangement that works best over a full year is usually mixed. One home session a week as the anchor, a second shorter online session in the fortnight before a deadline, and a clear rule about which one gets cancelled when the school timetable moves. Hybrid also solves the monsoon, when a weekday evening on LBS Marg can go badly wrong and both sides would rather move the session than lose it.

sections.heading: How a tutor is checked before they ever reach your gate
paragraphs: Before an IB home teacher in Runwal Greens is proposed to a family, we check three things that matter and ignore several that do not. Identity and address come first, then the specific programme and subject claim, then references from families they have actually taught in Mumbai. A Physics postgraduate who has never taught a DP student is not a DP Physics tutor, and we treat the claim and the qualification as separate items. We check the claim by asking them to talk through a recent IA they supervised and what feedback they gave on its second draft.

There is a limit to what any platform can verify, and a parent who knows the limit makes a better decision. We cannot tell you how a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old will get on. We cannot verify a result a tutor says a former student achieved, because we were not in that room and neither were you. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anyone who does is either unaware of how the assessment works or hoping you are.

So there are checks you should run yourself, and the trial session is where you run them. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or a fixed score improvement. Ask for the current subject guide reference for whatever they say they will cover. Ask what they will send you after each session, then see whether it arrives after the first one. Ask what happens if your child misses a week in the exam term. The answers to those four questions tell you more than any certificate.

The last check is about your building rather than the tutor. Confirm that the person coming to your flat has given the gate desk the same name and number you have, and that the arrangement is a standing entry rather than a fresh approval every Tuesday. A tutor who is turned away or kept waiting at the gate twice will quietly stop prioritising your slot, and nobody will tell you that is what happened.

sections.heading: The twelve-year view: why IB home classes in Runwal Greens are a long relationship
paragraphs: Runwal Greens is one gated complex of towers on LBS Marg, not a suburb, and that single fact changes how tutoring works here more than anything else on this page. There is one main gate, one visitor protocol, one clubhouse and a set of common study areas, and the children are bussed out to a handful of schools rather than spread across twenty. A tutor who is already inside the complex on a Wednesday for a family in another wing is a materially better bet than one who would be making a dedicated trip, and the gate log is the reason we can tell.

The note worth building a decision around is the position: Runwal Greens sits between Bhandup and Mulund, comfortably inside the travel radius of the tutor pool that works around NES International School. In practice that means the constraint most Mumbai parents hit, which is finding someone who will reliably show up on a school night, is softer here than it is for families in Powai or across the harbour. The constraint that replaces it is competition inside the complex. The same small pool is visible to every family in these towers, so good tutors fill their weekday evenings early and the booking you make in October is the one you keep.

This is why we treat the request as a long relationship rather than a transaction. A child who starts with a tutor in MYP Grade 8 and keeps them into DP1 saves an entire term of diagnosis, and a single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai schools teach does not exist, but a tutor who knows your child's handwriting, their avoidance patterns and their family's schedule is worth more than a marginally better subject specialist every September.

On cost, we do not publish a price list because there is no honest single number. IB tuition fees in Runwal Greens depend on the programme, the level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. A DP2 HL subject with an IA deadline in six weeks costs more per hour than MYP Maths support, because the pool of people who can do it is smaller. An IB private tutor Runwal Greens parents find through a neighbour may quote less and may also be a school teacher with no capacity to mark between sessions. Compare what is included, not just the hourly figure.

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking for better marks and you should not expect them. You are looking for three concrete things: your child knows what the next piece of assessed work is, they can say what the criterion or command word is asking for in their own words, and they are starting work without being chased into it. If none of those has shifted after four sessions, the match is wrong and you should say so rather than wait for a term to prove it.

At one term the marks should start to move, but unevenly and not in every subject. A student who was writing description where the criterion asked for analysis usually gains fastest, because that is a correctable habit. Content gaps take longer, especially in Mathematics, where a DP1 weakness often traces back to something left unfixed in MYP. A good tutor will tell you which of the two you are dealing with by the end of the first month. IB home tuition in Runwal Greens is not a way of buying marks; it is a way of buying attention that a class of twenty-four cannot give.

Across a full exam cycle the honest picture is that tutoring reliably improves preparation, drafting discipline and the quality of internal assessment work, and it influences the final result without controlling it. Examiners mark what is on the page in May. We do not guarantee grades and we will not quote a success rate, because any number we published would be unverifiable and you would be right to ignore it.

There are students for whom the answer is no tutor at all. A Grade 9 child doing well who is simply tired does not need another weekday commitment. A DP2 student failing three subjects in February needs the school's coordinator and a conversation about the diploma, not a fourth tutor. We would rather tell you that in the first call than take a booking we expect to end in April.
