sections.heading: Getting started in Seven Bungalows: what to have ready for home classes
paragraphs: Send four things and you will get a usable shortlist the same day: the year group and programme, the subjects that are slipping, the two or three evening slots you can actually protect, and one sentence about what triggered the search. That last sentence does more work than the rest. A mock result, a teacher's comment, a missed IA deadline and a child who has gone quiet all need different tutors. A single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hope exists rarely does at Higher Level, so tell us which two subjects matter most.

Before the first session, put three documents in one place. The last two pieces of marked work, with the teacher's comments still on them. The school's internal deadline list for the term. The current subject guide if the school has shared it. A tutor who can read those in the first ten minutes skips a fortnight of diagnosis. Also sort the room: a table, a chair at the right height and a lamp beat a sofa, and the dining table with the television off beats a bedroom where a sibling is practising piano.

The first home tuition session is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to work through a piece of recent marked work, ask the student to attempt something unseen, find the exact point where understanding stops, and leave with a plan for the next three sessions rather than a package. You should hear what the plan is before the tutor leaves the building, and so should your child.

Your job in the first month is light but not optional. Be at home for the first session or two, then step back. Protect the slot against everything except illness. Read the tutor's session notes rather than asking the child how it went, because an eleven-year-old will say fine about anything. And answer the two-week question honestly, which is the one thing that lets us fix a mediocre match before it costs a term.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Seven Bungalows for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the easier parts of the Western Suburbs to staff at that hour. faqs.answer: Not usually, and that is a real advantage here. faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Seven Bungalows depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on the level, the subject, the hour and the distance, and anyone who quotes a single number before asking about those four is guessing. Higher Level work with internal assessment supervision takes more preparation than Standard Level revision, so it costs more. A scarce subject has fewer tutors in Mumbai and prices accordingly. faqs.question: How soon can IB home tuition in Seven Bungalows actually start?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week, and sometimes within two or three days outside exam season. The shortlist typically reaches you within a day of your message, the call or meeting with your preferred tutor happens next, and the first session goes in as soon as you both have the same free evening. The bottleneck is almost never our side. It is the 7pm weekday slot, which is the most contested hour in the Western Suburbs. If you can take 5pm, half past five or a weekend morning, you will get a wider choice of tutors and start sooner.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for a Higher Level DP subject?
faqs.answer: For a strong, self-managing student, yes, and for a scarce subject it is often better than the local alternative. Screen sharing a worked solution, annotating a draft live and recording a session for revision all work well now. Where online struggles is with a student who drifts without a person in the room, or who needs the informal five minutes after the hour when the real question finally surfaces. The pattern most Seven Bungalows families settle on is weekly home tuition with the subject tutor plus a short online checkpoint before a deadline.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Tell us immediately, and be specific about what has not moved. Four weeks is enough to see behaviour change even when marks have not: homework started without an argument, shorter stalls, a draft that exists. If none of that has happened, the match is wrong and persisting costs you a term. Describe it concretely, because the fix differs. A pace problem is often solved by the same tutor changing approach and being told to slow down. A relationship problem is not. We re-match from the same local shortlist and your subject brief carries over.

faqs.question: The tutor is good but my child does not like them. Can we change?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should, without feeling that you need to justify it academically. A tutor your child will not talk to cannot find out where understanding stops, which is most of the job. We ask what specifically does not work, because the useful signal is in the detail: too fast, too formal, talks over her, makes her feel stupid when she asks twice. That tells us what to match for next. Changing tutor once early in a term is normal and costs you a week. Changing in April is much more expensive, which is why the two-week check exists.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one subject for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking for. A single tutor can often hold two related subjects at MYP level, or a science plus Mathematics at Standard Level, and that keeps your week simpler and your scheduling easier. At Higher Level the answer is usually no. The depth and the internal assessment demands of an HL subject mean you want somebody who teaches that syllabus regularly rather than somebody competent across four. We would rather tell you that two specialists are needed than sell you the convenient answer.

faqs.question: Do you cover Versova, Four Bungalows and Andheri West as well?

The Seven Bungalows–Versova corridor is a single working area for a tutor: Versova sits at the end of Metro Line 1, Four Bungalows is minutes away, and Andheri West is the largest source of tutors in this part of Mumbai. We name them because they are the schools Seven Bungalows families actually attend, and their calendars decide when your evenings get difficult. sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: which rung is your child actually on?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three programmes bolted into one ladder, and families in Sewri routinely ask for help on the wrong rung. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years and sets no external examinations. What it does carry is a transdisciplinary structure and a reporting style that reads strangely to a parent who grew up with marks out of a hundred. Support at this stage is about reading comprehension, number sense and written explanation, not revision.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and is assessed against published criteria for each subject rather than a single percentage. A child can be strong on one criterion and weak on another inside the same subject, which is why a good home tutor in Sewri asks to see the criterion-level feedback before deciding what to teach. The personal project lands near the end of the programme and needs planning and scheduling help far more than it needs subject coaching.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two years that shape university applications. Each subject is taken at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), and the difference is not simply more chapters: HL adds depth and a different style of question. Your school's DP coordinator holds the current subject combinations and the internal deadlines, and the official subject guide for each course is where the assessment structure actually lives. Those guides are revised on the IB's cycle, not ours, so read this year's.

Families get hurt at the transition. A child moving from MYP into DP1 at JBCN International School, Parel, or at any of Mumbai's island-city schools, meets a step change in writing expectation inside the first term, and the report that reflects it arrives in October or November. IB home tuition in Sewri booked in that window is remedial work on a deadline. Booked in the term before, the same tutor is doing preparation, and it costs the family fewer weeks of panic.
bullets: PYP: reading, number sense and explanation; nothing external to revise for.
MYP: criterion-level feedback tells you what to teach, not just the grade.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessment each subject carries
paragraphs: Subject choice is where island-city families spend the least time and lose the most ground. A child who picks a Higher Level subject because a friend did, or drops one because of a single bad test, is making a two-year decision in an afternoon. Our listing covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and a tutor in Sewri is matched per subject, not per child, so a DP2 student can run Chemistry with one tutor and Mathematics with another without either pretending to cover both.

Every DP subject carries an internally assessed component, and each one fails differently. A science IA is an individual investigation the student designs, so the risk is a research question too broad to answer in the pages available. A Mathematics exploration is a written piece on a chosen topic, where the risk is picking something with no mathematics in it. Language A courses carry written tasks and an oral; Economics and Business carry commentaries or a research project. Ask the teacher for this year's criteria sheet.

Then there is the core. The Extended Essay (EE) is an independent research piece supervised inside the school, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) carries an exhibition and an essay. Neither is a timetabled subject, so neither competes for attention the way Chemistry does, and both go wrong quietly. A DP1 student in Sewri who has not settled an EE topic by the end of the monsoon term has failed nothing yet, but she has spent the easiest planning window she will get.

Scarcity is real and it is subject-shaped. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English have a deep pool across South Mumbai. A second language at Higher Level, Computer Science, Psychology or Visual Arts narrows that pool sharply, and that is the case where IB home classes in Sewri sensibly become hybrid: a local tutor for the weekly table session and a specialist online for the assessed work. Pretending a generalist covers Visual Arts produces a pleasant match and a poor portfolio.

Sewri is now the island-city end of the Atal Setu, so Navi Mumbai sits a bridge away instead of a creek away, and a tutor in Vashi or Nerul can reach Sewri for a Saturday morning session in a way that was not practical before. sections.heading: The school calendar Sewri families actually live by
paragraphs: Children on this corridor are bussed, driven or taken by train to international schools across the island city. JBCN International School, Parel is the nearest IB and IGCSE campus for much of Sewri, and Bombay International School draws families from the western half of South Mumbai. Both run a calendar that has nothing to do with the state board year, and that calendar sets your tuition timetable whether or not anyone planned for it.

The year opens in June with the monsoon term and the first assessments that count land in August. October and November are the hardest fortnight in a DP student's year: school internal examinations, IA drafts and the TOK essay converge, and a Mumbai school layers its own mock timetable on top of all three. January and February belong to final IA submissions and mocks. By May, when external examinations run, tuition is triage and not teaching, and good tutors say so in October.

School-set deadlines sit earlier than the official ones, deliberately, because a coordinator needs time to check and upload work. A parent working backwards from a published date is already a fortnight late. Ask the examinations officer or the DP coordinator for the internal deadline sheet in June, and hand a copy to your home tutor in the first session. A tutor holding that sheet plans a term; a tutor without it reacts week to week and charges you for the difference.

The second calendar nobody mentions is travel. School buses on this corridor return later as the term wears on, through Parel and Wadala evening traffic, so a 6pm start that looked comfortable in June is a 6.40pm scramble by August. Build the slot at 7pm and keep it there. IB Gram has no affiliation with JBCN International School, Parel, Bombay International School or any other school named here; they appear because this is the calendar your family lives by.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix: what works in Sewri at 7pm?
paragraphs: Home tuition wins on a weekday evening here, and online wins for a scarce subject or an exam-season intensive. An IB home tutor in Sewri gets a child already at the table, a phone that can be left in another room, and a parent close enough to hear whether anything is happening. At 7pm on a Tuesday that is worth a great deal, because the alternative is a tired fifteen-year-old negotiating with a screen.

Building access is the part that actually breaks schedules. This corridor mixes older low-rise blocks with newer redevelopment towers, and the two behave differently at the gate: the older buildings need a word with the watchman and nothing more, while the newer towers want the tutor's name left at the building office so a standing weekly entry is pre-approved instead of argued each week. Do that once in week one. A tutor held eleven minutes at the gate loses a quarter of the session.

Where the lesson happens matters more than parents expect. A dining table with the television off beats a bedroom desk behind a closed door, especially for MYP work where the tutor needs to see rough working as it happens. A DP Physics or Chemistry session wants a flat surface, a plug point and nobody walking through. If the flat genuinely has no quiet corner at that hour, say so on the call and we will match an online specialist rather than send someone into a room where work cannot happen.

Hybrid is what most DP families on this corridor settle into by the second term: one home visit a week for teaching, one short online session for draft feedback, where sharing a screen beats reading over a shoulder. An IB online tutor in Sewri also answers the monsoon problem, because the week the roads flood is the week a standing slot is lost. Online is weaker for a child who drifts without an adult in the room, and for anything with hand-drawn working.

sections.heading: How are IB tutors in Mumbai checked before they reach your door?
paragraphs: Every tutor submits identity proof, degree documents and a teaching history we check by reference before any profile reaches a parent in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Before an IB home tutor in Sewri is put in front of you we also confirm the narrow thing you are hiring for: not that the person teaches science, but that they have taught this subject at this level recently and have seen IA work that a school has already marked and commented on.

Three separate things are verified and they are often confused. Identity, so you know who is entering your flat. Qualification, so the degree is real and in the subject claimed. Recent teaching, because a syllabus revision leaves a tutor who last taught the course four years ago subtly out of date in ways a parent cannot spot. We also record which boards each tutor works across, since many Mumbai tutors teach both IB and IGCSE, and we note where they are strongest.

Your own checks matter more than ours and they take one phone call. Ask which year groups the tutor taught last term. Ask to see a piece of written feedback they gave on a student's draft with the name removed. Ask how they would handle a criterion-level comment the family does not understand. Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, or who answers a syllabus question confidently without once referring to the current subject guide.

What verification cannot do is predict whether a tutor and a fifteen-year-old will work together. We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor does either. What we can do is keep the first two sessions low-risk and the swap fast. An IB private tutor Sewri parents hire through this platform is replaceable without an argument or a penalty, and that matters more than any rating, because the usual failure is not incompetence but mismatch.

sections.heading: The Atal Setu changed who counts as a local tutor in Sewri
paragraphs: Sewri is now the island-city end of the Atal Setu, and that one piece of concrete has quietly changed the matching maths for families here. For two decades the Sewri tutor pool was the island and nothing else: Wadala, Mazgaon, Parel, Dadar, Worli. Navi Mumbai was a creek and an hour away and never entered the conversation. The bridge lands on your side of the water, so a tutor in Vashi, Nerul or Belapur is now a bridge run rather than an expedition.

It does not change your Tuesday. A weekday 7pm slot still needs someone who can be at the building by 6.55pm after their own working day, and no bridge makes a 6pm departure from Belapur reliable in the evening peak. What it changes is the weekend and the scarce subject. A Saturday morning double session with a specialist who lives in Navi Mumbai is now a sane arrangement, and so is a fortnightly in-person review of an IA with a tutor who is otherwise online.

Take a DP1 student in Sewri sitting Economics at Higher Level, with an IA commentary due in the same fortnight as her school internal examinations. The deep Economics HL pool in South Mumbai is small and fully booked by October. Before the bridge, her realistic options were an online specialist she had never met or a nearby generalist. Now the shortlist can hold a Navi Mumbai tutor for two consecutive Saturdays while the Wednesday slot stays with a tutor from Parel. Two tutors by design, not a failed match.

Use the bridge deliberately and it buys specialists. Use it carelessly and it buys cancellations, because a tutor who agreed to cross for a weekday evening starts arriving late in week three and apologetic in week five. When we shortlist across the Atal Setu we say so on the profile, we put that slot on a weekend, and we name which tutor is the local anchor. Families who treat the bridge as a weekend widening of the pool keep their tutors for a full year.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look at whether your child can explain what the tutor did last week without being prompted, whether homework is attempted before the session instead of during it, and whether the tutor has told you something about your child's work you did not already know. If all three are missing after four sessions, the match is wrong and waiting another month will not repair it.

One term in, the evidence sits in the written work. A science IA draft with a defensible method. A Mathematics exploration with a question narrow enough to answer properly. An essay that answers the question asked rather than the one the child wanted. School report comments are a lagging indicator: an October report describes work done in August. Ask the tutor in week eight what they expect that report to say, because a tutor who guesses wrong is not reading the work closely enough.

Across a full cycle the honest picture is that tutoring changes the rate of improvement and the quality of what gets submitted, while results depend on a dozen things no tutor controls: sleep, the school's own teaching, which question comes up, moderation. We do not guarantee grades and we will not publish a success rate. Anyone offering either is telling you about their marketing rather than their teaching, and in Mumbai that pitch is common enough to be worth recognising.

IB tuition fees in Sewri depend on a short list of things, none of which is a published price. Board and level, because Higher Level DP work is scarcer to supply than MYP support. Subject scarcity, because a second language or Computer Science specialist has fewer alternatives. Travel distance and time of day, since a 7pm island slot costs a tutor more of their evening than a 4pm one. And session length and frequency, which is the one lever entirely in your hands.

sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition in Sewri this month
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful and all three take ten minutes to find. The last school report, including the comments nobody reads. One recent piece of marked work, ideally with the teacher's annotations still on it. And the school's internal deadline sheet for the term, which the examinations officer or the DP coordinator holds. A tutor who walks in with those three has a plan by the end of the first hour instead of the end of the first month.

Decide the slot before you decide the tutor. Pick the two evenings you can genuinely protect for a whole term, including the fortnight when a school production or a football season eats one of them. A standing 7pm Tuesday that survives October is worth more than a flexible arrangement that quietly dies in August. Tell us both evenings and we shortlist against them, rather than asking a family in Sewri to bend around a tutor's existing calendar.

The first session is a diagnostic. The tutor reads the report, looks at the marked work, sets one short piece to see how your child writes with no pressure on it, and then tells you in front of you what the gap is and what the first month will cover. You should hear something specific: a criterion, a paper-style question, a method half-learned and never corrected. If you hear general reassurance instead, ask the question again.

After that, ask for a line a week. Not a report, a line: what we did, what is set, what I am watching. Parents who get that line stay on top of a DP year without hovering over it. If the line stops arriving, the engagement has gone quiet, and that is your early warning rather than the next report. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families find through us is expected to send it.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP, not DP. Is a tutor premature?
faqs.answer: No, but the work is different and you should expect different output. MYP support is about criterion-level weakness: a child who can do the science but cannot write the evaluation, or who reads well and plans badly. A tutor should be reading your child's criterion feedback and teaching to the weak strand, not running ahead into DP content. Starting in MYP also means the transition into DP1 arrives with the writing habits already in place, which is where island-city families most often find the gap too wide to close in one term.

faqs.question: How soon can IB home tuition in Sewri start after I enquire?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week, sometimes within two or three days outside the October and January crunch. The shortlist takes a day or so to build, you need an evening to make the calls, and the tutor needs one clear slot in their week that matches one of your protected evenings. The slow cases are scarce subjects and peak season: a Higher Level Economics or second-language specialist in October may genuinely have nothing free until a weekend, and we would rather tell you that than fill the slot with the wrong person.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we re-match, usually inside a week. You do not owe anyone an explanation, though a sentence about what went wrong makes the next match better: wrong level, wrong pace, too much talking, no written feedback. A month is actually late for this call. By session two you already know whether your child answers questions or waits them out, and the swap is cheapest then. There are no packages to unwind and nothing to argue about, because a mismatch is a normal outcome rather than a failure.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for an IB student?
faqs.answer: It works well for some things and badly for others. Online is strong for IA and essay drafts, where a shared screen beats reading over a shoulder, and for scarce subjects where the right specialist does not live in South Mumbai. It is weak for a child who drifts the moment nobody is in the room, and for subjects with heavy hand-drawn working, where the tutor needs to watch the pen move. Most DP families on this corridor end up hybrid: one session at home each week and one online for feedback.

faqs.answer: For a weekend session, yes, and that is new. Sewri sits at the island-city end of the Atal Setu, so Vashi, Nerul and Belapur are now a bridge run rather than an hour around the creek. For a Saturday morning double session with a scarce-subject specialist it holds up well. For a weekday 7pm slot we still match inside the island, because a tutor leaving Navi Mumbai at 6pm in the evening peak will be late often enough to cost you the slot by the third week.

faqs.question: Who should help with the Extended Essay and TOK, the school or a tutor?
faqs.answer: The school owns both, and it should stay that way. Your child has an EE supervisor inside the school and a TOK teacher, and their guidance is the one that counts at submission. A tutor's useful role is scheduling and structure: holding the student to a topic decision early, reading a draft for argument rather than content, and asking the awkward question about whether the research question can be answered in the length allowed. A tutor who starts rewriting an EE is creating an academic honesty problem, not solving a writing one.

sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three separate programmes, and a tutor who is strong in one is often the wrong choice for another. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers the early and primary years through transdisciplinary units of inquiry. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years across eight subject groups, assessed against published criteria rather than a single percentage. The Diploma Programme (DP) covers the final two years, with each subject taken at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL). Ask which one your child is in before you ask anything else, because the answer changes who you should be hiring.

PYP support looks nothing like exam coaching, and a parent in Sion who books a DP specialist for a Grade 3 child usually regrets it by week three. PYP work is driven by inquiry and by the learner's own questions, so the useful tutor here builds reading stamina, number sense, written expression and the habit of explaining thinking out loud. The pressure point is rarely content. It is a child who understands the idea but cannot get it onto paper in a form a teacher can assess, or a child who has fallen behind in reading fluency and is quietly compensating. A PYP home tutor in Mumbai who works through the child's own unit documents, rather than importing a worksheet pack, is doing the job properly.

MYP sits in the middle and is where most confusion lives, partly because the marking looks unfamiliar to parents who grew up with percentages. Each subject group carries its own criteria, and a student can know the content well while losing marks on the criterion that asks them to communicate or to reflect. Year 5 adds the personal project, which eats time in a way families underestimate. A sibling page on this site goes deep on MYP specifically, so the short version here is this: if your child is in MYP, hire someone who has actually marked against criteria and can show you where the marks are going, not someone who only knows the final two years.

DP is the one parents usually mean when they search for an IB home tutor in Sion, and it is the most demanding to staff. Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus the core: the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity, service requirement. Each subject also carries Internal Assessment (IA) work that is drafted, fed back on and finalised to the school's own internal timetable, which is always earlier than the external one. The students who struggle are usually not the weak ones. They are the capable ones running four deadlines in a fortnight with no system for sequencing them, and that is a solvable problem.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Higher Level and Standard Level, and the assessments attached to each
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision that quietly sets up the next two years, and it is usually made in a fortnight with a form to return. The IB asks a DP student to pick one subject from each of several groups, then to take three of them at Higher Level. Higher Level is not simply more of the same content delivered faster. It adds topics, it raises the analytical demand of the questions, and in the sciences it adds depth to the practical and Internal Assessment work. A student who is comfortable at Standard Level in a subject is not automatically comfortable at Higher Level in it, and the honest version of that conversation is better had in the choosing fortnight than in the second term of DP1.

The internal assessments are where families most often ask for help, and they are different animals in different groups. A Mathematics exploration asks a student to pose their own question and sustain mathematical reasoning across it, which rewards the student who picks a tractable topic early and punishes the one who picks something glamorous in week ten. A science Internal Assessment lives or dies on the quality of the research question and whether the method actually isolates the variable being tested. A Language A written task asks for a reading of a text that is genuinely the student's own. A tutor who treats all of these as "the IA" and applies one template to them is not a subject specialist, whatever the profile says.

There is a second kind of request that comes in from Sion families, and it deserves naming. Plenty of households here are running two boards at once, because an older sibling is in DP while a younger one is somewhere in a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel pathway. Those parents want one point of contact who understands all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Sion might be asked to cover, even though each child needs a different specialist. That is a scheduling and coordination request as much as an academic one, and it is worth saying out loud in the brief so we can match slots that do not collide at the same dining table.

Do not take assessment structure from any page on the internet, including this one. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, so the number of papers, the shape of a component and what an Internal Assessment is required to contain can all change between the year a page is written and the year your child sits the exam. Get the current structure from your school's Diploma Programme coordinator or the live subject guide, and use a tutor to work out what your particular child is losing marks on. That second question is the one a page cannot answer and a specialist can, within about two sessions of reading real work.

paragraphs: Sion is a junction address, and that single fact drives almost everything about how home tuition in this part of Mumbai is arranged. Sion station is on the Central Line, Wadala sits on the Harbour Line and the monorail just to the south, Matunga is a short hop north, and Kurla is the next major interchange going up the Central Line. Add the SCLR running east toward Chembur and the Eastern Freeway dropping south into the island city, and a flat near the Sion–Dharavi junction is reachable from a genuinely wide arc. For a parent, the practical consequence is that you should not accept the standard island-city answer of "no tutor will come for that subject" without testing it.

Compare that with the rest of South Mumbai, which is where this locality is administratively grouped. South Mumbai is dense and short in distance but slow in practice: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers about eight kilometres and can still lose a large part of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals during the evening peak. Tutors on the island are therefore usually matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, and families in Napean Sea Road or Cuffe Parade live with a narrower pool as a result. Sion escapes a good part of that penalty because its roads run outward rather than through the most congested north-south pinch points.

The areas around Sion each behave slightly differently when you are actually scheduling. Matunga tutors are the easiest to hold for an early evening slot, because the trip is short enough that a 6pm start is realistic even on a weekday. Wadala has become a genuinely useful source of tutors since the Eastern Freeway opened, and a Wadala-based specialist can often take a Sion slot and a second slot further south on the same evening. Kurla works in the other direction, as the point where the Central and Harbour lines meet and where tutors travelling in from Chembur, Ghatkopar or Powai pass through anyway. An IB home tutor in Sion drawn from any of these three is arriving across a short, predictable route rather than a long gamble.

Two scheduling rules follow from the geography, and both save families from the mid-term collapse that ends a lot of arrangements. First, fix the slot and keep it, because a tutor who builds their evening route around a standing Tuesday in Sion will protect it, while a tutor asked to float across different evenings each week will eventually drop you for someone who did not. Second, prefer an earlier evening start if your child can take it. The arc from roughly half past six to half past eight is when every road in this part of Mumbai is at its worst, and a 5.45pm or a 8.30pm start quietly removes the single most common reason a tutor turns up late and tired.

Others travel further, to Parel, to Chembur, to Bandra Kurla Complex, which is exactly why the commute-friendly geography of this junction matters twice over: once for the child's school run and once for the tutor's evening route. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, and we name them only because the calendar they run is the calendar your tutor has to work around.

That calendar has shape, and the shape repeats. The June and July window after a new academic year opens is the quietest and the most valuable: nothing is urgent, so a tutor can spend four weeks on foundations without fighting a deadline. August through October is when Internal Assessment drafting lands for the senior years, and when MYP criterion-based tasks start arriving in clusters. The late-year window, roughly November into the winter break, is report and mock territory, and it is when most parents in Mumbai first start searching for a tutor. January to March is the hardest stretch for a DP2 student, with final Internal Assessment submissions, Extended Essay deadlines and mock examinations overlapping with revision that nobody has had time to start.

Here is what that looks like for one family rather than in the abstract. A DP2 student living near Sion station, sitting the May examination session, can easily have a Physics Internal Assessment final draft due in the same fortnight as her Theory of Knowledge essay, with a Mathematics exploration already overdue and mock examinations starting the week after. None of those four things is individually unreasonable. Together they are a sequencing problem, and the tutor who helps most in that fortnight is not the one who teaches new content but the one who sits down with a calendar, decides what gets a full effort and what gets a competent one, and protects the sleep that makes the rest possible.

The planning lesson from all of this is unglamorous: hire early in the year, not in the fortnight after the report. Parents who arrange IB home tuition in Sion in June or July get the pick of the tutors who live close enough to hold the slot, and they get the diagnostic work done while there is room for it. Parents who start in late November are competing with every other family in Mumbai who just read the same report, and are asking a tutor to fix a term's worth of gaps during the exact weeks when every deadline is already live. The content is the same either way. The amount of calm available is not.

sections.heading: Should you book home tuition in Sion or go online?
paragraphs: Book home tuition first and treat online as the deliberate exception. A tutor in the room reads the things a camera cannot: the pause before an answer, the page the student skips, the notebook that has no working in it, the fact that the study table is in the middle of the living room with a television on. For a student in PYP or the earlier MYP years this is not a preference, it is close to a requirement, because attention management is half of the work and no screen does that well. For most families in Sion the geography supports it, so an IB home tutor in Sion is usually a realistic first ask rather than a compromise.

Online earns its place in three specific situations, and it is genuinely better in all three. The first is a scarce subject: if your child needs Higher Level Economics or a less commonly taught second language, the right specialist may simply not live within reach of the island city, and an IB online tutor in Sion who is excellent beats a nearby generalist who is not. The second is the fortnight before an examination, when a student needs three short sessions a week rather than two long ones and travel time becomes the limiting factor. The third is the monsoon, which does more damage to standing arrangements across Mumbai than any other single cause.

Hybrid is what most of our longer arrangements settle into after a term, and it is worth designing on purpose rather than drifting into. The usual pattern is one in-person session a week for the work that needs a tutor physically present, which in practice means marking written work together, setting up practical or exploration design, and anything where the student needs to be watched while they attempt it. A second, shorter online session mid-week handles question-setting, doubt clearing and checking that the agreed task was actually done. The second session is the one that stops the week from quietly resetting, and because it is short and travel-free it survives a late evening or a rescheduled work commitment.

The honest trade-offs are worth stating plainly, because a page that claims all three modes are equally good is not helping you choose. Home sessions cost more per hour in effect, because you are paying for a tutor's travel time whether it appears on the invoice or not, and they are the first thing to break when the roads do. Online sessions need a parent to care about the setup: a door that closes, a device that is not the child's phone, and a tutor who makes the student share their written work on camera rather than reading answers out. Hybrid is the most robust and the most administratively annoying. Pick for your child and your week, not for the mode that sounds most serious.

sections.heading: How are tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every profile that reaches you has been through the same three checks, and the order matters. Identity comes first, because nothing else is worth doing until we know who we are dealing with: government photo identification, a working phone number and an address we have actually seen. Qualifications come second, verified against the documents rather than the claim, with specific attention to whether the subject and level on the profile match the subject and level in the teaching history. Teaching history comes third, and it is the one we spend the longest on. A tutor who says they teach IB is not the same as a tutor who has taught Higher Level Biology through two full examination cycles and can describe what the Internal Assessment feedback loop looked like.

What we cannot do is test for the thing you actually want, which is whether this specific adult will work with your specific child. No verification process predicts that. This is why the discovery call exists and why we ask you to treat it as a real interview rather than a formality. Ask the tutor which programme and level they taught most recently and in which year. Ask how they would spend session one with your child. Ask what they would show you after four weeks to prove something had changed. A tutor who answers those three questions concretely has done the work before. A tutor who answers in adjectives has not, however warm the conversation feels.

There are warning signs that are worth more than any credential, and the clearest is a promise about outcome. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest tutor can control what happens in an examination hall, and the ones who say otherwise are usually selling a package rather than teaching a subject. Be equally careful with the tutor who wants a large block of sessions paid up front before you have seen a single lesson, the one who will not put the weekly slot in writing, and the one who says your child's school is teaching the subject wrongly in the first conversation. An IB private tutor in Sion worth hiring will be relaxed about starting small.

The checks you run yourself matter as much as ours, and they take very little time. Watch session one if you can, or at least be in the flat for it. Look at the first piece of work that comes back marked and see whether the comments are specific enough to act on. Ask your child, after the second session, what they were asked to do differently, because a child who cannot answer that has been taught at rather than taught. Parents searching for the best IB tutor in Sion often assume the answer is a credential. It is far more often a match, and you are better placed than we are to see it in the first fortnight.

sections.heading: What do IB tuition fees in Sion depend on?
paragraphs: Fees for home tuition in this part of Mumbai are set by five things, and once you can see all five you can usually tell within one call whether a quote is reasonable. The first is the programme and level: a PYP session and a Higher Level Diploma Programme session are different kinds of work requiring different preparation, and they do not cost the same. The second is subject scarcity. There are many capable Mathematics tutors on the island and very few who can teach Higher Level Chemistry or a specialist Language A at Diploma Programme standard, and scarcity shows up in the rate before anything else does.

The third factor is travel, and this is where Sion families are quietly advantaged. Every home session includes a tutor's unpaid commute, and a tutor who spends ninety minutes in traffic each way prices that in whether the invoice itemises it or not. Because of the SCLR and the Eastern Freeway, a specialist coming from Chembur, Powai or Wadala reaches a Sion address in a fraction of the time the same journey would take into Worli or Colaba. That shows up as a shorter effective session cost and, more importantly, as a tutor who is still fresh at 7pm. Families comparing quotes across the island city should compare travel time, not just the hourly figure.

The fourth factor is session length and frequency, and the arithmetic here is not linear. Two ninety-minute sessions a week is a different engagement from one three-hour marathon, and the ninety-minute pair usually produces more because the week has two contact points instead of one. The fifth is the shape of the commitment: an intensive six-week run before mock examinations is priced differently from a standing weekly arrangement across a full academic year, and a tutor who is confident about the year will often be more flexible about the first month. We do not publish a price list on this site, because a single number for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Sion would be either meaningless or misleading.

The question that actually saves money is not "what is the rate" but "what am I buying per week". Ask whether marking written work between sessions is included or extra. Ask what happens to a session cancelled at short notice by you, and by the tutor. Ask whether the tutor will write two or three lines after each session saying what was covered and what was set, because that single habit is what lets you tell in four weeks whether the arrangement is working. A slightly higher rate with marking, a written note and a protected slot is cheaper than a lower rate that quietly becomes homework supervision by week five.

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks and one term in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at a grade. You should be looking for three things, and all three are visible without a report card. The tutor can name the specific weaknesses they found and say what they have done about each one. Your child can tell you, unprompted, what they are supposed to be doing differently. And at least one piece of returned work shows the change, even if the mark has barely moved. Four weeks is roughly six to eight sessions, which is enough time to fix a method and not enough time to rebuild two years of gaps, and anyone who tells you otherwise is managing your expectations in the wrong direction.

At one term, around twelve weeks, the mark should have started to move, and the movement should be explainable. A student who was losing marks on communication in MYP criterion work should be losing fewer of them for an identifiable reason: they are now showing method, or labelling, or justifying a choice. A Diploma Programme student should have an Internal Assessment that is actually in progress rather than perpetually about to be started. If a term has passed and nobody can point at a specific thing that changed, the arrangement has become a weekly habit rather than a piece of teaching, and that is the moment to have an awkward conversation rather than wait for the next report.

At one examination cycle, the honest claim is narrower than the marketing in this industry suggests. A good tutor raises the floor: fewer careless losses, better exam technique, work submitted on time and in the right form, a student who walks in having practised under timed conditions rather than having read notes. That is a real and often substantial difference. It is not a guarantee, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because the final mark depends on the student in the hall, the paper that comes up and a dozen things nobody controls. Any tutor or platform promising a specific outcome is making a claim they cannot support.

When it is not working, say so early and expect something to happen. Tell us in week two or three rather than month four, because the common failure modes are all fixable at that point: the subject match is slightly off, the level is wrong, the slot is at the end of a day when the child has nothing left, or the personalities simply do not fit. A replacement is normal and carries no penalty, and in our experience it is the parents who wait politely until the end of term who lose the most. There is also a version of this answer that nobody likes: sometimes the problem is not the teaching, and a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai can offer will not fix a sleep problem, an undiagnosed learning difference or a subject the child should not have chosen.

sections.heading: From first message to first lesson: shortlisting an IB home tutor in Tardeo

sections.heading: PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme: where your child actually sits
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three different animals wearing one name, and parents in South Mumbai are often quoted for the wrong one. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years and is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than subject textbooks. A tutor here is not drilling sums. They are building the reading stamina, number sense and written explanation that the Middle Years Programme will assume is already there.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and marks against published criteria, usually labelled A to D, in each subject group. This is where most Tardeo families first ask for help, because the shock is not difficulty but unfamiliarity. A child who has always scored well on content tests suddenly gets a mid-band criterion score for an investigation, and nobody at home can explain why. The answer is almost always that the work answered the question but did not do what the criterion asked.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years: six subjects at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries Internal Assessment (IA) work that is marked by the school and moderated externally. The level decision, HL or SL, is the single biggest lever on a DP student's workload, and it is usually made in a hurry at the end of the previous year.

An IB home tutor in Tardeo should be able to tell you, in plain terms, which of these three your child is in, what the marking actually rewards there, and which part of the current subject guide to read. Confirm structure with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle and the details move.

sections.heading: Which IB subjects do Tardeo families most often ask for help with?
paragraphs: Mathematics, the sciences and the language A courses, in that order. Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and the choice between them at Higher Level is where a lot of Diploma Programme distress begins. A student who picked Analysis and Approaches because a university page mentioned it, and who was comfortable but not quick in the Middle Years Programme, tends to meet trouble at calculus and proof rather than at algebra. A good tutor will say so in the first month rather than the fifth.

In Physics and Chemistry the complaint is almost never the content. It is the Internal Assessment. A student who can recite the theory will still produce an investigation with no real variable control, no honest uncertainty treatment, and a conclusion that restates the introduction. That is a skills gap, and it responds to being taught directly: how to choose a question narrow enough to be answerable, how to record what actually went wrong, how to evaluate rather than describe.

In English A, Language A and the other literature courses, the recurring loss is unsupported assertion. The essay has a view and no textual evidence close enough to defend it. Biology brings a different problem: volume. There is simply a lot to hold, and students who revise by rereading rather than retrieving fall behind quietly.

Across all of it, subject choice and level decisions deserve a conversation of their own. A tutor who covers all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Tardeo might be asked for is usually a coordinator, not a specialist. Requests for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Tardeo parents send in a single message usually resolve into two tutors rather than one. The platform's broadest internal listing reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, which is accurate and useless to a parent who needs Chemistry on Tuesday. For a specific subject, ask for someone who has taught that syllabus to examination, and ask what the last three students they taught found hardest in it.

Physics and Chemistry: Internal Assessment method loses more marks than theory
English: assertion without close textual evidence is the standard leak
Biology: retrieval practice beats rereading for sheer volume

sections.heading: Peddar Road, Mahalaxmi and Cumballa Hill: the radius a Tardeo tutor really works
paragraphs: Tardeo is compact, and so is the area a tutor can realistically serve from it. In practice an IB home tutor in Tardeo also covers Peddar Road, Mahalaxmi and Cumballa Hill, and that is not a marketing radius. It is the set of addresses a person can reach on a Tuesday evening and still get home at a sane hour. Peddar Road is a two-minute hop on the map and a different proposition at half past six, because the whole southbound flow funnels through it.

Mahalaxmi pulls in a slightly different crowd of families, many of them working to the Western Line through Mahalaxmi station and Mumbai Central, and Cumballa Hill sits uphill and quiet with the Jaslok and Breach Candy medical cluster at its edge. A tutor who already teaches two children on Cumballa Hill will take a Tardeo slot happily, because the two addresses are a short walk apart. The same tutor will hesitate at a single lesson in Chembur, and should.

Nearest stations are Mumbai Central and Grant Road, both on the Western Line, which matters for tutors who travel by train rather than car. Metro Line 3 has changed the southern commute, and the Coastal Road has changed the western one. Neither has changed the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, which is where the time still goes.

This is why IB Gram matches within the island for Mumbai home tuition in this part of town rather than importing a tutor from the suburbs. A suburban tutor can be excellent and still cancel twice in October, and two cancellations in an examination term is the point at which parents give up on the whole idea.

sections.heading: One school, two calendars, and why Tardeo is unusual in South Mumbai
paragraphs: Aditya Birla World Academy is in Tardeo, and it runs both the IB Diploma Programme and IGCSE. That makes this locality genuinely unusual in South Mumbai. Elsewhere on the island, a tutor planning a week juggles two schools with two term structures. Here, a tutor can have a Diploma Programme student and an IGCSE student from the same campus, which means one set of holidays, one mock season, one week when every child in the building is suddenly unavailable.

That cuts both ways. The good side is predictability: a tutor who teaches three children from one Tardeo campus knows in September which fortnight in the spring will be impossible, and can front-load content. The hard side is that the pressure arrives for everyone at once. When the school's internal deadlines cluster, a tutor cannot quietly move a Tuesday child to Thursday, because Thursday is also full of students from the same calendar.

Activity High School on Peddar Road adds the other half of the picture. Families here frequently have one child on an IGCSE pathway and a younger sibling still in the middle years, and the household needs two different kinds of help in the same flat on the same evening. Naming either school here is local context only: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Aditya Birla World Academy, Activity High School, or any other school on this page.

Practically, ask a prospective tutor which Tardeo and South Mumbai campuses they already teach into. A tutor who knows that a particular school front-loads its Internal Assessment deadlines will plan a term differently from one working off a generic syllabus timeline.

sections.heading: Should you book home tuition in Tardeo or go online for IB?
paragraphs: Start with home tutoring, because for most families in this part of Mumbai it is simply better. A tutor at your dining table sees the notebook, sees the handwriting, sees the moment the child stops following and starts nodding. Younger children in particular need a person in the room. IB home tuition in Tardeo also removes the negotiation about screens, which in a Middle Years Programme household is worth more than it sounds.

An IB online tutor in Tardeo makes sense in three specific situations. The first is a scarce subject: if your child needs Higher Level Economics or a less common language A course, the right specialist may not live within reach, and a strong online tutor beats a nearby generalist. The second is Internal Assessment supervision, where the work is a document and the useful session is two people looking at the same draft. The third is examination season, when a thirty-minute question clinic twice a week is more use than one long lesson and nobody wants anyone travelling through the peak.

Hybrid is what most Tardeo arrangements settle into by the second term without anyone planning it. The weekly teaching lesson happens at home, and the extra contact before a deadline happens online. Our honest view is that hybrid is the most sustainable shape for home classes in Mumbai, because it survives a tutor's dentist appointment and a school trip without a gap in the teaching.

The real trade-off to weigh is not quality but attention. Online demands more self-regulation than a thirteen-year-old usually has, and less than a seventeen-year-old working on an Extended Essay usually needs. Match the mode to the child, not to the fashion.
bullets: Home tutoring first: the tutor sees what a screen share hides

Short online clinics beat long lessons in the weeks before examinations

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks, and the three things you should check yourself
paragraphs: Before a tutor is introduced to a family, IB Gram verifies identity with government photographic identification, confirms the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and takes up teaching history, including which boards and which programmes the person has actually taught. Claimed examining or moderating experience is treated as a claim until it is evidenced. A tutor who says they have taught the Diploma Programme for several years should be able to name the schools, the subjects and the levels without hesitating.

What we cannot do is sit in the room. So three checks stay with you. First, ask the tutor to teach one topic in the trial lesson rather than talk about their method, and listen for whether they ask your child questions or deliver a monologue. Second, ask what they will do in the first month, specifically, and look for a plan that names topics and a checkpoint rather than promising improvement. Third, be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest tutor can offer one and the offer tells you what kind of operation you are dealing with.

An IB home tutor in Tardeo who is right for your family will also be comfortable being managed. They will send a short note after each lesson saying what was covered and what the child struggled with. They will tell you when the problem is not the subject but sleep, or a clash with a teacher, or a gap three years old. That candour is the thing worth paying for.

IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and will not publish claims about outcomes. What the platform can do is remove the unverified strangers from your shortlist so the conversation you have is a real one.

sections.heading: Why does a short drive in South Mumbai take so long?
paragraphs: Because the island has no alternative routes. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a distance you could cycle, and still loses a large part of an hour at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, because every southbound vehicle is in the same two lanes. There is no bypass to take. That single fact governs how a sensible tutoring arrangement in Tardeo is built, and it is the reason a tutor list that ignores geography is worthless here.

The consequence is counter-intuitive. In the Western Suburbs, a parent can reasonably hire a tutor from two suburbs away, because the Western Express Highway and the Western Line make the trip elastic. In South Mumbai, elasticity disappears after about five in the evening. A tutor who agrees to come from Andheri for a seven o'clock lesson is agreeing to a journey that works in September and breaks in the monsoon, and the arrangement ends not with a conversation but with a run of cancellations.

This is also why fees in this part of Mumbai behave the way they do. IB tuition fees in Tardeo depend on the board and the programme, the level, how scarce the subject specialist is, the length and frequency of the lesson, and travel. A Higher Level science specialist with Internal Assessment experience costs more than a middle-years generalist, and a tutor crossing the city costs more than one walking from Cumballa Hill, because their time in traffic is real time. We will not quote a price list, because a page that does is quoting a number it cannot honour.

The practical rule: shorten the journey and you buy reliability. For a weekly commitment that has to survive a monsoon and an examination season, a well-matched tutor from the island will beat a marginally better tutor from the suburbs almost every time.

sections.heading: Reading progress honestly: the signals that arrive before the grade does
paragraphs: Four weeks in, do not look at marks. Look at behaviour. The child who used to push the homework to Sunday night now starts it on Friday. She can tell you what the question is asking before she starts answering. She corrects herself mid-sentence. Those are the first real signs, and they show up well before any report does. If after four weekly lessons nothing in that list has shifted, something is wrong with the match and it is worth saying so out loud rather than waiting politely.

One term in, you should see the mechanical gains: fewer careless losses, work submitted on time, a draft that responds to feedback instead of being rewritten from scratch. In the Middle Years Programme that often looks like criterion scores moving up a band in one or two strands rather than across the board, which is normal and is progress. In the Diploma Programme it usually looks like an Internal Assessment draft that reaches a sensible shape weeks earlier than last year's did.

One examination cycle in, a grade may move. It may also not move while the underlying position improves, because a student who was carried by memory now understands the material and is being tested on harder content. A tutor who treats the first disappointing mock as a crisis is not helping. A tutor who can show you which specific question types still fail is.

The honest limits matter here. Tutoring cannot fix a subject chosen at the wrong level, cannot replace school teaching, and cannot compensate for a student who will not do the work between lessons. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anyone who tells you a term of home tuition will lift a child two bands is selling something.
bullets: Week four: watch behaviour and self-correction, not marks
One term: fewer careless errors and drafts that respond to feedback

sections.heading: Starting IB home classes in Tardeo, Mumbai: the first fortnight
paragraphs: Have four things ready and the first fortnight goes smoothly. The most recent school report, including the comments rather than only the grades. The child's own notebooks and any marked assessment, because a marked paper tells a tutor more in five minutes than a parent can in an hour. A list of the subjects and levels, written down, because parents often misremember whether a subject is Higher Level or Standard Level. And two usable time windows, honestly assessed against the actual school and activity schedule.

The first lesson is diagnostic and should feel slightly unsatisfying. A good tutor will spend much of it finding the floor rather than teaching the current chapter, because the current chapter is rarely where the problem started. Expect them to go backwards: to last year's topic, to a definition, to a piece of arithmetic. Expect them to ask your child to explain something rather than to listen. At the end, expect a short verdict and a plan for four lessons, not a syllabus for the year.

Within the fortnight you should also have settled the logistics: the regular slot, the room, the visitor and gate-pass arrangement at your building, what happens when a lesson is missed, and how the tutor will report. Get that written down early. Arrangements that fail in Mumbai usually fail on logistics rather than on teaching.
If the match is wrong, say so in the first month. Changing a tutor in week three costs a fortnight. Changing one in March costs a term.
bullets: Bring the latest report with comments, not just the grade summary
Have marked papers and the child's own notebooks on the table
Write down every subject and whether it is Higher or Standard Level
Agree slot, room, gate pass and missed-lesson policy in week one
Raise a poor match inside the first month, not at mock season

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Tardeo actually do in the first month?
faqs.answer: Diagnose, then teach to the gap. The first lesson maps what the child can and cannot do, usually by going back a year rather than forward a chapter, and ends with a short written verdict. Lessons two to four work the two or three weaknesses that cost the most marks, with one checkpoint at the end of the month so you can see whether the plan is working. Content coverage comes after that. A tutor who begins by teaching this week's chapter is teaching the school's timetable, not your child.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Tardeo for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the island geography is why we match locally. Tutors already teaching on Cumballa Hill, Peddar Road or Mahalaxmi can hold a Tardeo evening slot reliably because the journey is short and predictable. A tutor coming from the suburbs through the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at that hour is the arrangement that breaks first. When you book, give two windows rather than one, and tell us whether the lift and gate access slows arrival, so the tutor builds it into their plan.

faqs.question: How does society gate access and visitor entry work for home tuition here?
faqs.answer: Set it up once in the first week and it stops being a problem. Most Tardeo and Cumballa Hill buildings want a resident-authorised visitor entry, and some want the tutor pre-registered for a standing weekly slot. Give the security desk the tutor's name, photograph and the regular day and time, and ask whether a long-term pass is available. Tutors who teach regularly in South Mumbai are used to this. What causes friction is a last-minute substitution nobody told the gate about, so flag any change the day before.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one IB subject for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being sceptical. A single tutor can credibly cover Mathematics and Physics, or two language and humanities subjects, because the thinking overlaps. A tutor who offers Higher Level Chemistry, Mathematics and English to a Diploma Programme student is offering availability rather than depth. For Middle Years Programme students a broader tutor is often genuinely fine, because the work rewards method and structure as much as content. For the Diploma Programme, and especially for Internal Assessment supervision, ask for one specialist per subject even if it means two people in the week.

faqs.question: What do IB home classes in Tardeo cost, and what changes the price?
faqs.answer: We will not publish a rate, because a real quote depends on things only your request reveals. The board and programme matter, the level matters most, subject scarcity matters a great deal, and so do lesson length, frequency and how far the tutor travels. A Higher Level science specialist with Internal Assessment experience sits at the top of the range. A middle-years generalist walking from the next building sits well below it. Ask any tutor to state a rate per lesson, what it includes, and what happens to it during examination season before you commit.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for Internal Assessment and Extended Essay drafting?
faqs.answer: It works well, and often better than a home lesson. Draft work is a document, and the useful session is two people reading the same screen with a tutor asking why a paragraph exists. Younger students lose more online than they gain, because the attention cost is real. For a Diploma Programme student working on an Internal Assessment or the Extended Essay, a short online session two or three days before a school deadline is more valuable than an extra hour at the table a week earlier.

faqs.question: Which months in the Mumbai school year are the real pressure points?
faqs.answer: The two that catch families out are the stretch after the long holidays, when Internal Assessment deadlines and school examinations land close together, and the run into the final examination season when mocks, drafts and revision collide. Because Aditya Birla World Academy runs both the Diploma Programme and IGCSE on one Tardeo campus, those weeks hit a lot of local households simultaneously. Book the tutor before the crush rather than during it. Dates move year to year, so confirm them against your own school's published calendar rather than any general guide.

faqs.question: There has been no visible improvement after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: Have a direct conversation, in that order: with the tutor, then with us. Ask the tutor three questions. What exactly have you worked on? What does my child still get wrong? What will you change next month? A good tutor answers all three in specifics. If the answers are vague, or the diagnosis has not changed since lesson one, the match is wrong and we will arrange a replacement without you restarting the search. A month is long enough to judge the match and short enough that changing costs little.

faqs.question: Do you also cover Peddar Road, Mahalaxmi and Cumballa Hill?
faqs.answer: Yes. Those three are the standard radius for a Tardeo match, along with the Tardeo–Jaslok corridor itself, and tutors frequently teach in two of them in the same week. Beyond that we look at travel honestly rather than claiming coverage. Wider South Mumbai addresses are workable where the timing allows, but a tutor who has to cross the island at the evening peak will eventually cancel, which is worse for your child than a shorter shortlist. Tell us the address when you enquire, not after the introduction.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the lesson?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole lesson, but somebody responsible should be in the flat, particularly for younger students. For Primary Years Programme and early Middle Years Programme children, a parent nearby for the first two or three lessons helps you judge the tutor and helps the child settle. After that, presence is less important than the end-of-lesson note. For senior Diploma Programme students, a parent hovering usually reduces how honestly the student admits confusion. Keep the door open, keep the study space out of the bedroom if you can, and read the tutor's weekly note.

faqs.question: How is IB Gram different from a tuition centre or a WhatsApp group referral?
faqs.answer: IB Gram is an independent platform, not a school and not affiliated with any school named on this page. Tutors are verified on identity, qualification and teaching history before they are introduced, and you speak to them before booking anything. A referral gives you one name and no checks. A centre gives you whoever is free that evening. We do not guarantee grades and will not publish success rates, because neither is honestly knowable. What we offer is a shortlist you can interrogate and a replacement route if the match fails.

faqs.answer: Treat them as search phrases, not as findings. Parents type best IB tutor in Tardeo, or IB tutors near me Tardeo, and get directory pages ranking people nobody at those sites has met. There is no league table of tutors here, and anyone claiming the top position in one is claiming something unverifiable. Judge any IB tutor Mumbai directories list by evidence instead. The useful question is narrower: who has taught this subject at this level to examination, is free at the hour we need, and can reach our building reliably. sections.heading: How IB Gram builds a shortlist for a Thane West home tuition request
paragraphs: A request for IB home tuition in Thane West is read as four separate facts before anybody is contacted: the programme and year group, the subjects and levels, the exact address, and the evenings that are genuinely free. sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate runs three school-age programmes and they are taught in completely different ways, so the answer changes who you should hire. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers roughly Grades 1 to 5 and is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subjects. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs Years 1 to 5, which in Mumbai schools maps to roughly Grades 6 to 10, and introduces the four assessment criteria per subject that parents find most confusing. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years, with six subjects split between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service.

A PYP parent in Thane West usually does not need a subject specialist at all. What helps a Grade 3 child is an hour of reading stamina and number fluency with an adult who does not sigh. Hiring a DP Mathematics graduate for that is a waste of your money and of the child's attention. We say this on the call and it costs us the larger booking, which is the point of saying it.

MYP is where most Thane West enquiries land, and it is where the mismatch between a parent's expectation and the school's report is widest. An MYP report does not say 72 per cent. It gives a level against named criteria such as knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A child can be fluent at algebra and still sit low on communicating because the working is not shown. A tutor who has only taught state-board mathematics will drill more sums and the criterion level will not move. One who has taught MYP will make the child write the method out in sentences, which looks slower and is the actual fix.

DP is the sharpest end. Subject choice at the start of DP1 sets the next two years and is largely irreversible by the time the first school report arrives. HL means more content, more abstraction and in most subjects an extra paper. The internal assessments stack up through DP1 and the first half of DP2, and a child who drifts in DP1 is not recoverable in DP2 by working harder in the evenings. If you are reading this in the DP1 October break, that is the useful month.
bullets: PYP: transdisciplinary units, no subject papers, fluency and reading stamina
MYP: four named criteria per subject, levels not percentages
DP: six subjects across HL and SL, plus TOK and the Extended Essay
HL adds content and abstraction, not simply more homework
Subject and level choice in DP1 is effectively locked by DP2

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the internal assessments each one carries
paragraphs: Every IB subject carries at least one piece of internally assessed work that the school marks and the IB moderates, and this is the part a home tutor changes most. In Mathematics it is the exploration, a piece of independent mathematical writing on a topic the student picks. In the sciences it is a scientific investigation the student designs, runs and writes up. In the languages it is oral and written assessment under controlled conditions. In Economics it is commentary work on real articles. Do not take the structure in this paragraph as current: subject guides are revised on the IB's own cycle, so check the live guide or your school's Diploma coordinator for the components and weightings that apply to the year your child actually sits.

The HL and SL decision is the single most consequential one in the DP and parents are usually given about a week to make it. The honest test is not ambition. It is whether the child can already work independently for ninety minutes on a problem that does not resolve quickly. HL rewards that tolerance and punishes its absence, because HL papers ask for sustained multi-step reasoning rather than recall. A child who is strong but needs a prompt every ten minutes will survive SL comfortably and struggle at HL in a way that no amount of home tuition fixes in DP2.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Thane West is asked about the same four things in the first week: which route in Mathematics, whether to take a science at HL, whether the second language is going to be a problem, and what the internal assessment actually requires. A good tutor answers the fourth question by opening the criteria and showing the child what a top band paragraph looks like against a middle band one. That comparison does more in twenty minutes than a term of content revision, because most internal assessment marks are lost on structure and justification rather than on knowledge.

Enquiries arrive asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Thane West parents would like under one roof, and that is occasionally possible in the lower years. One home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families imagine hiring does not exist at Diploma level, because a Higher Level physicist is not also a language examiner. Below Year 9 a single generalist is often genuinely better than three specialists, because the child gets one working relationship instead of three sets of expectations.

Subject scarcity is worth knowing before you search. In Mumbai, Mathematics and the three main sciences have deep tutor pools at both HL and SL. Visual Arts, Music, Design Technology, Psychology, Business Management at HL, and second languages beyond French, Spanish, Hindi and Marathi are thinner. If you need one of those, start looking a month earlier than feels necessary and be flexible on the day of the week.

Sciences: a designed investigation, written up to published criteria
